````````````````````````````````````````text
> ## 5. Public frame API audit
>
> All findings below concern pinned **CPython v3.14.5**, GIL-enabled execution, valid live inputs and the admitted runtime-hook profile.
>
> | Operation | Declaration / classification | Ownership and behavior |
> |---|---|---|
> | `PyThreadState_Get()` | Public C API | Borrowed attached thread state; invalid attachment is not a recoverable scanner input |
> | `PyThreadState_GetInterpreter(tstate)` | Public C API | Borrowed identity; no allocation or Python dispatch |
> | `PyThread_get_thread_ident()` | Public C API | Native scalar identity; runtime/thread subsystem already initialized |
> | `PyThreadState_GetFrame(tstate)` | `Include/pystate.h`; Stable ABI since 3.10 | New frame reference; may materialize; initial NULL always rejects |
> | `PyFrame_GetBack(frame)` | `Include/cpython/pyframe.h`; public full API, not Limited/Stable | New reference or NULL; may materialize an ancestor |
> | `PyFrame_GetCode(frame)` | `Include/pyframe.h`; Stable ABI since 3.10 | New code reference; no materialization or allocating lookup on valid input |
> | `Py_TYPE` and pointer comparisons | Public C operations | No owning result, coercion, descriptor or rich comparison |
> | `Py_DECREF` | Public reference operation | Safe here only through the specific IR0 non-last proof |
> | `PyErr_Occurred()` | Public C API | Borrowed error observation |
> | `PyErr_GetRaisedException()` | Public; Stable ABI since 3.12 | Transfers error-indicator ownership to the caller |
> | `PyErr_SetRaisedException(exc)` | Public; Stable ABI since 3.12 | Transfers ownership back; safe here only with an empty destination indicator |
>
> The public frame getters do not themselves release the GIL or process signals/pending calls on these admitted paths. `PyFrame_GetCode`’s critical-section macros do not release the GIL in this build configuration. [Pinned declarations](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.5/Include/pyframe.h), [frame implementation](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.5/Objects/frameobject.c), [Stable ABI inventory](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.5/Misc/stable_abi.toml)
>
> Internal implementations were inspected as evidence; no internal frame accessor is proposed for candidate use.
>
> ## 6. Materialization behavior
>
> Initial and ancestor frame acquisition can reach `_PyFrame_MakeAndSetFrameObject` and `_PyFrame_New_NoTrack`. Code retrieval from an existing valid frame does not materialize another frame.
>
> The allocation path:
>
> - Can allocate frame storage.
> - Does not execute Python or run GC under the admitted allocator/runtime profile.
> - Does not unwind frames, release the GIL or process pending calls.
> - Can produce `MemoryError`.
> - Can **schedule later GC** by setting the GC scheduling bit; scheduling is distinct from running collection.
>
> Thus “no GC” must mean no collection execution during the protected interval, not an unchanged GC allocation counter or scheduling bit. [Frame materialization](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.5/Python/frame.c), [GC allocation and scheduling](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.5/Python/gc.c)
>
> This is not valid for arbitrary allocator or reference-tracer hooks. Object allocation dispatches through configured allocator machinery, and new-reference processing includes the reference-tracer path. Those dependencies must remain within the previously required authenticated hook profile. [Allocator dispatch](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.5/Objects/obmalloc.c), [reference initialization](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.5/Objects/object.c)
>
> ## 7. Initial-frame failure
>
> `PyThreadState_GetFrame` clears the error when frame materialization returns NULL. A NULL result can therefore lack an error indicator.
>
> The recovered P1 rule is correct:
>
> - Reject initial NULL.
> - Record **initial ancestry unavailable**.
> - Do not infer empty ancestry.
> - Do not fabricate an OOM diagnosis.
> - Do not enter canonical validation or publish E2/E3.
> - Release any acquired reservation before returning.
>
> A clear error indicator before inspection is essential: otherwise materialization could dispose of a previously saved exception on failure. [Pinned thread-state getter](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.5/Python/pystate.c)
>
> The internal clearing of its newly obtained built-in `MemoryError` is a separately bounded cleanup path, not a general permission to clear arbitrary exceptions.
>
> ## 8. Back-frame failure
>
> After a valid initial frame:
>
> - `PyFrame_GetBack` returning NULL with a clear error indicator means clean ancestry exhaustion.
> - NULL with an error means failed traversal; reject without accepting the scanned prefix.
>
> The pinned implementation can propagate ancestor-materialization failure, despite the documentation’s broader “raises no exceptions” wording. The implementation therefore controls this exact-build failure analysis. [Implementation](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.5/Objects/frameobject.c), [pinned documentation](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.5/Doc/c-api/frame.rst)
>
> On failure, P1 transfers the error out, releases IR0 references and E1, then restores the same error without formatting.
>
> ## 9. IR0 ownership/release
>
> | Reference | Independent owner | Established release rule |
> |---|---|---|
> | Initial frame | Its live interpreter frame owns the materialized frame object | After acquiring the next frame, or during rejection cleanup |
> | Each live ancestor | Its own live interpreter/generator frame | Same traversal discipline |
> | Returned code | Live frame’s executable ownership | Immediately after identity comparison |
> | Inspection exception | Ownership transferred from/to error indicator | No destructive scanner release |
> | Thread/interpreter identities | Runtime-owned, borrowed | No DECREF |
>
> Under retained GIL, no Python execution and no teardown, these live frames cannot unwind during scanning. Their scanner references therefore cannot be last references. Completed frames and suspended generators supplied independently are not valid substitutes for current ancestry.
>
> The unresolved point is narrower than this ownership proof: **when the final current-frame reference is released after clean ancestry exhaustion, relative to semantic validation**.
>
> The source proves that an earlier non-last release can be safe. It cannot prove that earlier release was the historically selected P1 sequence.
>
> ## 10. Error-state interaction
>
> | Case | Preserved treatment |
> |---|---|
> | Error already set | Reject before E1 and inspection; preserve unchanged |
> | Initial materialization fails and clears error | Fixed native rejection; no invented exception |
> | Ancestor materialization fails | Transfer error out, IR0 cleanup, E1 release, transfer back |
> | Valid code getter unexpectedly fails | Reject; never treat failure as completed inspection |
> | Canonical match without error | Native rejection reason; no formatting inside reservation |
> | Cleanup with an inspection error | Transfer ownership rather than destructively clear it |
>
> `PyErr_SetRaisedException` decrements an existing destination exception. Its P1 use therefore requires the destination to remain empty. [Error ownership implementation](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.5/Python/errors.c)
>
> The initial failure’s built-in `MemoryError` comes from the cleared freelist or retained last-resort object. Its disposal is bounded by that exact construction, not merely by its exception class name. [MemoryError implementation](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.5/Objects/exceptions.c)
>

> ## 13. Reservation-purpose analysis
>
> E1 protects the native configuration-writer slot and orders competing finalization attempts. It is already held during P1 scanning.
>
> It does not independently:
>
> - Keep native-cell storage alive—that belongs to live-handle/pin ownership.
> - Prevent Python execution—that requires retained GIL and callback exclusion.
> - Stop runtime signal recording.
>
> Moving the scan before E1 would alter the selected native-writer ordering and would not be a naming correction.
>
> ## 14. GIL-purpose analysis
>
> Retaining the GIL, while executing no Python, prevents another Python thread from beginning canonical mutation and prevents the current Python ancestry from advancing or unwinding.
>
> It supports both live-frame ownership and later canonical-container stability.
>
> It does not exclude unrelated native configuration writers or runtime signal producers. E1 excludes the former; the latter remain allowed to record pending state.
>

> ## 7. Selected T1/T2 decision
>
> **Select OPTION T1 — RELEASE AT SCANNER COMPLETION.**
>
> Freeze this successful sequence:
>
> 1. Inspect and compare the current frame’s code.
> 2. Release the returned code reference immediately after comparison.
> 3. Acquire the back-frame result while retaining the current frame.
> 4. For a valid successor, release the predecessor reference and continue.
> 5. For terminal NULL, establish that the error indicator is clear.
> 6. Release the final current-frame reference exactly once under IR0.
> 7. Establish that all scanner-owned frame/code slots are empty and no inspection error is owned.
> 8. Complete E1-A.
> 9. Enter canonical E1-B under the same E1/P0/GIL.

> ## 8. Selected-option safety proof
>
> At the terminal decrement:
>
> - Clean ancestry exhaustion has already been established.
> - The final frame belongs to current live ancestry.
> - Its executing interpreter/generator frame still independently owns the materialized frame object.
> - No Python execution, GIL release or teardown has occurred.
> - The scanner decrement therefore cannot be last.
> - No frame destruction, locals destruction, weakref/finalizer execution or collection follows from that decrement.
> - A non-last decrement does not change the Python error indicator.
> - E1 and P0 remain held.

> The pinned ownership transfer and clearing paths support that independent ownership; the public getters supply separate owning inspection references. ## D. B2.2 — INDEPENDENT HIGH-RISK FINDING

**Verdict: FAIL — BLOCKING rejected-attempt pin-lifetime incompleteness; also dependent on R1.**

### Finding R2: Precommit rejection does not close the P0 unwind contract

The package explicitly specifies P0 release for:

- Successful root release: after B4 publication and anchor-lease release.
- BF: after borrowed uses end and new P0 entry permanently closes.

See [CP §27](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-csr1-four-target-correction-comprehensive-continuation.md:326) and Appendix R2 §§22–23.

In contrast:

- The pin protocol defines acquisition conditions and CAS-based decrement machinery.
- B2 precommit rejection remains B2.
- Ancestry rejection specifies IR0 cleanup and synchronous **E1** release.
- Canonical rejection specifies ER0 cleanup, error preservation and “precommit release.”
- The generic pin oracle ends with `PIN_RELEASE`.

These do not establish a complete rejection-path mapping for the **P0 already acquired by the rejecting operation**. See [CP §§18–21](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-csr1-four-target-correction-comprehensive-continuation.md:220), [Appendix R2 §§18–20](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-csr1-four-target-correction-comprehensive-continuation.md:1863), and [PRE §40](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-csr1-independent-review-comprehensive-continuation.md:372).

The unresolved cases include:

1. P0 acquired, but E1 acquisition fails.
2. P0/E1 acquired, initial frame unavailable.
3. Ancestry match, depth rejection or ancestor-materialization failure.
4. T1 completed, then canonical semantic rejection.
5. Unexpected canonical helper error.
6. Pre-E3 invalidation while an operation owns P0.

The text does not connect each case to an exactly-once P0 relinquishment, its relationship to remaining borrowed/native uses and error restoration, and the final ownership state before Python resumes.

“B2 remains B2” does not resolve this: **phase and P0 occupancy are separate fields of the control word**. A returned rejected invocation retaining P0 would leave later admission busy without an admitted finalizer or specified cleanup owner. Prematurely releasing P0 while protected uses remain would violate the stated access contract.

This is an architecture omission, **not an observed runtime leak or use-after-free**. A safe unwind is possible, but choosing it is precisely the implementation decision the acceptance standard forbids leaving open.

### Positive B2.2 conclusions

The following are explicitly resolved:

- One canonical initialized-before-publication binding.
- First publication wins; repeated binding rejects rather than retrieves.
- A loser finding a binding allocates nothing.
- Prepublication root cleanup precedes private-handle destruction.
- Postpublication loss of the return value does not undo binding.
- A live handle lease exists before touching pin state.
- P0 is root-capable; P1 is native evidence-only.
- New P0 entry is forbidden after E3.
- Existing finalizer P0 remains counted through successful root release.
- P1 may retain native storage after root release.
- Last-lease destruction requires root NULL and all relevant leases/pins absent.

Publication before acquiring an *operational* P0 is not itself a defect: construction and handle/anchor leases already protect publication. P0 is required before operational root use.

I checked the pinned implementations of the dictionary, integer, function, generator and type-dictionary operations. For example, the generator getter increments the returned code reference, and the type-dictionary getter returns a new reference to the existing dictionary. These support the candidate’s ownership classifications. [CPython generator implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.5/Objects/genobject.c), [type implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.5/Objects/typeobject.c).

The allocation-free claim excludes both Python and native heap allocation on the admitted E1-B path. Cached allocation would still be allocation; stack-local scalars and fixed arrays are different. Callback-capable deallocation is separately excluded by ER0.

However, these are conditional guarantees: a closed operation list cannot establish the missing owner mapping or select the missing rejected-attempt P0 unwind. H1 therefore does not independently rescue R1/R2.

[CPython frame ownership](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.5/Python/frame.c), [public frame getters](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.5/Objects/frameobject.c).

## I. RAW SLOT / ERROR / REFERENCE / CLEANUP ANALYSIS

### Raw-slot validity

The specified validity interval begins only after:

- An independently live handle/cell and root-capable P0 exist.
- S3/profile/type/role and object extent are authenticated.
- The current parent edge owns the containing object.
- GIL and applicable writer exclusion hold.

The load copies `sizeof(PyObject *)` bytes into a local pointer representation. It acquires **no ownership**. NULL rejects; non-NULL must pass its own representation checks before dependent use.

The last permitted use occurs before the relevant owner/protection ends. Successful root release explicitly ends all borrowed descendant uses first. P1 evidence readers receive no permission to dereference historical pointers after B4. See [CP §29](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-csr1-four-target-correction-comprehensive-continuation.md:358).

A copied address is not self-validating. T1 does not replace any of these requirements.

### Reference census

| Reference | Establishment | End/classification |
|---|---|---|
| Metadata/type/module/image references | Bootstrap-owned entries | ER2 process-lifetime retention |
| Extra Registry reference | Binding construction | Successful ER0 release; retained on BF |
| Handle’s native cell lease | Private handle construction | Handle deallocation |
| Association’s handle reference | Publication member assignment | Ordinary graph lifetime after permitted root release |
| Construction lease | Private construction | Publication return or unpublished disposal |
| P0 | Live-handle operational acquisition | Success/BF specified; rejected-attempt mapping incomplete |
| P1 | Acquisition before native reader use | Native release; delays storage destruction |
| Scanner frame/code references | Public getters return new references | IR0 traversal/rejection/T1 cleanup |
| Dict/tuple/Unicode/function/raw-slot results | Borrow from current protected owners | No decrement; dependent use ends before owner/protection |
| Generator-code/type-dict temporaries | Owning getters | ER0 non-last decrement |
| Inspection exception | Transfer from error indicator to local owner | Transfer back into empty indicator after rejection cleanup |
| R0 F/O/adapter/source references | Preserved source-owner contract | LR0 or explicit unresolved retention; representation gap R1 |

**IR0/ER0/ER1/ER2 are reference-release/retention classifications, not four interchangeable exception states.**

- **IR0:** scanner reference is provably non-last under live-ancestry ownership.
- **ER0:** canonical temporary/root decrement is provably non-last under its specified independent owner.
- **ER1:** exact private unpublished handle may undergo its bounded native destruction; its heap-type decrement is separately ER0.
- **ER2:** explicit metadata retention, with no per-cell teardown.

### Error contract and conceptual failures

E1-B entry requires a clear active error indicator. The valid path preserves that state. Unexpected helper error stops validation and preserves the resulting indicator through canonical ER0 cleanup; it is not permission to continue validating with an error.

P1 differs: ancestor failure transfers the inspection exception out, cleans IR0, releases E1 and restores the same exception into an empty destination. The empty-destination condition matters because `PyErr_SetRaisedException` decrements the old destination exception. [CPython error implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.5/Python/errors.c).

| Failure location | Specified result | Remaining issue |
|---|---|---|
| Wrong runtime/profile/live handle | Reject before unsafe dependent access | No arbitrary pointer recovery |
| Existing error before E1 | Preserve; no scan/reservation | If P0 was acquired earlier, R2 requires its mapped unwind |
| Allocation before root acquisition | Dispose private native allocation | No publication/source effect |
| Failure after root acquisition | End borrows; root ER0; private handle ER1; native disposal | R1 affects eventual full source-owner representation |
| Failure after publication | Retain B2; never pretend unbound | Binding alone does not authorize installation |
| Initial frame NULL | Ancestry unavailable; reject even if error was cleared | R2 |
| Ancestor materialization failure | Preserve exception by transfer; IR0 cleanup; no truncated success | R2 |
| Canonical match/depth rejection | IR0 cleanup; no E1-B/E2/E3 | R2 |
| Canonical type/shape/value rejection | Stop before dependent invalid access; canonical ER0 cleanup | R2 |
| Unexpected H1 helper error | Preserve error; no formatting/clearing/replacement; no E2/E3 | R2 |
| Admitted restoration/release-proof failure | BF; root retained; no clean completion | R1 representation; no recovery inferred |
| Corruption/uncertain native execution | SC; only observed evidence survives | No guaranteed cleanup |

No safe cleanup is inferred for arbitrary invalid pointers. No double exception restoration is admitted. The architecture’s exception-transfer sequence is useful, but it does not itself release an operational pin.

The protections have different jobs:

| Registry/metadata ownership | Object and derivative lifetime | Writer exclusion |

Across successful E1-A→T1→E1-B→E2→E3, the text explicitly preserves these protections. T1 has no callback, GIL-drop or writer-reopening step.

Native signal recording remains possible; Python handler execution, signal checks and pending-call processing are forbidden inside the protected operation. Materialization may schedule future GC; scheduling is not collection. [CPython GC scheduling path](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.5/Python/gc.c).

For each main boundary, both questions matter:

- **Could another actor mutate it?** The successful path supplies GIL/E1/profile exclusion.
- **Could it die locally anyway?** IR0/ER0 and independent roots supply the separate non-last/lifetime proof.

R1 leaves part of the second answer incomplete. R2 leaves the protection-ending sequence incomplete on rejection. R3 concerns evidence that the intended contender actually reaches the claimed gate.

## L. ARTIFACT EQUIVALENCE

CP §32 requires equality of safety-relevant behavior, including:

- Ownership and GC representation.
- Binding setter and initialization.
- Pin/control-word/destruction behavior.
- Raw-load body and compiler expansion.
- Helper/error/reference contracts.
- T1 and E2/E3 order.
- Memory ordering and source effects.

Only fixed scalar evidence, native synchronization and parent markers are allowed differences. See [CP §32](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-csr1-four-target-correction-comprehensive-continuation.md:400).

This is a sound architectural equivalence requirement. It correctly rejects “same final value” as sufficient.

No future production/instrumented binary equivalence was verified: those artifacts do not exist yet. Their absence is a legitimate deferred qualification item.

Current obstacles are architectural:

- R1 leaves the representation whose equivalence must be checked unresolved.
- R2 leaves a safety-relevant cleanup path unspecified.
- R3 does not establish that its target-reaching instrumentation belongs to the permitted equivalence class.

A stronger observer root, retained frame, hidden pin or artificial reentry path cannot silently cure these gaps.

## M. E2 / E3 / CRASH / SC ANALYSIS

**E2** is immutable same-attempt observation after successful ancestry, complete IR0 cleanup, canonical validation and required canonical temporary cleanup. It is not source restoration, root release or invocation COMPLETE.

**E3** is separate one-shot finalization admission by the same owner/attempt under continuous protection. It forbids new P0 entry but retains the original finalizer’s P0.

Neither E2 nor E3 permits ordinary Python execution or automatically releases E1/GIL/root ownership. Successful root release occurs later, after restoration terminal publication, R0 discharge and resource terminal publication. See [CP §33](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-csr1-four-target-correction-comprehensive-continuation.md:408).

MX is not an additional production semantic gate that must execute a Python oracle before E2. Its evidence must faithfully correspond to the actual validation and publication.

Crash/SC treatment is appropriately bounded:

| Crash boundary | Permitted conclusion |
|---|---|
| Before/during T1 | Only already observed scan/release events |
| After IR0, before E1-B | No inferred canonical success/E2/E3 |
| During E1-B | No inferred cleanup or validation publication |
| During private binding | No assumed disposal or publication |
| After publication | A witnessed binding is not restoration/admission |
| After E2, before E3 | E2 may exist; admission must not be inferred |
| During closure/root release | Only completed observed transitions; no inferred B4/resource completion |
| After E3 | Existing admitted-failure/SC limits; no retry or recovery authority |

R2 concerns **intact-runtime rejection**, so SC cannot excuse it. Likewise, R1 cannot be deferred by declaring ordinary source ownership a crash concern.

## K. R3-MX — TARGET ACKNOWLEDGEMENT / DISPOSITION / EVIDENCE CLASS

**NEW PROSPECTIVE CORRECTION — freeze the occupied branch.**

Within `P0_TRY_ACQUIRE`:

1. Load the control word with its admitted atomic ordering.
2. Reject an ineligible phase at a distinct phase gate.
3. For eligible B2 with P0 occupied, execute the occupied-P0 rejection branch.
4. Return a unique native gate/result pair:

```text
gate = P0_OCCUPIED
disposition = REJECT_NO_ACQUISITION
```

5. Perform no successful-acquisition CAS, occupancy decrement, E1 operation or root access on this branch.

The gate tag has exactly one producing branch in the audited primitive. The qualification driver cannot inject or substitute it.

The helper evidence sequence is:

```text
FIXTURE_CONTROL_WORD_READY
→ EXACT_PRIMITIVE_CALL
→ RETURNED_GATE_P0_OCCUPIED
→ REJECT_NO_ACQUISITION
→ CONTROL_WORD_UNCHANGED
→ NO_RELEASE_OBLIGATION
```

The driver records the input and resulting word plus returned gate/disposition in preallocated scalar storage. Artifact inspection must establish that the busy branch performs no write; equality of endpoint words alone is insufficient to exclude an intervening illicit mutation.

| Target | Evidence class | Permitted conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| Occupied branch acknowledged; rejection; no mutation/acquisition/release | Helper-scoped direct primitive qualification | Exact occupied-state decision rejects without changing the incumbent word. |
| Earlier production context gate acknowledged | Negative/interface evidence for that gate | That actor/path was excluded there. No occupied-P0 conclusion. |
| Native Python-thread precursor attempts GIL acquisition during protection | Existing exclusion evidence | No Python entry before GIL availability; not a P0 contender. |
| Source/artifact closure excludes same-thread callback or nested native entry | Static admitted-profile proof | No such production route exists within the audited topology. |
| Missing occupied tag, wrong phase, fixture interference or missing attribution | INCONCLUSIVE for occupied-P0 | No branch qualification. |
| Occupied branch grants acquisition, mutates occupancy or releases it | FAIL | Violates the occupied-state contract. |

The failed helper call owns no P0 obligation. The synthetic incumbent bit is never passed to the R2 release path. Disposing of standalone fixture storage is fixture teardown, not `PIN_RELEASE` or a native-cell destruction qualification.

# C. R1 — INDEPENDENT HIGH-RISK FINDING

**Verdict: PASS — the owner/handle representation defect is closed.**

The acceptance is supported by explicit ownership, publication, rollback and responsibility boundaries in CAND §§B–E, read with R0 and CP §§13, 24–27.

## 1. Scope and identity

The S/H split is authorized.

The broader architecture assigns source responsibility to a capability-retained SourceAuthority and distinguishes architectural roles from experimental class names. R0 expressly treats concrete representation as a constrained prospective choice. The correction authorization explicitly permits distinct owner and published-handle entities.

The former B2.1 “SourceAuthority handle” terminology did not independently establish that its non-GC wrapper must directly contain every R0 reference. That unresolved relationship was precisely PR’s R1 finding.

The correction now assigns:

- **S:** the preserved semantic SourceAuthority.
- **H:** the published non-GC representation handle.
- **D:** the separately anchored native cell.
- **C_R0:** S’s embedded R0 storage.

Adding prospective `Assoc._source_owner` does change the eventual schema. It does not change the frozen current implementation or inherit its layout authentication. CAND §E explicitly requires new schema/image authentication. I found no required scope escalation.

## 2. Ownership reconstruction

| Edge/entity | Ownership and visibility | Establishment and termination |
|---|---|---|
| Anchor → D | Native lease outside Python GC | Construction; removed after successful root release, or unpublished rollback |
| D → Registry | One owning Python reference held by the separately anchored native cell | Construction; explicit ER0 root release; retained on BF |
| Registry → Assoc | Existing canonical strong map ownership, GC-visible | Canonical reservation; ordinary graph lifetime |
| Assoc → S | Strong, GC-visible member | Canonical setup once; ordinary disposal only before responsibility or after lawful responsibility-root release |
| Assoc → H | Strong, GC-visible member | Publication store; immutable through the published lifetime |
| S → H | Strong, traversed member | Before publication; unpublished rollback or ordinary post-responsibility clearing |
| H → D | One native lease | H construction through H destruction |
| S → A_src | Strong, traversed reference | Adapter establishment for canonical S; later structural/evidence lifetime |
| S → ledger | Strong, traversed reference to the existing ledger | Preserves canonical source/cut ownership; no copied ledger |
| Configuration | Embedded native record | Scalars and named callable-slot roles; no hidden owning callable cache |
| S’s F/O slots | Two installed and two original owning slots when populated | Explicit retention; same-invocation LR0 discharge or named unresolved retention |
| C_R0 | Embedded storage, not an independently leased object | Cannot outlive S |
| C_R0 reference slots | Individually owned and traversed | Reservation, verification, expected-installed and displaced-reference purposes; exact R0 transfer/release rules |
| D’s S/Association/work identities | Non-owning comparison data | No owner dereference; historical scalars after B4 |
| Metadata | Existing explicit ER2 ownership | Process-lifetime anchor bundle; not per-source retention |

Two Python references to H do not create two native H leases. C_R0 embedding does not hide its Python references.

A_src is the already-required source-lifetime adapter role, not the canonical retaining adapter used for Q. Its access to callable slots is borrowed. The candidate’s graph and prohibition on hidden owners/caches do not permit adding an adapter-owned S or F/O cache.

## 3. Uniqueness, publication and rollback

The one-to-one relationship is selected, not deferred:

```text
Assoc._source_owner = S
Assoc._source_lifetime = H
S.handle = H
H.cell = D
D.bound_source_identity = comparison identity of S
```

Canonical setup creates S once. The binding writer obtains that S from the current Association. Alias factories, shared handles, replacement and retrieval-through-bind are excluded.

The inherited callback-free construction interval and first-publication-wins rule prevent a second publication during private initialization. Pre-native reentry can win first; the outer binding then rejects before allocation. These rules are preserved in [CP §25 and Appendix R2 §§11–16](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-csr1-four-target-correction-comprehensive-continuation.md:306).

Failure accounting is complete for the affected construction edges:

| Failure boundary | Required state/result |
|---|---|
| S allocation or storing S | No source effect, H or R0 callable obligation; ordinary disposal is safe; no replacement of an already established S |
| D allocation, before root | Dispose private native candidate |
| After root acquisition | End borrows; clear/decrement root using independently live Registry argument |
| H allocation or later private initialization | Root disposal; remove unpublished anchor; dispose any acquired H/construction ownership |
| After S → H, before publication | Clear S.handle while constructor independently owns H; then ER1 H release and construction-lease release |
| Publication completed | B2 persists; losing the return value does not undo publication |
| Crash/uncertain execution | SC; no inferred rollback or publication |

Clearing S.handle during rollback cannot be H’s last decrement because the constructor still owns H. Removing the root first cannot destroy Registry because the binding argument independently owns it.

Rollback returns the existing S to its unbound state; it does not create another source owner.

## 4. Published but not installed

This interval is safe within the specified architecture.

H publication establishes a native binding and root, not installed-source status. At this point S may have no adapter or callable slots populated. R0’s L1–L4 sequence establishes S, then A_src, then owned callable references, all before source mutation.

An observer can see the published binding. **P0 acquisition is not categorically forbidden merely because installation has not occurred:** eligible B2 admits a root-capable inspection. P0 does not itself authorize restoration, installation or E3.

The relevant safety boundaries are already present:

- Installation independently checks current binding/profile/source prerequisites.
- Finalization retains its Phase-A and enclosing semantic/handoff prerequisites.
- Current graph access must validate representation before dependent use.
- Binding alone supplies none of those semantic facts.

Consequently, accepting H or acquiring P0 cannot legitimately make empty source slots actionable as installed-source authority.

A failure after publication retains B2 and the same S/H graph. It does not justify rollback, rebinding, BF by inference or source-effect replay. Pre-E3 invalidation preserves ownership while forbidding admission. The future activation implementation remains separately unqualified; this correction does not invent an activation-recovery route.

## 5. GC, mixed cycles and caller loss

The ownership cycle is real:

```text
D → Registry → Assoc → S → H → D
```

Its D → Registry edge is externally rooted, so active/BF responsibility is not an isolated collectible Python cycle.

S traverses its Python fields, including embedded C_R0 references. The native lease from H does not pretend to be a Python ownership edge. On success, explicit D → Registry root removal breaks the retaining cycle before ordinary collection becomes permissible.

The relevant CPython GC mechanism distinguishes external references from references within the collected containers and invokes clearing on the resulting unreachable set. This supports the external-root argument; it does not permit omitting S’s own references from traversal. [CPython 3.14.5 GC implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.5/Python/gc.c)

The safety predicate is supplied by the lifecycle:

- **Before responsibility:** source-instance obligations have not begun.
- **Active/BF:** external rooting retains S; ordinary clearing cannot discharge responsibility.
- **After lawful B4:** restoration/resource prerequisites have completed and required callable obligations have ended before root release.

A second, invented GC “permission bit” is unnecessary. An implementation that clears active/BF S or uses `tp_clear` for restoration would violate the selected contract.

Caller loss cannot remove Anchor → D → Registry → Assoc → S. S also keeps H alive while that relationship is required.

After B4:

- Retained H can keep rootless D alive without keeping S.
- D cannot expose C_R0 or dereference S.
- Its comparison identities remain historical scalar data.
- Metadata remains independently ER2-owned.
- Last-lease destruction remains governed by root NULL, terminal state, absent anchor/H/P0 and zero P1.

A pointer-shaped representation is not permission to dereference the historical identity. The exact representation and all uses must satisfy the candidate’s scalar-only contract and future artifact audit.

S can exist without D before binding or after its H edge is cleared during lawful ordinary teardown. The candidate does not permit active S to lose the H/D lifetime it requires.

## 6. R0 references, LR0 and BF

The named categories match original R0. Separate populated slots denote separate owned references even when they contain the same F or O object.

The decisive accounting rules are:

- Reserved O ownership transfers once to registration.
- Displaced registration ownership transfers once into C_R0.
- Guards and remaining temporaries receive their specified non-last release.
- S’s installation/original slots are separate source-lifetime references.
- Transferred ownership is removed from its old slot and is not decremented again.
- Unused slots remain empty; unresolved references stay in named slots.

I examined CAND §D’s “transfer or release” wording after restoration publication. It does **not** authorize delaying registration replacement’s ownership transfer until then: §D first requires completion of the separately governed transaction, and §C expressly retains R0’s transfer rules. A reservation already transferred by that transaction is no longer C_R0-owned and cannot be transferred again by the later discharge step. No alternative transfer sequence is accepted here.

Successful ordering remains:

```text

# D. R2 — INDEPENDENT HIGH-RISK FINDING

**Verdict: PASS — the rejected-attempt P0 unwind defect is closed.**

The decisive material is CAND §§F–I and the inherited [live-handle/pin model](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-csr1-four-target-correction-comprehensive-continuation.md:316).

## 1. Acquisition, release and interference

Successful acquisition CAS is the only event creating invocation-local P0 ownership. Recording that obligation belongs to the same uninterrupted native execution. No admitted Python exception, callback or signal-processing boundary occurs between those steps. Crash/corruption is separately SC.

An implementation that returns from a successful acquisition without recording ownership would violate the contract; choosing a variable, flag or equivalent compiled representation does not change the selected semantics.

P0 occupancy is separate from phase, E1 and P1 count. Release requires this invocation’s recorded obligation and clears that occupancy through the existing atomic transition while preserving unrelated fields.

Legitimate P1 interference may require retry. A failed CAS is not release. An ownership inconsistency does not authorize clearing occupancy.

There is no legal P0 ABA handoff during those retries:

1. Only this invocation may release its acquired P0.
2. Another acquisition requires P0 absent.
3. P1 changes its own count, not P0 ownership.
4. Another main-thread protected invocation cannot intervene while the current native call retains the admitted execution context.

E1 release may allow a configuration writer to proceed, but it does not transfer P0 or permit that writer to release it. Invalidation does not erase the rejecting invocation’s obligation.

This establishes safety, not a new wait-free progress guarantee. The inherited lock-free design and qualification timeout discipline remain; a timeout is not successful release evidence.

## 2. The H-lease question

**There is no omitted invocation-owned H lease to release.**

CP Appendix R2 §18 selects an independently live H passed through the ordinary Python/C call boundary. H owns one native cell lease for H’s lifetime. CAND §C explicitly preserves that single lease, and §I adds no S/H ownership decrement to rejection.

Thus:

- P0 cannot be acquired before live H exists.
- H’s lease protects D throughout release.
- Dropping rejected-attempt P0 cannot be D’s last lifetime protection.
- Returning from the native invocation does not require releasing an invented extra handle lease.
- Construction ownership exists only on the distinct binding path.

In B2, canonical Assoc/S references also retain published H. Ordinary argument/reference cleanup therefore cannot destroy H on the acquired-P0 rejection paths at issue. A stale live H rejected before acquisition retains the inherited bounded H destructor contract; that is not P0 unwind or source cleanup.

## 3. Rejection coverage

Here **I** means scanner ownership, **C** canonical owning temporaries, and **X** transferred inspection exception.

## 5. Error preservation

The inspection transfer is sound under the selected constraints. The pinned getter removes the exception from the indicator without destroying it. Restoration installs that owned exception and decrements the old destination; the required empty destination avoids a callback-bearing replacement. E1/P0 operations are explicitly prohibited from Python API calls, allocation, decref, callbacks or deallocation. [CPython 3.14.5 exception implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.5/Python/errors.c)

No invocation-owned H decrement remains after restoration. X therefore survives independently after P0 release, and no omitted terminal cleanup clobbers it.

For canonical errors, the active indicator remains in place. The owning getter temporaries have independent owners: the live generator retains its code, and the retained type owns its dictionary. Their matching non-last decrements do not invoke destruction. [Generator getter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.5/Objects/genobject.c), [type-dictionary getter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.5/Objects/typeobject.c)

Ordinary rejection retains a scalar/native disposition. Any Python diagnostic construction occurs after both obligations end and cannot replace an error that must be preserved.

## 6. E2, E3, BF and actors

E2 is immutable and bound to lifetime/attempt/profile/table/Association. R2-K1 terminates that attempt’s admission eligibility; later calls cannot submit old E2 as authority. Capacity constraints prevent overwriting it to disguise reuse.

E3 is the separate one-shot commit. It changes the same invocation’s role to admitted finalizer. It does not run the rejected-attempt epilogue or transfer P0 to another executor. Uncertain E3 execution remains SC.

Success preserves P0 through B4 and anchor drop. BF closes new P0, ends required uses, releases the executor’s pin and retains the responsibility graph. Neither is folded into ordinary rejection.

Actor boundaries remain distinct:

- Native configuration writers may proceed after E1 release.
- Another P0 acquisition requires occupancy release and admitted context.
- Python callbacks/signal processing remain excluded until protected return.
- P1 may overlap but receives only scalar evidence rights.
- Native signal recording may continue without Python handler execution.

**R2 conclusion:** acquisition, every admitted rejection class, terminal ownership, errors and success/BF separation are architecturally complete. No hidden H/evidence cleanup or unresolved release-order choice remains.

Preparation-facts contents need not be reconstructed: successful canonical preparation validated them, and configuration identity remains checked.

### 24. Function/code-image review

The getter-based approach reproduces the current identity comparisons without generator/frame internal reads.

The complete image set includes:

- `_CLASS_IMAGES`, including its enum classes.
- `_FUNCTION_IMAGES`, including property getters.
- The separate canonical action image.
- `_EXECUTOR_CODE`.
- Required C1 module-global bindings and P1 census identities.

A module/class name is insufficient provenance.

`PyGen_GetCode` returns a new reference. Function code/default/keyword-default/closure getters return borrowed values. Absent defaults or closure can legitimately be NULL; that is not the same as a required project slot being NULL.

The getters’ exact-type preconditions must be established before calling them.

### 25. Cut/settlement minimization

The source establishes:

1. `_cut` invokes admission and `_runner`.
2. It captures the current epoch and checks expected identity.
3. It checks adapter pending state.
4. It stores `cut_attempted` and `_cut_epoch`.
5. It arbitrates using `first.setdefault(0, _CUT)`.

Only the winning discriminator establishes K. The first two stores do not.

A receipt winner prevents a cut winner in the same cell. A later admitted settlement is blocked by CLOSED. Replacement epochs arise through `_settle` only after coherent action/accounting checks. Therefore old episode history need not be reconstructed at E2.

Winning cut does not prove normal return, restoration or COMPLETE.

### 26. Retaining-adapter minimization

The predicate survives:

`absent OR no attempt OR dequeued`

with exact role, type, cell representation, authority and fault checks.

- Attempted before receipt completion: pending remains; reject.
- Retained but not dequeued: reject.
- Dequeue interrupted before its first-winner store: reject.
- Dequeue store completed, return interrupted: continuation disposition is already published; other owner/activity gates remain separate.
- Dequeued earlier epoch followed by settlement/cut: valid.
- Foreign adapter or fault: reject.

Requiring `_epoch is final_cut_epoch` would incorrectly reject a qualified history. Its omission is justified.

### 27. Acquisition-bridge minimization

The predicate survives for the assigned terminal observation:

`absent OR (_released is True AND exact _errors dictionary is empty)`

with current composition, type, authority and fault checks.

Earlier `_entered`, `_entry_result`, `_stage`, `_finish_claim`, `_published`, captured epoch and establishment fields are not needed on this terminal path.

This does not authorize reusing the F2 policy for new work after release. Such work remains outside the admitted closed lifetime.

### 28. F2 terminal-evidence proof

The bridge’s `_finish` checks, before setting release:

- Active state and running owner.
- First finish claim.
- Publication and current epoch.
- Exact F2 policy/image.
- Zero depth.
- No delivery or pending representative.
- No F2 failed state.
- Completed protection scopes.
- Every recorded signal restoration marked restored.
- Staged receipt materialization, if needed.

An interruption before release leaves release false. An interruption after release can retain an error; the candidate rejects nonempty errors. If error-detail publication itself is interrupted after release, the preceding required effects have already happened; normal return is not part of this terminal fact.

The authenticated Case-F trace showed unreleased bridge, retained stage and failed/unresolved F2 restoration before ambient cleanup. That supports the distinction; it was not rerun.

### 29. Fault/invalidation equivalence

Registry and association fault cells are separate authorities. Both must be exact and empty.

Required sharing:

`association faults = invocation faults = ledger faults = current faults = binding faults = present composition faults`

The extra binding checks preserve constructor-established sharing. Cut faults need no separate read when cut/current identity is established.

A supported canonical fault cannot be replaced by an empty diagnostic copy. Native validation must not call `_invalidate` or clear a fault.

| Role | Necessary read subset | Review |

| Registry | `_associations`, `_faults` | Sufficient |
| Registry-map association entry | `registry`, `work` | Needed for complete storage validation |
| Selected Association | Seven current role slots, `_faults`, future `_source_lifetime` | Existing checks sufficient; future binding gated |

Omissions of invocation diagnostics, old accounting/history, adapter epoch and earlier bridge/F2 state are justified under the stated terminal and continuity predicates.

All slot values are object references. Boolean roles require exact singleton identity, not a C scalar interpretation.

### 31. K observation boundary

CS-R1 can observe K through:

`live root → current map member → selected association → current ledger → current/cut episode → canonical first cell → _CUT`

Required:

- Current graph and faults valid.
- Current and cut epoch identical.
- Exact first cell with the authenticated winner.
- No receipt won that cell.

`cut_attempted=True` is consistent representation/history evidence, not the winning authority.

### 32. Q observation boundary

CS-R1’s assigned Q portion covers:

- Prior accounting consumed through lawful settlement/cut causality.
- Adapter continuation discharged or absent.
- Bridge/F2 terminal continuation discharged or absent.

It does **not** independently establish other-thread mask discharge, physical source coverage or native configuration ownership. The later seam must combine those external prerequisites.

### 33. U observation boundary

CS-R1 can reject:

- Incomplete current receipt/claim/accounting combinations inconsistent with winning K.
- Unresolved adapter continuation.
- Unreleased/error-bearing bridge.
- Canonical graph/configuration/fault invalidity.

It does not prove that future restoration effects will be certain. Post-E3 physical uncertainty and external native/mask uncertainty have separate authority.

### 34. CS-R1 / R1 responsibility split

| R1 term | Supplier |
|---|---|
| A | Canonical SourceAuthority/native association plus Phase-A identity |
| K | CS-R1 current cut observation |
| Q | CS-R1 participating obligations **plus** external native/thread/source obligations |
| I | P1 live-ingress admission |
| U | CS-R1 canonical uncertainty **plus** applicable external uncertainty |
| C | Source continuous-coverage contract |
| X | Source/native writer admission and exclusion |

CS-R1 is not a substitute for the complete conjunction.

### 35. Callback-free helper whitelist

**The candidate does not yet provide a complete executable whitelist.** The following named subset is auditable; generic categories are not enough to finish the contract.

All permitted entries require the GIL, intact runtime, exact live objects and continuous writer exclusion. None may release the GIL or process signals/pending calls.

| Symbol/operation | Purpose and precondition | Ownership/allocation/error treatment |
|---|---|---|
| `Py_TYPE`/exact type comparison | Already-live object | No new reference/allocation |
| Pointer/singleton comparison | Authenticated references | Native comparison only |
| `PyDict_Size` | Exact dict established first | Scalar; invalid-argument error branch forbidden |
| `PyDict_Next` | Exact stable dict, valid position | Borrowed entries; no hash/equality dispatch |
| `PyTuple_GET_SIZE`, `PyTuple_GET_ITEM` | Exact tuple; bounds checked | Borrowed; no allocation |
| `PyType_GetDict` | Exact retained live type | New reference; release ER0 |
| `PyGen_GetCode` | Exact retained generator | New reference; release ER0 |
| Four selected `PyFunction_Get*` getters | Exact retained function | Borrowed; absent optional fields handled explicitly |
| `PyErr_Occurred` | Current thread state | Borrowed observation; no fetch/normalization |
| `Py_DECREF` for the two getter temporaries | Independent owner established | ER0 only |
| Fixed native evidence writes | Preallocated record | No semantic state mutation |
| Native atomic operations | Exact fields/order must be frozen | No Python interaction |
| Raw slot-load helper | **Not concretely frozen in candidate** | See §36 |
| Integer/string validators | **Exact helpers/error paths not frozen** | Must not coerce or allocate |

For example, exact-string type checking alone does not make UTF-8 conversion allocation-free: `PyUnicode_AsUTF8AndSize` can populate a cache. Exact integer checking must precede any API with a coercion fallback. [Pinned Unicode implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.5/Objects/unicodeobject.c), [pinned integer implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.5/Objects/longobject.c).

Selecting and auditing these remaining helpers is a required correction, not permission to use the examples here.

### 36. Raw slot-load primitive review

A sufficient architecture contract must specify:

- Already-live exact containing object.
- Internal fixed role entry.
- Authenticated object-reference slot, bounds and alignment.
- Overflow-safe address calculation.
- One pointer-representation load into a local value.
- No automatic INCREF.
- NULL rejection before nested use.
- No descriptor or arbitrary address interface.
- Exact compiler aliasing/load assumptions.

An ordinary load is sufficient under genuine writer exclusion; atomics cannot repair a missing lifetime proof.

The candidate’s “fixed-table slot loads” does not select the load/aliasing contract. A fixed-size copy into a pointer local is one possible correction, but adopting that correction here would exceed independent review. This contributes to the new helper-whitelist finding.

### 37. Memory-ordering review

| State/data | Required relationship | Candidate result |
|---|---|---|
| Python slots/containers | GIL plus no legitimate writer | No extra atomic slot access required |
| S3 table | Initializer release; users acquire | Specified |
| E1 reservation | Exclusive admission; acquire on success, release on rejection | Existing P1 input |
| Operation pins | Pin acquisition versus destruction must be one safe protocol | Incomplete |
| Read-closed/root-held | Closure excludes new root users before pointer clearing | Incomplete ordering |
| E2 payload/commit | Payload before release commit; observers acquire | Specified |
| E3 | Same attempt’s one-shot acquire-release transition | Specified |
| Root-released witness | After pointer clear and corresponding decrement | Needs integration with pin/closure protocol |
| Instrumentation | Fixed evidence release/acquire, no ownership | Required, exact mapping pending |

Native preemption does not invalidate Python observations if neither GIL nor exclusion is released.

### 38. Error-state review

The safe required policy is:

- Inspect an existing Python error before semantic reads.
- Reject without fetching, normalizing, formatting or replacing it.
- Retain a separate native rejection reason.
- Release E1 before Python-facing diagnostics.
- Preserve the original error when one already exists.

The candidate mentions error inspection but does not select this policy precisely enough for a complete whitelist.

Wrong exact types and NULL required slots must be handled by native reason codes before calling helpers whose invalid-argument paths construct exceptions.

### 39. Precommit rejection review

The intended rejection contract is sound:

- No source-finalization effect.
- No canonical repair/mutation.
- No E3 consumption.
- Root remains owned through all borrowed uses.
- Temporary getter references released ER0.
- Bounded native reason committed.
- E1 released before Python resumes.
- No invocation FAILED manufactured.

Its implementation-level completeness remains blocked by the cell lifetime and helper issues. A crash or corrupted pointer is SC, never this clean path.

### 40. E2 witness review

E2 may contain:

- Opaque lifetime and attempt identity.
- Role-table/profile identity.
- Canonical association/epoch observation IDs.
- Graph/qualification and assigned K/Q/U outcomes.
- Validation completion sequence and commit marker.

Raw addresses are optional audit data only. They cannot establish identity across allocation reuse or authorize later dereference.

E2 is not accepted from callers and cannot be reused after rejection or for another lifetime.

### 41. E2 reader model

| Reader | Permission |
|---|---|
| Same native executor | Consume same-attempt E2 for immediate E3 |
| Native observer/instrumentation | Acquire-read committed immutable evidence |
| Python diagnostics | Read/project after protected return with GIL |
| Later seam composition | Use the reviewed observation mechanism within the same reserved attempt |
| Unrelated caller | Diagnostics only; no semantic certificate authority |

Reader pins protect record memory, not K/Q/U authority. Their lifetime must be distinguished from root-capable operation pins.

### 42. E2→E3 handoff review

The same-call handoff survives as a logical protocol:

`continuous E1 + completed E2 release publication → same-attempt E3 one-shot commit`

No Python gap, writer release or GIL release is allowed. Native observers may see E2 without E3. A crash between them establishes neither admission nor restoration.

The unresolved cell/pin machinery must enforce this protocol; E2 cannot compensate for it.

### 43. Successful CS-R1 path

The smallest intended path is:

`eligible profile/table + valid published association + live cell/root + E1/P1`

→ current root traversal  
→ graph and qualification checks  
→ assigned K/Q/U observations  
→ cross-field coherence  
→ ER0 temporary cleanup  
→ immutable E2  
→ immediate E3.

Physical restoration is outside CS-R1’s observation operation. Later root release depends on the successful enclosing lifetime contract.

This path is not approved for seam use yet.

### 44. CS-R1 rejection path

`E1 → failed gate/read/check → bounded native reason → safe temporary cleanup → E1 release → Python`

No E2-success witness, E3 or source-finalization effect.

A pre-E1 rejection has no E1-acquired witness and cannot satisfy a test specifically targeting E1 cleanup.

Crash/corruption remains SC.

### 45. Successful later root-release sequence

The candidate needs the following order made explicit:

1. E3 has committed.
2. Restoration and its observation complete.
3. Restoration terminal publication.
4. R0 callable discharge.
5. Resource terminal publication.
6. Permanently close **new root-capable entry**.
7. Establish no other root-capable operation can remain.
8. Finish the final current-edge/ER0 proof using the finalizer’s existing ownership.
9. End all borrowed root uses.
10. Clear the native root slot exactly once.
11. DECREF that former reference exactly once under ER0.
12. Publish root-released state.
13. Permit protected exit.

Read closure cannot prohibit the finalizer from completing its already-owned final proof; it prohibits new users. This distinction and its pin ordering are not fully frozen in the candidate.

A failed release proof after E3 is not a clean precommit rejection.

### 47. Production/instrumented artifact mapping

Evidence transfers only when instrumentation leaves unchanged:

- Root/reference ownership.
- Object and native-cell layouts relevant to the property.
- Table/schema binding.
- Reservation/pin/destruction behavior.
- Callback-free operation set.
- E2/E3 ordering.

Native markers may add preallocated scalar evidence. They may not retain the root, block an otherwise possible schedule or manufacture terminal state.

For R10, a meaningful oracle records the existing owning edges, read closure, pin disposition, root-slot clear and associated decrement without adding an owning reference. Survival by itself is insufficient.

Production must separately execute its own artifact/table admission gates and exposed interfaces. Instrumented layout agreement cannot qualify a different production table.

### 48. Adversarial schedules

The following tables use shared preconditions to avoid hiding assumptions in repeated text.

- **L:** pre-origin bootstrap; no responsibility/source effect. Python may run outside protected validation, but metadata discovery must not dispatch through candidate descriptors.
- **V:** same canonical owner, published candidate cell/root, exact profile/table, E1 reserved, intact runtime, no prohibited live ancestry and no legitimate writer executing.
- **R:** admitted enclosing finalization after resource publication, with continuous exclusion.
- **Clean:** native rejection at the stated gate, E1 released if acquired.
- **U:** unresolved architecture obligation; no approval.
- **SC:** process failure, not clean rejection or success.

For V/R rows, Python execution is forbidden until protected return/rejection. Raw reads are permitted only through authenticated live parents; no read of a rejected child is permitted. Every row requires the specified target and disposition evidence before cleanup.

**D. State model and transition authority**

State is a product, not one health enum:

- Registry: absent or canonical retained capability.
- Invocation: not prepared, PREPARED, ACTIVE, FAILED or COMPLETE. FAILED is native executor closed with no positive COMPLETE. COMPLETE dominates a still-returning post-commit epilogue; runtime frame closure and logical completion are distinct.
- Episode: no intent, retained/unresolved, claimed, accounted, cleanly settled. Repetition is bounded first-intent plus subsumption information; no unbounded signal-count queue.
- Action: unclaimed; claimed/entry unobserved; entry observed; accounted completion; unresolved uncertainty before/after observed entry. Claimed plus escaped executor without completion already implies no-replay uncertainty; a later uncertainty flag is not required to make replay unsafe.
- Source: uninstalled/unqualified, broker-owned pre-cut, cut-authoritative CLOSED. A cut attempt is not CLOSED; the successful arbitration witness is. CLOSED means old-receipt authority ended, not physical handler removal.
- Restoration: original facts retained, not attempted, attempted/unverified, verified per setting; aggregate handoff unavailable or separately qualified. No assumed restoration-resumption transition from FAILED.

| Transition / trigger | Authority and required evidence | Permitted afterward | Prohibited afterward |
|---|---|---|---|
| No owner → canonical record | Legitimate actor registry registration before mutation/work | Prepare, inspect | Work or source installation before ownership |
| PREPARED → ACTIVE | Sole registered non-yielding executor enters | Driver, eligible receipt, diagnostics | Second executor, replacement owner |
| ACTIVE → FAILED | Runtime closes executor without positive COMPLETE; pre-existing basis and obligation references survive | Pre-cut receipt/retention, inspect, ordinary unrelated computation subject to host qualification | New work, delivery/replay, clean settlement, COMPLETE, detachment |
| ACTIVE → COMPLETE | Private positive commit after all prerequisites | Diagnostic reads; lawful ordinary later behavior | FAILED/reopen/work reuse of old capability |
| No intent → retained epoch request | Qualified receipt ordered with settlement/cut | Same-epoch repeat retention; eligible sole dispatch | Generation-based membership; delayed discretionary acceptance |
| Retained → subsumed repeat | Same-work eligible receipt before clean settlement | Retain bounded repeated disposition | New action merely because callback is later |
| Unclaimed → claimed | Sole runner consumes attempt with prerequisites | At most that attempt can enter action | Second claim |
| Claimed → entry observed | Action entry itself, not callback | Account completion if proven | Infer completion from entry |
| Claimed/entered → uncertain | Missing qualified completion on escape or failed recording | Retain receipts and evidence | Replay to obtain certainty |
| Accounted → settled | All §7 obligations, qualified ordering | Fresh receipts under applicable later rules | Stale clearing, premature settlement |
| Pre-cut → CLOSED | Cut wins common arbitration, source coverage contract valid | Qualified restoration/routing only; inspect | Old qualified ingress, FAILED-as-cut inference |
| Restoration → verified | Actual configuration operation plus verification from owned adapter | Only authorized later handoff/completion | Caller assertion as evidence |
| Pre-cut FAILED → restoration resumption | No qualified transition exists yet | Report unavailable | Invent resume, call new close, reset generator |

Required invariants: FAILED never implies CLOSED or healthy reuse; native closure never supplies a source cut; retained intent never supplies action completion; CLOSED rejects old explicit qualified ingress; positive COMPLETE cannot follow FAILED; one claimed action cannot be replayed; restoration uncertainty blocks clean completion; later fresh delivery is not suppressed after genuine completion. These are enforced by private state authority, not by trusting a report object.

**E–F. Source ownership and Gate 13**

The eventual actor retains CapabilityRegistry before interruptible source changes. SourceAuthority captures exact originals and unresolved installation/restoration obligations before mutation. Only SourceLifetimeAdapter may install/remove handlers; it is unavailable for live use in early increments. Module import must be inert. Failure during activation cannot leave an unowned source: activation itself requires the later source-lifetime qualification, not simply an owner constructor test.

Cut authority is the winning discriminator in the ledger arbitration cell, with the corresponding epoch reference retained. A separate `closed=True` write after winning would recreate a visibility gap and is not the architecture. A cut request alone grants nothing. All source routes must consult the authoritative discriminator, not invocation disposition.

Gate-13 path: canonical source callback → pre-cut check → qualified V7-semantic receipt → unresolved epoch 0 selected/subsumed → retained obligation. Invocation FAILED is not part of the receipt rejection predicate. The callback cannot dispatch. The sole dispatcher separately rejects FAILED, and uncertainty separately consumes replay permission. Thus retention cannot reopen work or manufacture COMPLETE.

CLOSED explicit old ingress: canonical source check finds cut witness → reject before old receipt. Actual runtime callbacks after cut must instead use the separately qualified ordinary/coverage route; rejecting an ordinary later cancellation is not acceptable merely because explicit old ingress rejects. In early repository integration no live source factory is exposed, so this missing handoff route cannot be exercised by production callers. Repository tests can qualify bounded isolated routes without claiming whole-host activation.

FAILED before cut leaves SourceAuthority and EpisodeLedger reachable through the capability. The future actor must not detach them or exit under a claimed successful shutdown. Ordinary handoff eventually requires verified actual originals, resolved required obligations and continuous coverage through pending delivery, under the future source-lifetime contract. The experiment's ordinary post-cut forwarding is evidence for its fixed profile, not sufficient production handoff authority.

**G. Uncertain-action contract**

| Action state | Evidence retained by ledger | Later eligible pre-cut receipt | Replay rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unclaimed | Pending epoch, chosen closed profile | Select/subsume same epoch | Only sole eligible first claim can dispatch |
| Claimed, entry unobserved | Attempt consumed; no trustworthy entry evidence | Retain/subsume | No second invocation even if entry may not have happened |
| Entry observed | Claim plus entry witness | Retain/subsume while active/unresolved | No second invocation |
| Accounted intended raise/return | Claim, completion disposition, required evidence | Subsumed until clean settlement; later fresh receipt follows authority | Intended exception is not replay permission |
| Uncertain before/after entry | Claim plus absence of qualified completion; entry fact when available | Retain obligation, remain FAILED if invocation escaped | Never reinvoke to learn outcome |

Existing `GovernedSpawnHandle.wait` is not this action dispatcher and its `_wait_consumed` field is not imported as an action claim. Descriptor F2 delivery is also separate. The new ledger consumes established subordinate evidence but does not replace it. Recording diagnostics may fail; claim consumption and no-completion interpretation must already make retry impossible.

**H. V7 and frozen acquisition boundary**

V7 input responsibilities remain: fixed same-work action profile, admitted source mapping, canonical main runner, existing episode identity, one-attempt acquisition binding and exact continuation provenance. V7 output responsibilities remain: selected/subsumed qualified receipt, retained earlier membership, claim/accounted/uncertain state, clean-settlement ordering and binding/restoration disposition. The invocation owner consumes those facts and adds no second membership ledger or action claimant.

V7 is a protected temporary implementation, not a repository package to import via `/private/tmp`. The new component will translate its semantic operations into module-owned private code with a per-operation equivalence map. It must preserve the closed profile, not introduce a generic callable protocol. Test-only diagnostics move outside semantic decisions. Foreign outcome/observer, vocabulary, nested representative, publication-before-ingress and one-attempt tests are mandatory requalification. No protected V7 source changes are needed or proposed.

Frozen acquisition keeps descriptor scope, result-cell ownership, its own failed/restoration state, continuation and retirement semantics. The bridge may observe depth, pending/binding retention, actual restoration completion and policy failure through the already qualified integration points. It holds exclusion through continuation and never treats a changed representative as new membership. Outer completion is blocked by unresolved acquisition. Outer FAILED cannot cure acquisition failure; acquisition success cannot COMPLETE the outer invocation. No generic F2 wrapper around waits, no status-12 child-cleanup fallback, no policy edits. If faithful integration requires a protected semantic change, the increment stops as architectural conflict.

**I. OWNER-INTEGRATION-FIRST boundary**

Owner/state/receipt implementation may precede production shutdown only as an internal unattached component. Production source activation and actor entry points remain absent, not controlled by a mutable `experimental=True` switch. No public constructor accepts caller-created restoration/native-terminal certificates. Read-only snapshots are expressly non-authoritative.

Hooks reserved for future work are read-only unresolved-obligation inspection and private adapter-owned update points for actual original capture, attempted change and verified change. There is no public `mark_restored`, `handoff`, `resume_failed` or `set_complete`. Until a separately qualified adapter exists, those production transitions remain unavailable. Tests may use isolated fixtures and actual interpreter signals under instrumentation; fixtures are not shipped as production source factories. No false source-handoff or child-terminal evidence is substituted merely to enable COMPLETE.

This permits safe dormant code integration, not operation with permanently broker-controlled failed sources. Live activation is **shutdown-prerequisite**, even though unattached owner integration is owner-first. Gap 4D remains INTENTIONALLY UNQUALIFIED, with production activation blocked by its broader source-lifetime prerequisite.

## 2. Default continuation: checkpoint plus authenticated delta

A continuation task identifies a reviewed comprehensive checkpoint and a bounded, authenticated delta from it. Conversational memory is non-authoritative for project-critical facts. A summary can locate evidence; it cannot authenticate it or grant permission.

Before writes or experiments, authenticate:

- The protocol's exact path, byte identity and adoption/effectiveness record, and the checkpoint's exact identity and review record.
- Repository path, branch/upstream, local HEAD, tracking HEAD, independently queried live-remote branch HEAD, ahead/behind, index, and full mutable path inventory with tracked/untracked classifications.
- Current delta authority and relevant source/test/evidence identities, including their relationship to the checkpoint and any prior failure/review.
- Protected/frozen identities the delta could affect, including indirect dependencies. Establish the preservation baseline required by stronger authority before writes.

Use `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` or `git --no-optional-locks`. Query the live remote without fetching or changing refs; a tracking ref is not an independent remote observation. An unavailable remote is unresolved authentication, not proof of equality. Run `git diff --check`; check new untracked text separately because Git's ordinary diff omits it. Never refresh the index, stage, clean, reset, or touch live operational storage merely to simplify authentication.

Read the complete authority and current evidence materially needed for the task. Do not automatically reauthenticate every historical external artifact on every small increment when the reviewed checkpoint authenticates that history, the task does not depend on reopening it, and no mismatch exists. Record which history was referenced through the checkpoint and which primary artifacts were checked now. Never report an unperformed recheck as performed.

This is a default retrieval optimization, not a waiver of full preservation or a stronger inventory requirement. The current Stage-3C checkpoint's §10 requires its 698-path inventory and specified bindings; that requirement remains. A task expressly requiring all bound external identities still requires them. Changing such a requirement needs its own compatible authority; adopting this generic protocol does not silently supersede it.
````````````````````````````````````````
