````````````````````````````````````````text
## K. REPLAY / VERIFICATION MEMBERSHIP

Replay is correctness-producing for the inspected preparation result:

```text
snapshot
→ independently reconstructed projection
→ validated projection publication
→ replay reconstruction
→ replay/population schema validation
→ profile/artifact validation
→ aggregate validation
```

The [publication/replay path](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/evidence_preparation_worker.py:432) consumes published projections. Replay failure can invalidate an otherwise successful projection.

Thus:

- A domain claiming to own **full preparation success** must include required replay and later validation in its success predicate.
- A narrower execution domain may classify preparation as predecessor work only after identifying that predecessor’s owner and cancellation consequences.
- No evidence establishes replay as harmless post-domain qualification for the preparation result.
- No rule presently determines replay-failure versus canonical cancellation precedence.

The zero-input case has a different evidence-production path, not permission to bypass its required validation.

## L. ACCOUNTING / REAPER MEMBERSHIP

```text
AI     = U
RG     = U
ACK    = U
WA     = U
CO     = U
EOF    = U
FU     = U
REAPER = U
```

| Item | Established fact | Why uniform IN/POST classification fails |
|---|---|---|
| AI | Establishes operation bindings and initial charges | May precede worker launch; domain creation unbound |
| RG | Prepares a prospective growth request from fresh observations | Can authorize later work only after ACK |
| ACK | Commits grant/sequence; matching capacity is single-use | Failure after issuance preserves uncertainty/floor |
| WA | Uses a matching grant and validates actual growth | Includes controller artifact writing, not just primary worker execution |
| CO | Records verified growth | Future requests can remain possible |
| EOF | Affirmative orderly-completion classification plus reconciliation | Physical transport EOF alone is insufficient |
| FU | Retains acknowledged/actual conservative floors and failure | Resource finality does not establish workload finality |
| REAPER | Owns native wait through authoritative terminal disposition | Child exit is not completed reaping; cancellation cannot abandon owner |

The [reservation contract](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/runtime.py:1950) distinguishes bare EOF, orderly reconciliation and uncertain failure. The resource operation may span several controller phases.

The [sole-reaper governance](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/governance/rq003-stage3c-sole-reaper-interruption-admission-clarification-candidate.md:145) requires continuous responsibility after admission. Only the admitted operation may finish its native disposition; supported cancellation cannot unwind it into an ownerless active state.

Attributable reap does not prove worker success. Terminal native failure closes retry authority but does not prove successful reaping or zombie absence.

A broad preparation/result domain cannot declare success while required resource-legitimacy checks may still invalidate it. Conversely, the evidence does not establish an independent post-domain failure result for all late accounting/reaping. **POST is therefore not justified.**

One cancellation domain could prospectively contain several subordinate accounting operations, but no such domain-wide ownership relation is frozen here.

### Mandatory Gate-13 compatibility

A critical distinction is required:

**Immutable workload-result finality is not automatically the end of canonical receipt eligibility.**

Accepted source routes consult the winning cut discriminator, not invocation disposition. A new workload-terminal flag cannot silently replace that discriminator.

Therefore the proposed rule “terminal publication wins, so every later signal belongs elsewhere” requires an explicit compatible owner/routing relationship for the interval before the existing source cut. Merely naming `O_s`, a next domain or a shutdown owner does not establish it.

This does not select a source cut. It identifies the missing composition burden.

| Schedule | Required retained fact | Unresolved domain fact |
|---|---|---|
| DF1 Failure physically known → qualified receipt → proposed terminal publication | Receipt remains retained/consequential | Failure/cancellation result precedence and publication eligibility |
| DF2 Receipt → action/invocation failure → workload failure | Membership survives; no replay or clean settlement from FAILED | Workload-result classification |
| DF3 Proposed domain terminal publication → receipt while source remains pre-cut | Existing eligibility cannot be rejected solely by new domain label | Compatible post-terminal target/owner |
| Success predicate ↔ receipt ↔ publication | Physical completion time cannot determine membership | Exact arbitration and cancellation effect |
| Failure predicate ↔ receipt ↔ publication | Failure cannot erase earlier membership | Finite result precedence |
| Replay failure ↔ cancellation | Required replay failure remains evidence | Same-domain membership and priority |
| Accounting failure ↔ cancellation | Charges/failure duties survive | Domain result precedence and late owner |
| Preparation/readiness failure before allocation | Allocated attempt may never exist | Earlier cancellation subject |

The accepted failed-invocation history remains:

```text
eligible receipt qualifies
→ action/invocation may fail
→ membership and uncertainty remain retained
→ dispatch/replay/clean settlement remain prohibited when FAILED
→ workload classification, if separately authorized, cannot erase that receipt
→ source-specific finalization retains its own prerequisites
```

No failed-source resumption is inferred.

## R. DOMAIN CARDINALITY / SEQUENTIAL-DOMAIN MODEL

**DCARD-U — unresolved.**

Evidence distinguishes three different cardinalities:

- Registry supports different work keys, without defining process-wide workload serialization.
- Official orchestration retains lifecycle ownership per instance; this does not serialize separate instances process-wide.
- Accounting governance permits separate concurrent operation roots. That does not authorize concurrent cancellation domains sharing one untagged process signal.

DCARD-C is **unsupported under the presently unbound process-wide source model**, not physically impossible. No accepted rule attributes one untagged signal to exactly one overlapping domain. Broadcasting it to all domains would require separate authority.

NO-DOMAIN
→ A active
→ A terminal
→ A receipt eligibility ended under a compatible contract
→ NO-DOMAIN or B
```

Its critical transitions are not established.
````````````````````````````````````````

````````````````````````````````````````text
## C. CD-U INHERITED RESULT-BINDING PROBLEM

The inherited problem is exactly:

```text
canonical Association’s same-work cancellation action
→ one specifically named workload-result owner
```

The investigation establishes a sharper distinction inside that edge:

```text
receipt selected
→ action claimed
→ configured action entered
→ configured outcome accounted
```

is implemented locally, whereas:

```text
accounted action
→ workload owner observes a cancellation effect
→ owner applies its legitimate result contract
```

is not established.

An identifier association alone cannot supply the latter effect.

The following remain separate:

| Identity | Authority actually established |
|---|---|
| Registry `work` | Structural selector within one retained Registry |
| Association | Fixed capability/source ownership graph |
| Ledger episode | Selected/subsumed receipts and one action claim |
| InvocationRecord | Cancellation executor disposition |
| Official attempt | Allocated scientific/control-result identity |
| Preparation aggregate | Content identity of authenticated preparation evidence |
| Accounting `operation_id` | Resource coordination |
| Worker / child identity | Local execution, evidence or native disposition |

Neither temporal adjacency nor a common controller can merge these authorities.

## D. ACCEPTED SAME-WORK / RECEIPT / ACTION SEMANTICS

### Same-work classifications

**SW-U — unresolved.**

**SWC-U — unresolved.**

Accepted governance requires admitted sources to mean cancellation of the **same enclosing work**, with no independent per-request side effects. It does not equate that work with an episode, Association, official attempt, preparation assessment or controller request.

Accordingly:

- The beginning of the concrete workload relation is unbound.
- Its result subject is unbound.
- Eligible repeated receipts may subsume within the active episode under the existing same-work premise.
- The end of that workload relation is unbound.
- Episode settlement does not establish workload completion.
- Source CLOSED does not establish workload completion.

The [receipt/settlement supplement](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/governance/rq003-stage3c-sole-reaper-cancellation-receipt-settlement-clarification-candidate.md:120) establishes indivisible receipt/membership ordering, participating retention, no discretionary acceptance delay, and fresh treatment after genuinely clean settlement.

### Canonical action

The exact local chain in [cancellation_capability.py](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:613) is:

| Responsibility | Owner / behavior |
|---|---|
| Receipt qualification | `_Ledger._receive`, through an admitted mapping |
| Membership | Current `_Episode`; first selects, eligible repeats subsume |
| Action claimant | Sole admitted `_Ledger._dispatch`, consuming the episode claim |
| Action executor | Fixed `_closed_action` |
| Configured outcome | Exact `KeyboardInterrupt` or `SystemExit` profile |
| Direct action effects | Record entry and binding; raise the preconstructed outcome |
| Intended-outcome accounting | Dispatcher catches that exact outcome and records accounting |
| Unexpected action failure | Propagates without manufacturing intended-outcome completion |
| Workload notification | No established call, state publication or propagation to a workload-result owner |

**The intended configured exception is caught inside the canonical dispatcher.** It cannot be treated as proof that official execution or preparation was interrupted.

The accepted [closed-action contract](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-u1-u2-rr1-pass-comprehensive-continuation.md:9435) excludes arbitrary caller callbacks, observer closures, subclasses and per-source actions. Attaching a new effect recipient would require explicit architecture classification.

### Effect ceiling

| Proposed effect | Present authority |
|---|---|
| Prevent official launch | No canonical integration established |
| Interrupt official execution | No workload propagation established |
| Stop preparation | No canonical integration established |
| Record cancellation membership/action accounting | Established |
| Invoke arbitrary controller work | Not permitted by the closed action |
| Terminate unrelated workers | No authority |
| Terminate a particular worker | Requires its existing process authority and an explicit propagation contract; not supplied here |
| Directly write official `VALID` / `INVALID` / `FAILED` | No authority |
| Directly write preparation `VALIDATED` / `REJECTED` | No authority |
| Modify accounting legitimacy | No authority |
| Invalidate published immutable evidence | No authority |
| Synthesize child disposition or successful reaping | Prohibited |
| Retry an uncertain action or failed workload | No authority |

One action is not presently authorized to determine multiple independent workload results. A composite result would need its own complete contract.

## E. PREPARATION / OFFICIAL RESULT RELATION

**PH-A — preparation evidence is immutable predecessor evidence consumed through the readiness/launch chain.**

This classification concerns the evidenced predecessor relationship. It does **not** claim that every `EvidencePreparationAssessment` object is directly passed to every `OfficialOrchestrator`, or that preparation snapshots equal launch snapshots.

The governing [readiness specification §9.4](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/specifications/experiment-execution-readiness-v1.1.md:973) expressly separates Phase-3B preparation evidence from later attempt-local launch snapshots.

| Property | Preparation assessment | Official allocated execution |
|---|---|---|
| Identity | Successful evidence has content-derived `evidence_preparation_identity`; no established unique cancellation-request identity. Rejection may have empty identity. | Domain-separated `attempt_identity`, permanent ordinal, allocation receipt and namespace |
| Created when | Assessment returned after outer collection/authentication succeeds or a handled failure is classified | Atomic allocation confirms immutable receipt and consumes ordinal |
| Result owner | `validate_evidence_preparation` for the assessment | Authorized live official execution owner, represented by bound `OfficialOrchestrator` lifecycle and terminal authority; governed failure/recovery authority where applicable |
| Terminal states | `EVIDENCE_PREPARATION_VALIDATED`, `EVIDENCE_PREPARATION_REJECTED` | `VALID`, `INVALID`, `FAILED`; `INCOMPLETE` is derived and nonterminal |
| Reusable? | Immutable evidence graph can be reused under qualifying seals; assessment-call identity is not a single-use allocation token | Attempt identity and namespace are not reusable for retry |
| Depends on other | Required environment, tests, snapshots, projection, replay, profile/artifact validation and aggregate authentication | Current readiness, authenticated launch inputs, smoke, remote revalidation, allocation, primary work and terminal authority |
| Cancellation effect | Unbound | Unbound |
| Association binding today | None established | None established |
| Accounting relation | Applicable preparation resources affect evidence production/legitimacy; operation identity does not own assessment | Required resource facts remain relevant, but no canonical domain-wide accounting conjunction is established |
| Child/reaper relation | Child evidence is subordinate; outer owner can reject it. Required reaping cannot be abandoned. | Worker candidates require authorized validation; native child terminality is not official scientific terminality |

Preparation follows the inspected sequence:

```text
request / authority
→ dependency and test evidence
→ snapshots
→ independently reconstructed projection
→ projection publication
→ replay reconstruction
→ schema/profile/artifact validation
→ aggregate
→ detached transport
→ outer authentication
→ assessment
```

The zero-input profile omits snapshot/projection production and uses governed zero-input replay evidence. It does not eliminate preparation validation altogether.

Official allocation follows later launch checks. The gap includes current-readiness reconstruction, launch-input preparation and authentication, smoke, remote-head revalidation and allocation authority. It is not an instantaneous boundary.

No evidence assigns canonical cancellation ownership to that gap.

## F. RESULT STATE SPACES

### Official state/disposition matrix

The authoritative meanings come from [readiness §§4.3–4.4 and §12](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/specifications/experiment-execution-readiness-v1.1.md:419) and [control_storage.py](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/control_storage.py:31).

| State / disposition | Who establishes it | Preconditions | Immutable terminal? | May cancellation cause it? | Later facts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ALLOCATED` | Shared allocator | Durable immutable receipt | No; allocation fact itself permanent | Not established as cancellation effect | Start or terminal evidence may follow |
| `STARTED` | Official control publisher | Durable write-once start record | No | Not a cancellation result | Does not prove code ran |
| `VALID` | Authorized live owner | Required scientific manifests, reconstruction, validation and unique durable terminal authority | Yes | Cancellation alone cannot establish it | Later cancellation cannot overwrite it |
| `INVALID` | Authorized live owner | Explicit governing scientific/conformance invalidity evidence and terminal authority | Yes | Cancellation alone cannot establish it | Later cancellation cannot overwrite it |
| `FAILED` | Authorized failure publisher; governed recovery where applicable | Snapshot-derived failure facts and durable authorized publication | Yes | Possible for established interruption/failure facts; canonical mapping missing | Cannot replace an existing valid terminal candidate |
| `INCOMPLETE` | Derived from control history | Allocation/start exists without unique valid terminal record | **No** | Interruption may leave this condition | Authorized evidence/recovery may later resolve it |
| `READINESS_REJECTED` | Readiness authority | Pre-seal readiness failure | Pre-attempt disposition | No canonical mapping | Not an allocated attempt failure |
| `LAUNCH_REJECTED` | Launch authority | Launch eligibility/check failure before allocation | Pre-attempt disposition | No canonical mapping | No ordinal consumed |
| `EXECUTION_FAILED` | Governing execution/control classification | Execution interrupted without scientific terminal authority | Not scientific evidence | Possible under actual governed facts | Distinct from `EXECUTION_INVALID` |

No official `CANCELLED` or `INTERRUPTED` control state exists.

The orchestrator’s implementation-progress states are separately:

```text
requested
current_ready
launch_prepared
smoke_passed
second_fetch_passed
allocated
started
primary_frozen
authorized
evaluated
terminalizing
terminal
```

They are not an alternative scientific result space.

### Official failure causes

The closed authoritative classes and normalized facts are:

| `failure_class` | Governed facts |
|---|---|
| `ambiguous_state` | `conflicting_authoritative_control_records`; `indeterminate_authoritative_control_state` |
| `infrastructure_failure` | `shared_control_storage_failure`; `execution_infrastructure_failure` |
| `interruption` | `governed_owner_terminated`; `governed_owner_unavailable` |
| `validity_not_established` | `premature_outcome_access`; `terminal_scientific_authority_not_established` |

Classification uses governed facts and precedence, **not exception type or signal identity**. Cause, boundary and control history are authoritative persisted evidence, not merely diagnostics. An arbitrary new “cancelled” cause cannot be inserted into the closed schema.

### Preparation state/disposition matrix

The exact [assessment contract](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/evidence_preparation.py:114) is:

| State / condition | Owner | Preconditions | Terminal assessment? | Cancellation interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `EVIDENCE_PREPARATION_VALIDATED` | Outer `validate_evidence_preparation` | Collector returns authenticated aggregate | Completed assessment | No canonical cancellation mapping |
| `EVIDENCE_PREPARATION_REJECTED` | Same outer assessor | One of its handled exceptions is classified | Completed assessment | Not synonymous with cancellation |
| `controller_evidence_passed` | Detached producer | Child completes evidence production | **Not** authoritative outer assessment | Transport success only |
| Nonzero controller exit / timeout / malformed output | Transport/collector, then assessor if handled | Observed transport or validation failure | Can become `REJECTED` | Cause may be generic; not proof of canonical cancellation |
| Escaping `KeyboardInterrupt` / `SystemExit` | No assessment terminalizer established by this path | Exception reaches outer call | Assessment can remain absent | No authoritative preparation interruption result |
| Untrusted aggregate | Outer authentication | Identity/origin/shape mismatch | Handled rejection where applicable | Never accepted because child claimed success |

`REJECTED` covers more than evidence-invalidity: it includes resource, timeout, transport and internal failures. But that breadth does not establish a cancellation mapping.

Exact diagnostic codes include:

```text
ARTIFACT_CONTRACT_INVALID
INPUT_MISMATCH
INPUT_MUTATED
INPUT_SCHEMA_MISMATCH
INPUT_UNAVAILABLE
INPUT_UNSAFE_TYPE
OUTCOME_ISOLATION_VIOLATION
POPULATION_MISMATCH
PROFILE_POLICY_MISMATCH
PROJECTION_INVALID
READINESS_TEST_FAILED
REPLAY_IDENTITY_MISMATCH
REPLAY_NONDETERMINISTIC
RESOURCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
TEST_COLLECTION_MISMATCH
WORKER_OUTPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
WORKER_TIMEOUT
EVIDENCE_PREPARATION_INTERNAL_REJECTED
```

There is no preparation cancellation or uncertainty disposition.

### Invocation, accounting and child state spaces

| Subject | Exact state vocabulary / authoritative facts |
|---|---|
| Invocation | `no_owner`, `prepared`, `active`, `failed`, `complete` |
| Executor | `absent`, `created`, `running`, `closed` |
| Intent | `none`, `retained`, `settled` |
| Action | `unclaimed`, `claimed_entry_unobserved`, `entry_observed`, `uncertain_before_observed_entry`, `uncertain_after_observed_entry`, `completion_accounted` |
| Source | `uninstalled`, `pre_cut`, `closed` |
| Restoration / handoff | `unresolved` / `verified`; `unavailable` / `verified` |
| Allocation transaction | `committed`, `rejected_before_consumption`, `ambiguous_ordinal_consumed` |
| Control append | `committed`, `stale_snapshot`, `authority_unavailable`, `ambiguous_completion` |
| Accounting | Snapshot flags `pending_request`, `terminal`, `uncertain`, `eof_pending_classification`; sequence and charged/reserved quantities |
| Child wait result | `GovernedWaitStatus("exited", code)` or `("signaled", signal)` |
| Reaper failure | Retained native failure/mismatch disposition; no fabricated successful reap |
| `InterruptedError` in admitted wait | Nonterminal retry inside that same admitted native operation |

Accounting has no single `SUCCESS/FAILED/CANCELLED` enum. `orderly_eof` establishes final successful reconciliation; bare EOF does not. `fail_uncertain` retains conservative floors and excludes further healthy admission. A terminal protocol rejection is not automatically orderly completion.

## G. RESULT-OWNER ANALYSIS

| Candidate target | Result identity | Result owner | Target owner | Cancellation-effect owner | Terminal publisher | Receipt-target authority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Official execution | Allocated `attempt_identity` | Authorized official live owner / bound orchestrator lifecycle | Unbound | Ledger owns action; workload effect unbound | Official control publisher plus authorized evidence authority; governed failure/recovery path | Ledger membership exists; attempt capture absent |
| Preparation assessment | Successful aggregate identity; request-attempt identity unbound | `validate_evidence_preparation` | Unbound | Ledger owns action; assessment effect unbound | Outer assessor returns disposition; immutable graph publication is separate | Preparation target capture absent |
| Composite | None established | None spanning both results | Unbound | Unbound | None established | Absent |
| Worker result | Worker/component identity | Worker producer, subject to parent validation | No canonical binding | Existing process owner only within its contract | Worker transport / parent acceptance | Absent |
| Accounting result | `operation_id` | Reservation/descriptor-accounting authority | No workload binding | No canonical mapping | Accounting transition owner | Absent |

The official owner is a **semantically plausible result owner**, with a real terminal contract. The preparation assessor is likewise a **plausible owner of its own assessment**. Neither is selected as canonical cancellation recipient.

For official execution, the chain is:

```text
primary worker candidate
→ bound TerminalEvidenceAuthority reconstruction
→ owner validates context and evidence
→ atomic control publication
→ OrchestrationResult
```

The governing contract additionally requires matching final execution-control/scientific evidence. The inspected port-driven orchestrator is not proof of completed production storage integration.

For preparation:

```text
detached child evidence
→ transport parser
→ aggregate identity/origin authentication
→ sole outer assessor
→ caller
```

A child’s stdout does not own `EVIDENCE_PREPARATION_VALIDATED`.

The sole reaper owns native disposition, not either business result. Required unresolved reaping cannot be ignored to claim successful cleanup or a result whose contract includes that cleanup. Attributable reaping is still not worker success.

## H. CANCELLATION-MAPPING ANALYSIS

**Final canonical mapping classifications:**

| Candidate | Classification | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Official result | **MAP-U** | Existing interruption representation is available, but canonical action does not establish its requisite owner/failure facts |
| Preparation assessment | **MAP-U** | Handled failure can yield rejection; canonical cancellation-to-assessment effect and cause remain unbound |
| Composite | **MAP-U** | No composite result contract or mapping |
| Cancellation representation overall | **CR-U** | No authoritative workload mapping selected |

### Official alternatives

| Mapping | Finding |
|---|---|
| Cancellation → `INVALID` | Rejected without independent governing invalidity evidence |
| Cancellation → `FAILED` with cause | Conditionally representable using existing governed facts; not derivable from receipt/action or exception alone |
| Cancellation → no scientific result, controller failure/interruption | Supported as a general control distinction; exact canonical integration absent |
| Cancellation → new `CANCELLED` | Requires a new result distinction; not necessary merely because interruption exists, and not selected |
| Cancellation → absent terminal record | Possible observed outcome; means `INCOMPLETE`, not completed cancellation |

OA1, preventing primary launch after allocation, could be represented only through an explicit owner rule. OA2, interrupting active work, needs actual propagation. OA3, terminal failure, needs authoritative failure facts/publication. OA4 has no existing state. None follows automatically from the current action.

The orchestrator catches `Exception` after allocation and can raise `OrchestrationIncomplete` with recovery progress. That is not automatic terminal `FAILED`. `KeyboardInterrupt` and `SystemExit` are not caught by that `Exception` handler; moreover, the canonical dispatcher already catches its intended outcome internally.

### Preparation alternatives

| Mapping | Finding |
|---|---|
| Cancellation → `REJECTED` | Not established |
| Cancellation → transport/controller failure | Possible if an actual such failure occurs; still requires attribution |
| Cancellation → prospective `INTERRUPTED/CANCELLED` | New distinction; not selected |
| Cancellation → absent assessment | Possible when an unhandled interruption escapes; no accepted terminal-absence owner |
| Cancellation → child termination only | Insufficient to define parent assessment |

PB1–PB5 therefore remain conditional or incomplete. In particular, an interruption-induced nonzero child exit could produce generic rejection, but that does not preserve an authoritative cancellation cause.

### Result absence

Official allocation may remain with no scientific result and derived `INCOMPLETE`. Governed failure/recovery authority may later publish `FAILED`; absence alone is nonterminal.

Preparation can fail to return an assessment. No accepted owner turns that absence into a durable preparation cancellation result.

Action execution alone therefore cannot establish terminal workload cancellation. The legitimate result owner must establish the actual effect and its authorized disposition; that handshake is missing.

## I. PREPARATION REUSE / RETRY

**PR-N — preparation evidence may be reused.**

This finding applies to the immutable evidence graph, not to an invented reusable cancellation-request object.

The [detached-publication decision](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/governance/execution-readiness-v1.1-detached-evidence-publication.md:432) explicitly permits later qualifying seals to reuse the same graph and original publication. Its namespace is immutable and compare-only; identical qualifying publication is an idempotent no-op.

There is no one-attempt consumption token in the aggregate identity. Official allocation binds readiness/launch authority and fresh validated input facts, rather than consuming the outer assessment object.

Consequences:

- PR-1 is not supported.
- A graph may remain valid historical evidence when a downstream attempt fails.
- Reuse does not bypass current-readiness or launch-time validation.
- Reuse of predecessor evidence does not authorize reuse/import of failed attempt scientific artifacts.
- Later loss of current eligibility does not rewrite the historical assessment or graph.

**PRT-U — preparation retry identity semantics remain unresolved.**

A new function call can perform a fresh assessment, and identical content can reproduce the same aggregate identity. That does not define whether two calls are one request, two requests, or a retry of one cancellation domain.

A rejected assessment may have no aggregate identity. Consequently, content identity alone cannot identify every active or interrupted preparation attempt.

## J. OFFICIAL ATTEMPT BINDING / RETRY

**OR-A — no retry under the same identity; retry requires a new ordinal and attempt identity.**

The [allocation contract](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/specifications/experiment-execution-readiness-v1.1.md:1054) makes consumed ordinals permanent. Ambiguous allocation cannot be treated as unused. Recovery does not resume the scientific attempt.

| Attempt field | Preparation relationship | Immutable? | Full preparation-result binding? |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `external_input_snapshot_identities` | Validated **launch** snapshots compared with readiness expectations | Yes | No; input facts |
| `readiness_identity` | Binds readiness evidence, including preparation graph through its governed chain | Yes | Indirect evidence binding, not ownership of assessment request |
| `readiness_seal_commit` | Binds qualifying seal | Yes | No cancellation/result-owner transfer |
| `launch_authority_snapshot_identity` | Fresh launch authority | Yes | No |
| `source_commit` | Source identity used in governed evidence | Yes | No |
| `remote_head_commit` | Launch-time authority | Yes | No |
| Allocation authority / allocator contract | Shared allocation semantics | Yes | No |
| Kind / experiment / ordinal / namespace / output revision | Attempt identity and permanent output allocation | Yes | No |
| Preparation request ID / cancellation state | No such direct attempt field established | — | Absent |

The exact builder is [build_allocation_bundle](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/attempts.py:166).

Before allocation, this official attempt does not exist. Cancellation during preparation cannot retroactively target it. Pre-allocation failure is a readiness/launch disposition and consumes no ordinal.

**OTA-U — official cancellation-target admission unresolved.** Allocation, STARTED and primary entry are distinct events; none is accepted as target admission merely because it exists.

The inspected `OfficialOrchestrator` instance also rejects a second lifecycle. Abstract reuse of a result-owner role must not be confused with reuse of this concrete object or an attempt identity.

## K. ASSOCIATION / LEDGER TARGET-BINDING ANALYSIS

The [Association](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:386) fixes Registry, work selector, invocation, ledger, executor and entry/preparation references. Reservation permanently retains the first owner. The Registry explicitly is **not new-work admission authority**.

Accepted source architecture additionally fixes:

```text
Association → canonical S
Association → canonical H
S.handle = H
H.cell = D
D’s bound-source identity = S, for comparison only
```

No second S, shared H, alias factory or rebinding is admitted.

| Candidate binding | Semantic assessment |
|---|---|
| Association → allocated official attempt | Not present. Constructor binding requires the attempt to exist first; otherwise explicit late admission is needed. Actual order unbound. |
| Association → preparation request | Not present. Aggregate identity is produced too late to identify all active/rejected requests. |
| Association → composite transaction | No existing identity/owner |
| Association fixed to S, subordinate target changes | Conceivable, but a new mutable authority; not bookkeeping or existing Registry behavior |
| Ledger episode → workload identity | Episode currently records membership/action state, not an authoritative workload-result binding |

A correct future binding must be immutable for each qualified receipt. Preparation receipts cannot become official receipts; old attempt receipts cannot become new-attempt receipts; action failure cannot erase or replace the original target.

Ledger membership must semantically retain the target relationship, whether directly or through an immutable retained binding. No field layout is selected.

The result owner cannot acquire S restoration, E3 or reference-release authority. S cannot declare preparation validity, official terminality or accounting legitimacy to enable its own finalization.

## L. ACTIVE-TARGET OWNERSHIP / STATE MODEL

**ATG-C — an active workload-target authority would require explicit new owner/state as an architecture correction.**

This classifies the proposed mechanism’s novelty. It does not adopt that mechanism or establish its compatibility.

No existing actor is authorized to admit, publish, close, retire and transition such a target:

- Registry reserves fixed structural ownership.
- Association retains the canonical graph.
- Ledger owns receipt/action membership.
- Result owners own their respective dispositions.
- None presently owns cross-result target admission.

A fixed single-result architecture could avoid a changing active-target slot, but would still need an immutable result binding and complete before/after ownership. Neither AR-A nor AR-B currently supplies that contract.

The proposed state list is not yet a sufficient selected model:

| Proposed state | Distinction it expresses | Remaining issue |
|---|---|---|
| `TGT-NONE` | No admitted workload target | Who owns eligible ingress? |
| `TGT-ACTIVE` | Eligible for new target receipts | Result transition and closure ordering |
| `TGT-RESULT-TERMINAL` | Result immutable | Does new attribution remain open? |
| `TGT-RETIRED-BUT-REFERENCED` | No new attribution; old references remain | Retention/settlement authority |
| `TGT-RETIRED` | No new attribution and no required retained references | Destruction/reuse permission still requires authority |

If target closure can precede result terminality, an additional closed-but-result-pending condition is needed. The supplied list alone does not represent that schedule.

A useful analytical separation is:

- Result terminality.
- New-receipt eligibility.
- Existing-receipt retention.
- Destruction/reuse eligibility.

No finite operational state machine is selected while their ordering remains unresolved.

## M. RESULT TERMINALITY / TARGET CLOSURE

**RTR-U — result-terminal/target-close relationship unresolved.**

**WTC-C — introducing TARGET-CLOSED requires an explicit architecture correction**, including its owner and composition with existing ingress. No completed closure contract is adopted.

Official terminality requires the governing evidence and durable terminal authority. Preparation assessment completes after outer authentication/classification. Neither event presently publishes target closure.

| Proposed ordering | Required explanation | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| Result and target closure coincide | One authoritative ordering against receipt qualification | Absent |
| Result precedes closure | Meaningful effect/owner for later receipts that cannot alter result | Absent |
| Closure precedes result | Retained pre-close cancellation and later result arbitration | Absent |
| Another conjunction | Exact owners and prerequisites | Absent |

TARGET-CLOSED cannot silently become SOURCE-CLOSED. A source receipt after target closure still needs a legitimate owner, or an explicitly compatible rule preventing canonical qualification while preserving required event handling.

Publication failure cannot be repaired by inferring closure from a terminal result. Conversely, uncertainty about target closure does not authorize rewriting an independently immutable result.

For either candidate, remaining work after valid result terminality may include retained receipt settlement or independently owned cleanup **only if that work cannot still change the claimed result under its own contract**. Accounting, reaping or publication required for that result must already be resolved before asserting terminality.

## N. RECEIPT TARGET / GATE-13 ANALYSIS

The [accepted Gate-13 path](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-u1-u2-rr1-pass-comprehensive-continuation.md:9507) retains eligible pre-cut receipts even when the invocation is FAILED. FAILED separately excludes dispatch, replay, clean settlement, COMPLETE and healthy reuse.

For a future target binding:

```text
qualified receipt → immutable target
action/invocation FAILED
→ same retained receipt and target
→ no replay
→ result remains under its independent owner
```

The last target edge is a mandatory requirement, not implemented evidence.

A result may be independently established while receipt/source obligations remain. Nothing in the inspected result APIs makes ledger settlement their terminal authority. However, this does not complete canonical target-retirement or late-attribution semantics.

The converse is also possible at the component level: clean episode settlement creates a successor episode while the retained capability remains. This demonstrates that episode settlement is not inherently result terminality. A universal episodes-per-workload rule is still unbound.

| Race | Established requirement | Unresolved contract |
|---|---|---|
| RT-R1 — before target admission | Future target cannot retroactively own receipt | Pre-target owner |
| RT-R2 — simultaneous admission | Exactly one ordering and recipient | Admission linearization |
| RT-R3 — active target | Preserve qualified membership | Concrete result target/effect |
| RT-R4 — simultaneous result publication | Scientific/evidence truth and receipt ownership remain distinct | Cancellation/result precedence |
| RT-R5 — terminal result before closure | No retroactive result change | Meaning of new old-target receipt |
| RT-R6 — simultaneous target closure | Pre-close retains old target; post-close cannot acquire it | Closure discriminator/owner |
| RT-R7 — closure with old receipt unsettled | Old receipt remains retained; cannot migrate | Later ingress owner |
| RT-R8 — next-target admission | No dual attribution or ownerless qualification | Transition authority |
| RT-R9 — next target active | Old receipt remains old; new receipt uses admitted current target | No accepted transition exists |
| RT-R10 — action failure | Gate-13 retention; no replay or target reset | Workload consequence remains owner-specific |

A late receipt after immutable `VALID`, `INVALID`, `FAILED`, or a completed preparation assessment cannot rewrite that fact. Retaining its cancellation obligation is meaningful under source/ledger authority; assigning it a **new effect on that closed result** is not established.

For official and preparation result races alike, qualification time cannot simply be declared to override result publication. A real target/result arbitration contract is required.

An immutable subordinate preparation result does not logically forbid a composite result. It does require the composite to be a separately identified result with its own owner. No such owner was found, and creating one merely to avoid transition arbitration is unjustified.

AR-X has **no complete smaller alternative**:

- Invocation COMPLETE would be circular if used to authorize its own source prerequisites.

## X. QUALIFICATION / ARTIFACT EQUIVALENCE / AUTHORITY CLASSIFICATION

No qualification was performed.

| Future target | Required oracle |
|---|---|
| Result subject | Actual workload identity matches selected contract |
| Result owner | Actual authorized owner establishes disposition |
| Cancellation mapping | Actual action effect produces the required fact/cause without corrupting result meaning |
| Target admission | Exact admission precedes target eligibility |
| Receipt capture | One immutable recipient survives interrupted return and action failure |
| Result terminality | All required evidence exists; later cancellation cannot rewrite it |
| Target closure | Actual ordering separates pre/post-close attribution |
| Transition | Old obligations remain retained; no double or missing recipient |
| Preparation handoff | Immutable predecessor evidence; fresh launch validation preserved |
| Retry/reuse | New official identity; graph reuse distinct from request retry |
| Owner/publication loss | No inferred success, closure, transfer or successor |

**PASS = actual target + attribution + required disposition + artifact equivalence.**
````````````````````````````````````````

````````````````````````````````````````text
## D. ACCEPTED CLOSED-ACTION / DISPATCHER SEMANTICS

The strongest recovered architecture is the [accepted closed-profile interface contract](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-u1-u2-rr1-pass-comprehensive-continuation.md:9435), subordinate to adopted receipt/reaper governance. The current [implementation](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:548) establishes:

| Step | Exact semantics |
|---|---|
| Configuration | `_prepare` selects exact `_ActionProfile.KEYBOARD_INTERRUPT` or `.SYSTEM_EXIT`; binds the module-owned action and exact exception class. |
| Allowed types | Exact `KeyboardInterrupt` or `SystemExit`. No subclasses, caller callables, observer closures or per-source actions. |
| Receipt | `_receive` validates canonical source/configuration and open ingress. `first.setdefault` selects the first receipt; eligible repeats mark subsumption. |
| Admission | `_dispatch` requires admitted canonical runner context, prepared/open ledger, running retained executor, healthy graph and matching episode. Acquisition responsibility must be released. |
| Claim | `epoch.claim.setdefault` consumes the single claim before possible action entry. Existing claim rejects replay. |
| Exception creation | **After claim**, `binding.outcome()` constructs the exact exception instance; `epoch._outcome` retains it. Preparation retains its class/profile, not this later instance. |
| Invocation | Dispatcher invokes the authenticated `_closed_action(epoch, outcome)`. |
| Action body | Validates canonical caller, association, claim and outcome identity; writes `entered` and `_entry_binding`; raises that exact instance. |
| Intended catch | Dispatcher catches `BaseException`, but recognizes success only when `error is outcome` and all binding, entry, type and integrity checks pass. |
| Accounting | Writes `_accounted_binding`, then `accounted = True`. |
| Outward return | Successful dispatch returns `None`. The intended exception is consumed. |
| Unexpected exception | Re-raised; no intended-outcome accounting is manufactured. An unexpected normal action return is rejected. |
| Invocation terminality | `_Invocation` has one positive `_complete` commit. Native executor closure without it derives FAILED; optional caught detail is not success authority. |
| Repeat | No second action claim for that episode; no replay after uncertain entry/completion. Fresh post-settlement receipt is a separate governed case, not replay. |

An exception constructor failure or interruption after claim but before entry also consumes the attempt. Absence of observed entry does not establish permission to try again.

**Dispatcher boundary:** the ordinary successful caller observes return from dispatch, and an authorized diagnostic reader can inspect local state. The configured exception does not escape to official or preparation workload code. Unexpected propagated failures cannot be relabeled successful canonical cancellation.

**Caller census:** repository production code contains the dispatcher definition and its internal action invocation, but no production workload call site invoking `_dispatch`. The accepted architecture assigns that role to a future sole canonical runner. Current prerequisite producers explicitly remain unavailable; fixtures do not establish production activation. The retaining adapter and acquisition bridge provide ingress/continuation, not workload dispatch.

The outer `_Registry._enter` drives the retained invocation generator. It does not turn a caught action outcome into a workload exception. Current `_invoke` is a closed internal lifecycle driver, not a wrapper around arbitrary workload code.

**DCG-U:** the semantic change needed for a complete future effect remains unresolved. This decision leaves the dispatcher unchanged. Letting its intended exception escape would change its accepted boundary; it is not an observation of current behavior.

The process-supervision path in [git_state.py](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/git_state.py:170) includes a real selector loop and optional periodic guard. Its production callers use that guard for resource enforcement, not canonical cancellation. Finding a callback-shaped internal parameter does not authorize a generic cancellation callback system.

The collector event paths are real polling/checkpoint mechanisms in [RFC-008 collection](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/rfc008/collector.py:84). Their existence does not grant their owners authority over official execution, detached preparation, or canonical receipt membership.

## G. EFFECT-RECIPIENT / OWNER ANALYSIS

“Unbound” means an incomplete semantic contract, not permission to fill the cell with an implementation choice.

| Recipient | Existing interface | Prospective bounded interface | Pre-start | Active | Terminal/stale | Ack capability | Process |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Official owner | Explicit lifecycle/ports; no cancellation interface | Plausible observation point; complete scope unproved | Existing allocation/start authority; cancellation denial unbound | Worker ports expose no stop request | Immutable control result protected; stale-effect interface absent | Governed result/failure evidence, not canonical effect ack | Controller plus implementation-specific workers |
| Preparation owner | Sole outer assessor; no cancellation interface | Plausible owner request interface; completion unproved | Can own invocation decision; cancellation disposition unbound | Detached controller/workers lack canonical channel | Published evidence/returned assessment cannot be rewritten | Generic assessment; cancellation attribution absent | Outer process, detached controller, child workers |
| Child/spawn owner | Authenticated gate/process control within profile | Canonical request admission would be new | Existing gate control | Existing bounded termination prerequisites | Must authenticate disposition and avoid stale PID authority | Request/system evidence and independent reaping | Cross-process |
| Admission authority | Official allocator/start gates; bounded bootstrap gate | Cancellation-aware decision not established | Local gate authority exists | Admission alone cannot stop admitted work | Existing closed/consumed identity rules | No canonical denial acknowledgement | Profile-dependent |
| Result publisher | Atomic official publication / outer preparation return | Effect-cause linkage would be new | Cannot invent missing attempt/result | Cannot replace application with writing a result | Existing immutable result stays fixed | Only its own authoritative result facts | Profile-dependent |
| Controller shutdown owner | Source quiescence and F2 retirement are distinct | No universal workload shutdown interface | No general cancellation admission authority | Retirement is not child cleanup | Source-finalization prerequisites remain | No workload ack | Controller-local; child effects separate |
| Sole reaper | Exclusive final native operation | No new cancellation-to-kill permission | Outstanding obligation must remain executable | Supported cancellation must not unwind admitted wait | Retains disposition; admission permanently closed | Native disposition only | Parent observes governed child |
| Collection owner | `request_stop`/Event and loop checks | No transfer to canonical profile established | Local loop can avoid starting iterations | Cooperative stop at existing checks | Collector-specific completion | No canonical receipt/ack linkage | Own collector process |
| Ledger/dispatcher | Receipt and action interface | Workload-effect authority absent | Cannot borrow admission authority | Cannot borrow worker-control authority | Cannot rewrite workload results | Acknowledges only local action evidence | Canonical component process |

The actor applying an effect **need not conceptually be the result owner**. For example, a legitimate child controller could apply an authorized interruption and a separate result publisher could authenticate its consequence. That separation is compatible with the existing authority boundaries.

What is missing is the accepted delegation/binding between these roles. A common controller process or shared identifier is not sufficient.

## H. OFFICIAL OWNER EFFECT INTERFACE

**OO-U — unresolved.**

The [official orchestrator](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/orchestrator.py:849) provides finite lifecycle boundaries, but none currently consults canonical cancellation state.

| Lifecycle point | Existing observation/authority | Canonical state visible? | Cancellation consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pre-allocation | Readiness, launch preparation/authentication, smoke, remote revalidation | No | No cancellation admission/result rule |
| Allocation completion | Immutable allocation bundle and attempt identity | No | Ordinal cannot be silently returned or reused |
| STARTED publication | Atomic control append | No | STARTED does not prove primary work ran |
| Before primary work | Issued capability and profile checks | No | No cancellation check or governed denial transition |
| Active work | Synchronous ranking/characterization/evaluation ports | No | Ports provide no canonical interrupt interface |
| Child supervision | Depends on concrete worker implementation | No canonical binding | Existing process authority cannot be borrowed |
| Terminal reconstruction | Bound terminal-evidence authority/context | No | Worker output remains subject to independent reconstruction |
| Terminal publication | Unique nonterminal snapshot and atomic append | No | Cannot overwrite immutable terminal result |
| Failure/recovery | `OrchestrationIncomplete` and separately governed recovery facts | No | No automatic terminal FAILED from cancellation accounting |

The post-allocation handler catches `Exception`, not `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit`. More fundamentally, the canonical intended exception is already caught inside its dispatcher.

The smallest **plausible** extension would allow this owner to observe a receipt-linked obligation at an existing lifecycle boundary and apply an independently authorized transition. That observation alone does not complete active interruption, pre-allocation disposition or terminal arbitration. Therefore OO-P is not established for the full requested profile.

Official-side acknowledgement candidates:

| Candidate | Finding |
|---|---|
| Admission denied | Requires a cancellation-aware admission decision and attributable outcome; absence of work is insufficient. |
| Termination request accepted | Could prove a request step under exact child authority; not target stopped. |
| Owner enters cancelling/interruption state | No such canonical lifecycle state/transition is established. |
| Governed FAILED record | Potential downstream evidence, subject to actual failure facts and attribution. |

**OFP-A — suitable downstream acknowledgement, conditionally.** A valid governed FAILED record with an applicable interruption cause can establish its own result-level fact. It cannot establish canonical delivery by itself.

The existing interruption causes are `governed_owner_terminated` and `governed_owner_unavailable`; they cannot be asserted merely because a child stop was requested or an action accounted. [Failure classification](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/control_storage.py:640) must remain evidence-based.

A prospective effect acknowledgement could precede terminal result publication if it acknowledges only a committed owner transition. No current canonical transition or acknowledgement publisher establishes that sequence.

**PRA-B — unsuitable as a standalone canonical cancellation acknowledgement.** `EVIDENCE_PREPARATION_REJECTED` is broad, and the closed diagnostic vocabulary contains no canonical cancellation cause. Generic nonzero exit or internal rejection does not prove canonical application.

Before launch, cancellation-specific refusal has no established preparation result meaning. During work, existing supervision may clean up its own processes under its existing conditions; that does not authorize canonical process termination or establish which already-published evidence remains usable.

After evidence publication, cancellation cannot invalidate immutable evidence merely by arriving. After assessment completion, no retroactive assessment rewrite is permitted. Before completion, cancellation/assessment arbitration remains unbound.

## J. RETAINED-INTENT ANALYSIS

**RI-RU — receipt/intent relationship unresolved.**

Receipt membership already retains **cancellation-side intent**. It does not currently authorize a workload owner to treat that membership as a command.

This distinction matters because:

- `_episode_view` exposes `IntentState.RETAINED` diagnostically.
- Accepted read-only snapshots cannot authorize transitions.
- Eligible pre-cut receipts remain retainable after InvocationRecord FAILED.
- The dispatcher separately rejects FAILED execution.
- Settlement can replace the current episode after its existing prerequisites; there is no workload acknowledgement retention rule.

Promoting membership into workload-actionable intent therefore adds responsibility; it is not merely renaming existing bookkeeping.

| Creation candidate | Assessment |
|---|---|
| RI-C1 Qualified receipt | Avoids a later publication gap, but makes intent precede action claim and survive failed invocation. Its authority to cause workload application is unestablished. |
| RI-C2 Action claim | Binds one attempt, but claim does not prove action entry/accounting or delivery. Failure can occur immediately afterward. |
| RI-C3 Accounted outcome | Preserves a success-first ordering, but adds a failure window between accounting and intent publication. No replay can repair that gap. |
| RI-C4 Another point | No exact alternative established. |

**RI-CU.**

**AI-EU — action-accounting/effect relation unresolved.** Neither independent receipt consumption nor action-accounting-gated workload action is already accepted. They cannot both become independent cancellation effects.

**RI-AUTH-C:** treating current receipt membership as an authoritative workload command would be an **architecture correction** to its current role. Whether a particular correction fits stronger governance or requires amendment depends on its application/failure rules. No completed extension is selected.

A future retained obligation would need, at minimum, immutable linkage to the existing Association/episode and action claim, plus a legitimate owner/target context. A new global request ID is not established as necessary.

The current evidence does not assign workload-intent creation, retention, publication, application and acknowledgement to exact owners. The ledger remains the receipt/action authority; the workload owner cannot inherit source authority through observation.

**NEUTRAL-U — unresolved.** A common vocabulary for intent is possible in principle, but “apply its own already-authorized semantics” is incomplete when neither primary owner has a complete canonical application interface.

## K. OBSERVATION / APPLICATION MODEL

**OP-U.** No finite canonical workload observation obligation is established.

Existing finite points—official pre-primary entry, preparation worker launch, supervision iterations, terminal publication—are possible locations, not accepted cancellation checkpoints.

The following distinctions are required for any future contract:

| Fact | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Delivery | Legitimate owner obtains authoritative access to the exact obligation. |
| Observation | Owner actually reads/accepts that obligation under its interface. |
| Application | Owner commits the specified cancellation-relevant transition. |
| Acknowledgement | An authorized actor publishes evidence of that application or another exact disposition. |

A returned diagnostic snapshot is not automatically delivery. Successful intent publication is not automatically observation. A request accepted by a child controller is not automatically work stopped.

Conceptual ordering burdens remain:

| Race | Required prospective property | Current status |
|---|---|---|
| Intent publication / admission | One ordering; cancellation-first follows denial rule, admission-first follows active rule | No common arbitration authority |
| Publication / active progress | Identify committed work and next cancellable transition; no invented rollback | No progress prohibition or safe-point obligation |
| Publication / terminalization | Identify the owner’s authoritative terminal predicate and effect ordering | Unbound |
| Observation / owner loss | Retain distinguishable delivery/application evidence | No canonical retention/ack contract |

Indefinitely missing an intent would violate a contract that promised bounded observation. No current owner has that promise. It would be incorrect to label existing workload progress a canonical cancellation violation before defining the obligation.

Same-process storage would still need owner, lifetime, ordering and reentrancy rules. Cross-process visibility would additionally require receiver identity and loss/duplicate semantics. Neither is supplied by a shared boolean or serialized worker request.

## L. ACKNOWLEDGEMENT MODEL

**ECOMP-U — effect completion unresolved.**

There is no accepted workload acknowledgement state machine. The following is an **analytical minimum vocabulary for evaluating candidates**, not a frozen API or selected effect contract:

| State/fact | Minimum meaning | Evidence ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| NONE | No delivery/application established | Does not prove absence unless independently observed |
| DELIVERED | Legitimate recipient obtained authoritative access | Intermediate fact; not application |
| APPLIED | Specified owner transition committed | Does not mean target stopped unless that is the specified transition |
| STALE | Exact target was already immutable before application; no mutation performed | Does not mean cancellation succeeded |
| FAILED | Exact application/delivery operation definitively failed at its specified boundary | Does not erase the receipt or imply no partial effect |
| UNCERTAIN | Required observation cannot distinguish material outcomes | Not a successful acknowledgement |

“ACKNOWLEDGED” need not be a separate state: publication of an attributable disposition is the acknowledgement event.

Minimum prospective acknowledgement content would bind the receipt/episode, legitimate owner context and target where required, exact effect meaning, disposition, and supporting application/terminal evidence. No serialization format is selected.

Only the effect owner, result owner with sufficient evidence, or an accepted delegate could publish it. The dispatcher cannot acknowledge workload application merely because it delivered a request.

Monotonicity constraints for any such contract:

- APPLIED cannot later become STALE for the same operation.
- STALE cannot later authorize application against the old immutable target.
- FAILED cannot silently become APPLIED.
- UNCERTAIN can be clarified only through authorized independent evidence, not destructive replay.
- An acknowledgement publication failure does not reverse a known application.
- Conflicting acknowledgements require conflict handling; no last-writer-wins rule is justified.

**WA-AUTH-C:** adding a required workload acknowledgement is an architecture correction. Making it a new clean-settlement prerequisite would also change settlement integration. No authority for that completed dependency is established here.

## M. PRE-START / ACTIVE / TERMINAL EFFECT MODEL

The phases cannot currently be closed with one selected effect.

| Phase | Delivery | Application | Ack | Failure behavior |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PRE-START | No canonical admission interface | Cancellation-aware denial unbound | Absence of launch insufficient | Cannot invent failure/rejection or consume an absent attempt |
| ACTIVE | No canonical owner channel | Cooperative stop/child request not bound | Request acceptance differs from stopping | No blind retry; existing cleanup duties remain |
| TERMINALIZING | No shared effect/result arbitration | Cannot infer whether result predicate or application won | Requires owner-authoritative ordering | Preserve independent result evidence and uncertainty |
| TERMINAL | No stale-effect interface | Immutable result cannot be rewritten | STALE would require proof by legitimate owner | Receipt cannot be dropped; no rerouting/replay authority |

Candidate applicability:

| Candidate | PRE-START | ACTIVE | TERMINALIZING | TERMINAL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Retained intent | Could reach admission owner | Requires observation/application profile | Requires arbitration | Requires stale handling |
| Prevent-start | Applicable only before admission | Insufficient by itself | Generally too late to supply active cancellation | No retroactive denial |
| Active interruption | Requires separate pre-start rule | Requires accepted interruption owner/mechanism | Requires terminal race rule | Cannot interrupt immutable result |
| Child termination | Requires exact child and authority; child may not exist | Profile-specific | Termination and result publication remain distinct | No stale PID/result mutation |
| Two-stage intent + ack | Could describe all phases abstractly | Owner rules still required | Requires exact acknowledgement/result order | Requires authoritative stale disposition |

No STALE acknowledgement is adopted. **Non-mutation of an already immutable result is preserved authority; a new stale acknowledgement protocol is prospective.**

If cancellation wins before admission, a complete future rule must make denial monotonic for that target. If admission wins, the obligation must move into the active-phase rule without another action claim. Existing evidence does not establish either transition.

## N. CHILD / PROCESS EFFECT ANALYSIS

**CT-U — canonical child-termination applicability unresolved.**

The [bounded process contract](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/governance/rq003-experiment-005-bounded-streaming-source-processing-prerequisite-v1.md:1722) requires authenticated process-instance/group membership immediately before signaling. PID alone is insufficient. On controller termination, active worker termination precedes independently authenticated controller-group termination.

The [existing helper](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/runtime.py:449) performs a group-signaling operation after checks. Its existence does not establish canonical cancellation admission, an idempotent retry protocol or result ownership.

The distinct chain is:

| Step | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Owner receives authorized request | Delivery |
| Owner invokes permitted termination operation | Application attempt |
| System call succeeds | Request/system-call evidence; not terminal disposition |
| Sole reaper retains attributable exited/signaled status | Native disposition evidence |
| Workload result owner authenticates consequence | Separate result-level evidence |

`GovernedSpawnHandle` provides `wait()`, not a cancellation method. Its preserved `_wait_consumed` implementation is the known failed correction candidate; stronger sole-reaper governance remains controlling. It must not be presented as a newly qualified cancellation interface.

The [sole-reaper contract](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/governance/rq003-stage3c-sole-reaper-interruption-admission-clarification-candidate.md:301) requires:

```text
native terminal disposition retained
→ required restoration/teardown
→ pending interruption delivery or explicit failed completion
→ final public return/raise
```

It also requires that admitted waiting finish without relying on deferred cancellation to perform the work necessary for the wait to finish. Therefore:

**A post-reaper canonical action cannot be used to justify terminating the same still-active child so that the prerequisite wait can finish.** That would create a dependency cycle and borrow termination authority.

Reusable semantic pattern: responsibility precedes work; supported interruption cannot erase it; terminal evidence survives caller loss; no second native operation follows uncertainty. Reaper-specific authority is not transplanted.

Existing `_run_bounded_process` cleanup and RFC-008 child cleanup are separate local mechanisms. Their repeated-call checks/escalation behavior do not establish canonical at-least-once termination semantics.

**XP-U — unresolved.** The preparation topology crosses processes, but an effect owner might reside in the parent and use an already-authorized child-control path. Thus a new IPC protocol is neither established nor proved unavoidable. A neutral complete contract cannot assume away process loss or descendant control.

## O. SETTLEMENT / SOURCE COMPATIBILITY

**ES-U — prospective workload-effect settlement relationship unresolved.**

Current accepted settlement is exact. The [receipt/settlement supplement §7](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/governance/rq003-stage3c-sole-reaper-cancellation-receipt-settlement-clarification-candidate.md) requires native terminal disposition, required restoration/teardown, accounted selected action, retained delivered/subsumed membership, and no unresolved required delivery/invocation/restoration represented as success.

Its intended-exception “delivery” rule concerns the adopted action-delivery contract. It does not prove the additional workload-side delivery defined in this task.

Current `_settle` checks coherent action accounting and prerequisite facts. It does not read a workload acknowledgement. This observation cannot silently:

- Add workload acknowledgement to settlement.
- Declare a new workload obligation independent of settlement.
- Treat unresolved new delivery as already covered by local accounting.

Those are architecture choices; changing stronger “required delivery” meaning may require a governance amendment rather than only component correction.

**SF-U — prospective source-finalization dependency unresolved.**

Accepted source prerequisites remain binding. No new workload-ack prerequisite is currently represented, but no selected effect contract establishes that an unresolved workload obligation may outlive finalization independently. Source timing is not selected.

Failure distinctions:

| Condition | Established implication |
|---|---|
| InvocationRecord FAILED | No positive invocation completion; existing failed-state exclusions and receipt retention apply |
| Action accounting failed/uncertain | No coherent intended-action completion established; no replay |
| Delivery failed | Would concern owner access; not represented by current invocation state |
| Application failed | Would concern owner transition; action accounting cannot decide it |
| Ack uncertain | Application may be known or unknown independently |
| Target stale | Immutable result remains fixed; receipt/source duties are not automatically settled |

Workload results can currently become terminal without canonical acknowledgement because no such interface is integrated. A prospective effect must handle that possibility without circularly requiring cancellation to establish a result that already terminalized.

Gate-13 remains exact: eligible pre-cut receipt survives FAILED; retention does not authorize dispatch, reuse, successor ownership, clean settlement or restoration resumption. A future workload consumer may not use retained membership as a backdoor replay authority.

## T. DELIVERY / APPLICATION / ACK FAILURE MATRICES

These matrices state **claim ceilings and required constraints**, not an adopted effect implementation.

For every row:

- Qualified receipt membership is not erased.
- No second canonical action claim is authorized.
- No successor effect owner is created.
- Process death supplies no Python retention guarantee.
- “Observation” means an already-authorized evidence read, not a new recovery or reapplication operation.
- New workload-effect settlement eligibility remains ES-U; existing failed/uncertain invocation cannot be represented as clean settlement.

**Effect-owner loss**

| Case | Effect / ack state | Workload claim ceiling | Receipt/episode consequence | Permitted next operation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EO-F1 Lost before delivery | Delivery absent or unknown; no ack | No cancellation application proved | Existing receipt remains consequential | Observe existing evidence only |
| EO-F2 Delivered, lost before application | Delivery known; application absent/unknown | Cannot claim stopped/prevented | No inferred settlement | Observe; no successor application |
| EO-F3 Application possible, ack absent | Application uncertain | Cannot claim success or absence | Retain uncertainty where authority survives | Independent observation; no destructive replay |
| EO-F4 Ack published, owner lost | Exact authenticated ack survives only within its retention contract | Claim only ack’s stated fact | Ack does not automatically settle receipt | Read retained ack/result evidence |
| EO-F5 Terminal target, lost before stale ack | Terminal evidence may exist; stale ack absent | Result remains immutable | Receipt not discarded | Authorized terminal evidence observation |
| EO-F6 Lost during termination | Request/system effect may be uncertain; child disposition separate | No terminal-child claim from request | Reaper duty not erased | Existing admitted reaper only, if still authorized/executable |

**Effect-publication failure**

| Case | Evidence / claim ceiling | Required handling |
|---|---|---|
| EP-F1 Rejected before effect exists | Known failed publication; no delivery | No invented intent or application; preserve action/receipt facts |
| EP-F2 Ambiguous publication | Intent visibility uncertain | No automatic republication/destructive replay |
| EP-F3 Owner observed; publisher cannot prove | Owner evidence may establish delivery; sender uncertainty remains | No inference from expected behavior; inspect authoritative owner evidence if permitted |
| EP-F4 Duplicate attempted | No canonical duplicate contract | Reject/retain conflict; cannot claim safe idempotence |
| EP-F5 Result terminalizes during ambiguity | Terminal result remains independent | Do not rewrite result; application/stale ordering requires evidence |
| EP-F6 Finalization attempted while unresolved | New effect dependency unbound | No new source-cut permission or fabricated clean completion |

**Acknowledgement failure**

| Case | Application fact | Ack fact | Claim / next-operation ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|
| AK-F1 Definitely absent | No application | No success ack | Do not equate action accounting with application |
| AK-F2 Definitely succeeded, ack write fails | Application known | Publication failed | Application is not undone; only authorized evidence-based ack completion could be considered, never reapplication |
| AK-F3 Outcome uncertain | Unknown | No successful ack | Independent observation only; no replay |
| AK-F4 Stale target, stale ack fails | No mutation; terminal evidence may be known | Stale publication absent | Preserve result; do not infer completed acknowledgement |
| AK-F5 Conflicting ack | Evidence conflict | No unique accepted ack | No last-writer-wins; retain conflict |
| AK-F6 Ack owner disappears | Depends on retained application evidence | Absent or independently retained | No invented delegate; existing observation only |

**Result-terminal / effect races**

| Case | Required claim ceiling |
|---|---|
| RE-F1 Intent wins before terminal predicate | Only a defined owner/progress rule could make later progress forbidden; current contract supplies none |
| RE-F2 Terminal predicate wins before observation | Preserve immutable result; prospective STALE needs authoritative proof |
| RE-F3 Simultaneous | Requires one owner-authoritative ordering; wall-clock proximity is insufficient |
| RE-F4 Result published while application uncertain | Neither fact repairs the other; retain uncertainty and immutable result |
| RE-F5 Effect applied, result owner lost | Effect evidence cannot mint result-owner authority; final result may remain absent/incomplete |
| RE-F6 Stale ack after immutable result | Could confirm no mutation for that target; cannot mean cancellation succeeded or reopen result |

**Settlement / effect races**

| Case | Existing authority / unresolved addition |
|---|---|
| SE-F1 Settlement before delivery | Current settlement checks adopted action/source obligations; no permission to declare a newly required workload delivery resolved |
| SE-F2 Delivery before settlement | Delivery alone does not prove application or existing settlement prerequisites |
| SE-F3 Application uncertain | Cannot claim successful effect; whether additional episode blocking is required remains ES-U |
| SE-F4 Target stale | Result unchanged; stale fact does not itself satisfy action/restoration/receipt duties |
| SE-F5 Invocation FAILED, effect may have happened | Preserve both facts independently; no action replay, clean reuse or fabricated effect ack |
| SE-F6 Source cut requested with effect unresolved | No cut selected; a future contract must establish whether obligation remains source-related or lawfully independent |

Definitive application failure does not establish whether the workload continues, fails or remains without a result. That depends on the effect owner’s actual authorized transition. Another owner cannot “try instead” without authority.

Known delivery with unknown application is different from action-invocation uncertainty. Known application with lost ack is different again. None is repaired by rerunning `_closed_action`.
````````````````````````````````````````

````````````````````````````````````````text
The inherited edge is:

existing qualified, retained receipt membership

## D. ACCEPTED RECEIPT / MEMBERSHIP / ACTION SEMANTICS

The controlling sources are the [receipt/settlement supplement](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/governance/rq003-stage3c-sole-reaper-cancellation-receipt-settlement-clarification-candidate.md:120), the [sole-reaper delivery contract](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/governance/rq003-stage3c-sole-reaper-interruption-admission-clarification-candidate.md:301), and the [accepted owner-integration architecture](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-u1-u2-rr1-pass-comprehensive-continuation.md:9405).

| Fact | Exact accepted/current meaning |
|---|---|
| Episode existence | Ledger construction creates an initial empty episode. An episode object alone proves no receipt. |
| Qualified receipt | Source-specific legitimate ingress retains the request and membership as one operation ordered against settlement. |
| First receipt | Selects the current episode’s configured action; return to the caller is not the retention point. |
| Same-work | Admitted sources must cancel the same enclosing work and require no independent per-request effect. Concrete workload attachment remains unresolved. |
| Repeated receipt | Eligible repeats belong to the active episode and subsume; no additional action claim. |
| Participating retention | Earlier authorized adapter retention participates in receipt. Later dequeue is continuation, never fresh membership. |
| Action claim | Sole admitted dispatcher consumes one attempt before possible action entry. |
| Closed action | Validates its canonical context, records entry/binding and raises the exact configured outcome. |
| Accounting | Dispatcher recognizes that exact outcome and coherently records local completion. |
| FAILED | Native executor closes without the sole positive COMPLETE commit; optional diagnostic detail is not failure authority. |
| COMPLETE | Positive private commit after its required source, restoration, receipt and composition prerequisites. |
| Settlement | Sole runner; all adopted prerequisites, coherent action accounting, no unresolved required delivery or uncertainty; ordered against receipt. |
| Successor | Settlement replaces `current` with ordinal `n+1`; subsequent first qualified receipt is fresh. |
| Source cut | Winning common discriminator, not an attempted cut or FAILED status. Receipt-winning current membership prevents a cut win in that cell. |
| FAILED retention | Eligible pre-cut receipts remain retainable; FAILED separately excludes dispatch, settlement, COMPLETE and healthy reuse. |
| Views | Diagnostic descriptions; not transition capabilities. |

The [current ledger](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:690) reflects these distinctions. Its production prerequisite producer remains unavailable. Source reading here does not establish production activation or new qualification.

| M1 Source event/request admitted | **PROVED** | An admitted request reached qualified ingress. An OS event is not required for cooperative participating receipt. |
````````````````````````````````````````
