| M4 One canonical action owed/claimable | **CONDITIONAL** | First retained intent establishes the selected-action obligation. Claimability additionally requires the sole eligible runner and an unconsumed claim; FAILED may leave the obligation undelivered and unclaimable. |
| M5 Workload owner must observe | **NOT PROVED** | No admitted workload-observer duty. |
| M6 Workload owner must alter behavior | **NOT PROVED** | No delegated application/progress rule. |
| M7 Workload effect delivered | **NOT PROVED** | Retention is not workload access or delivery. |
| M8 Cancellation applied | **NOT PROVED** | No owner-authoritative application fact. |
| M9 Cancellation acknowledged | **NOT PROVED** | No workload acknowledgement contract. |

M1–M4 cannot establish M5–M9.

## F. GATE-13 SCHEDULE MATRIX

“Workload unresolved” below means no MI workload authority is established. It is neither permission to continue affected work nor proof that the workload stopped.

| Schedule | Membership state | Claim/accounting state | Workload-intent state | Progress allowed? | Settlement allowed? | Claim ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1 Failure before claim | Selected/subsumed membership retained | Unclaimed; no accounting | Workload unresolved | Failed capability cannot authorize affected healthy reuse/new work; attached workload consequence unresolved | No while runner unavailable/FAILED or action unaccounted | No alternate runner; an unused claim does not overcome failed admission |
| G2 Claim → pre-entry failure | Membership retained | Claim consumed; entry absent/unproved; no coherent accounting | Workload unresolved | Same failed-authority exclusion | No | No second claim, even if entry did not occur |
| G3 Entry → pre-accounting failure | Membership retained | Claim consumed; entry/outcome evidence may exist; accounting unavailable/uncertain | Workload unresolved | No healthy continuation through failed protection authority; wider workload rule unresolved | No | No replay to recover accounting or learn effect |
| G4 Coherent accounting | Membership remains current until lawful settlement | Claimed, entered, exact intended outcome accounted | No workload observation/application proved | Existing authorities only; accounting grants no new workload permission | Eligible only with all other prerequisites and a lawful runner | Local action completion only |
| G5 FAILED → later eligible pre-cut receipt | First receipt selects, or repeat subsumes, in retained current episode | Whatever earlier claim/accounting facts exist remain; no new dispatch | Workload unresolved | Failed capability stays excluded; unrelated computation is separately bounded | No | Receipt does not reactivate dispatcher or reset claim |
| G6 Participating membership | Membership begins at qualified retention; dequeue preserves old epoch | Independent of later dispatch/accounting | Same missing workload delegation | Adapter cannot authorize workload action | Existing prerequisites apply; dequeue alone is insufficient | No fresh claim or receipt from continuation |

The proposed candidates differ as follows. These are **conditional model consequences**, not selected authority:

| Schedule | MI-A | MI-B | MI-C | MI-D |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | Observation duty would begin at receipt despite no claim | No activated duty | No activated duty | T1 could derive; later triggers do not |
| G2 | Duty would already exist | Duty would begin at claim and must survive failed entry | No activated duty | Depends on whether derivation preceded failure |
| G3 | Duty would already exist | Duty would already exist | No activated duty without coherent accounting | T1/T2/T3 could derive; T4 does not |
| G4 | Claim/entry/accounting improve local evidence, not create another duty | Duty begins at claim | Duty begins at coherent accounting | One derivation at the selected trigger |
| G5 | New selected membership could activate without dispatch | Only an already-activated same-episode duty could cover repeats; an unclaimed episode cannot activate | Only an already-accounted same-episode duty could cover repeats; unaccounted membership cannot activate | T1 could derive after FAILED; dispatcher-dependent triggers cannot newly run |
| G6 | Same qualified-membership rule would apply | Participating origin would not bypass claim | Participating origin would not bypass accounting | Derivation must use the earlier membership, not dequeue as fresh ingress |

For **every candidate**, the workload actor requires new legitimate delegation. No candidate gets that authority from the activation timestamp.

For G1–G3 and G5, existing failed/unaccounted settlement exclusions remain regardless of candidate. For G4, the additional workload-disposition dependency is unresolved. G6 inherits the actual episode’s state.

Gate-13’s “consequential” meaning is **not merely diagnostic**: retained membership preserves undelivered/uncertain obligations, constrains settlement and successful shutdown, preserves attribution, and does not permit detachment or healthy reuse. That normative consequence does not, by itself, prove an additional workload-observation obligation.

| Action claim/accounting | Ledger and sole admitted dispatcher |
| Settlement | Sole runner acting through ledger prerequisites |
| Diagnostic interpretation | Reader has no transition ownership |

Recovered views:

| `_ReceiptResult` | Receipt/continuation result; not a workload command |

A workload actor cannot acquire command authority merely by reading these objects.

## H. WORKLOAD-OWNER ADMISSION

**WO-B — a separate admitted workload-owner binding is required.**

“Separate” here means a new semantic delegation/binding. It does **not** establish that a new actor, stored object or process is necessary.

The current [Association](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:386) retains Registry, work selector, invocation, ledger and executor relations. The [Registry](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:410) permanently reserves the first invocation owner and expressly lacks application actor attachment/new-work authority.

The accepted “future legitimate actor” is a placeholder for later attachment. It is not presently admitted to consume workload intent.

A sufficient future binding must establish:

- Exact observing actor identity and the authority that admits it.
- Its relation to the canonical Association and already-defined enclosing work.
- Whether it observes only, or enters a separately authorized effect protocol.
- Immutable attribution for existing receipts.
- Admission before authoritative use.
- Explicit timing relative to receipt qualification.
- No source, settlement, result, child-termination or retry authority transferred merely by observation.
- Retention and exclusion on owner loss, without an inferred successor.

**OB-U — owner-binding timing unresolved.**

OB-A avoids late adoption but cannot silently make missing workload binding a new receipt-rejection condition. Gate-13 receipt eligibility remains source-governed.

OB-B would require an explicit non-retargeting adoption transition grounded in an already-fixed work context. Neither its admitting authority nor that transition exists.

No actual workload-result owner is selected.

## I. ACTIONABILITY DEFINITION / TARGET CONTEXT

**WA-MI1** is the minimum meaning sufficient for this gate:

> Membership authorizes a legitimately admitted workload owner to observe the obligation and enter a separately governed effect protocol.

This definition does **not** authorize destructive application. It identifies the minimum authority being evaluated; it does not establish that current membership already possesses it.

**MIN-P — a neutral core is possible, with owner profiles supplying application semantics.**

Observation authority can be described without choosing official versus preparation result. However, a result-neutral description still needs an admitted actor and immutable same-work attribution. Neutral vocabulary does not complete those facts.

**MT-U — exact minimum target context remains unresolved.**

Association/work context alone currently identifies structural ownership, not an admitted workload consumer. Exact workload-owner identity plus fixed work attribution could suffice without a result target, but its sufficiency depends on the missing admission/timing rule. Exact result-target selection is neither required by this finding nor performed here.

## J. ACTION CLAIM / ACCOUNTING RELATION

**EAC-B — the existing action claim is dispatcher-local only.**

The [dispatch path](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:830) consumes the episode claim before constructing and invoking the exact outcome/action. It authorizes at most that canonical attempt.

It does not:

- Transfer membership ownership.
- Admit a workload observer.
- Prove action entry.
- Prove delivery to a workload.
- Supply a second actor’s destructive-effect claim.

One existing claim cannot silently become permission for two independently executing consumers. A composed shared claim would require new authority specifying both operations and every partial-failure disposition.

Coherent accounting establishes the exact local entry/outcome/accounting chain. The intended exception is caught inside the dispatcher. Accounting presently supplies no workload observation fact.

Under hypothetical MI-A, this action would retain its legitimate accepted purpose: the required cancellation-side selected action and evidence consumed by settlement. It could not also be described as a second workload application.

Under hypothetical MI-D, derivation would connect cancellation-side truth to a distinct workload responsibility. Accounting would remain local evidence unless an explicit derivation contract made it a trigger. The existence of two stages alone does not justify two cancellation attempts.

No accepted latency bound requires workload observation to wait for claim/accounting, or proves such waiting safe. Prompt qualified receipt is required; a new workload scheduling guarantee is not established.

## K. CURRENT / HISTORICAL / SUBSUMED MEMBERSHIP

**CURRENT-MEMBERSHIP:** qualified selected/subsumed membership belonging to the ledger’s current unresolved episode.

**HISTORICAL-MEMBERSHIP:** established membership of an earlier episode after lawful advancement. Historical attribution cannot become a fresh receipt or migrate to a new owner/target.

The sole admitted settlement runner publishes advancement by replacing `ledger.current`. Receipt/settlement ordering prevents prior completed receipt from being reassigned to the successor.

A material retention distinction:

- Settlement does not overwrite the old episode into a new receipt.
- Existing adapter/bridge references or retained evidence may preserve earlier facts.
- The current implementation does **not** establish a permanent archive of every prior episode.
- A surviving old object or diagnostic snapshot is not a retained workload-command capability.

Thus “old membership remains immutable” means its established attribution cannot be rewritten. It does not prove an independently retained post-settlement workload obligation.

**SUB-U — workload-obligation aggregation remains unresolved.**

Accepted cancellation-side behavior is one selected action plus eligible subsumption. Any future workload model must preserve that aggregation and introduce no independent per-request effects. SUB-A is compatible in principle, but its workload duty has not been admitted.

## L. FRESH EPISODE / PARTICIPATING MEMBERSHIP

**FE-U — fresh workload-observation obligation unresolved.**

A successor episode’s first qualified receipt is unquestionably fresh under applicable cancellation rules. That fact does not yet establish a fresh workload-observation duty. FE-B cannot be assumed: no authority makes one historical cancellation absorb all future episodes indefinitely.

**PM-U — workload-observation semantics for participating membership unresolved.**

Accepted receipt semantics are identical in the relevant respect: participating retention establishes real membership before dequeue. A future uniform membership-observation contract could support PM-A. There is no current basis for PM-B’s asymmetry.

Pending-only ordinary signal work remains outside ledger membership. TH-B/R0 ordinary service is not promoted into canonical intent by this gate.

Membership lifetime:

| Stage | Current membership? | Historical evidence? | Workload-observation obligation? | Repeated observation? | New destructive effect allowed by MI itself? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before first receipt | No; empty episode may exist | Prior evidence only if retained | None established | Diagnostic reads only | No |
| First selected receipt | Yes | Receipt evidence retained | Unresolved | Diagnostic reads repeatable | No |
| Subsumed repeats | Same episode | Earlier attribution preserved | Unresolved; no per-request effects | Same ceiling | No |
| Action claim | Yes | Claim fact retained | Not established by claim | Same ceiling | No |
| Action entry | Yes | Entry fact retained | Not established by entry | Same ceiling | No |
| Coherent accounting | Yes until settlement | Local completion evidence | Not established by accounting | Same ceiling | No |
| Invocation FAILED | Retained eligible membership survives | Failure/claim facts remain | Unresolved | Authorized diagnostics only | No |
| Clean settlement | Old membership no longer current | Survives only through actual retained evidence/references | Survival requirement unresolved | Historical diagnostics, not commands | No |
| Successor episode | Empty until fresh receipt | Prior attribution cannot migrate | Fresh workload duty unresolved | Current/history distinction required | No |
| Workload result terminal | May still be current | Immutable result independently preserved | Stale/disposition contract unresolved | Existing authorized reads only | No result mutation |
| Source cut | Successful cut excludes old new ingress; earlier episode facts remain historical where retained | Cut witness retained | No workload rule follows from cut | Diagnostic reads only | No |

## M. FAILED INVOCATION / WORKLOAD-PROGRESS CONSEQUENCE

**FI-U. WPF-U.**

These unresolved codes concern the **attached workload-wide consequence**, not established component exclusions.

The [accepted FAILED transition](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-u1-u2-rr1-pass-comprehensive-continuation.md:9492) permits pre-cut retention, inspection, and ordinary unrelated computation subject to host qualification. It prohibits new work, delivery/replay, clean settlement, COMPLETE and detachment through the failed capability.

The stronger reaper contract additionally requires explicit failed completion and prevents normal work through the affected protection authority when restoration, teardown or delivery fails. It forbids successful public completion with required delivery unresolved.

Neither source establishes:

- A separately admitted workload-observation duty surviving FAILED.
- Automatic terminalization of every associated workload result.
- Universal controller retirement.
- Permission for healthy affected work to continue merely because no workload consumer exists.

The missing work/observer binding prevents deciding whether an independently progressing operation is the affected governed work or permitted unrelated computation. WPF-B therefore cannot be asserted as a blanket continuation rule.

**Retirement authentication:** [controller retirement §4–6](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/governance/rq003-stage3c-controller-retirement-status-clarification-candidate.md:118) assigns status 12 only to independently established controller acquisition/handoff ownership uncertainty.

Its ordering is acquisition uncertainty → irrevocable RETIRING → permitted bounded housekeeping, if any → non-returning exit. It is not triggered by an ordinary exception or canonical InvocationRecord FAILED alone. Process exit does not prove child cleanup or discharge external obligations.

Consequently FI-B is unsupported. F2 retirement cannot be borrowed to make G1–G5 complete.

## N. MEMBERSHIP CONSUMPTION / EFFECT-CLAIM ANALYSIS

**MC-U. TRIG-U.**

Existing diagnostic observation is non-consuming and repeatable. An interrupted or uncertain read does not consume the canonical action claim.

A future authoritative read could also be non-consuming. Repeated observation need not violate no-replay. But a repeated observation cannot itself authorize repeated destructive application.

A separate effect claim is:

- **Not proved necessary** if the eventual authorized transition is monotonic/idempotent and its own authoritative state prevents duplication.
- **Not proved unnecessary** for an arbitrary active interruption mechanism.
- Not supplied by the existing dispatcher claim.

No idempotent collector latch, admission denial or cancelling-state transition is imported into the generic contract.

If a future effect claim were consumed and its owner disappeared, absence of acknowledgement would not permit replay. Application would remain failed/uncertain according to actual evidence, with no successor inferred.

Trigger alternatives:

| Model | Benefit | Missing authority |
|---|---|---|
| Level-triggered current membership | Repeated reads can recover missed observation without another receipt | Owner duty; what retains the level; disposition/settlement ordering |
| Edge-triggered derived obligation | Can retain a distinct delivery responsibility | Creator, trigger, owner, missed-edge retention and nonduplication |
| Diagnostic observation only | Already repeatable and non-consuming | Does not resolve AE-U because it creates no workload duty |

Mere permission to inspect is insufficient. WA-MI1 requires an admitted obligation to enter the owner’s effect protocol, not just an available read API.

## O. SETTLEMENT / SOURCE / INVOCATION-COMPLETE COMPATIBILITY

**MSC-U. SA-U. MSF-U. IC-U. SE-U. SM-U.**

These classify the unresolved **MI addition**. Existing settlement and COMPLETE rules remain unchanged.

Clean settlement currently requires retained terminal disposition, resolved restoration/teardown, accounted selected action, delivered/subsumed receipt dispositions, and no unresolved required delivery/invocation/restoration represented as success. The [implementation’s settlement transition](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:865) checks local prerequisites and replaces the current episode; it does not inspect workload acknowledgement.

The intended-exception delivery rule cannot be silently redefined as workload observation.

| Candidate | Settlement before workload disposition | Governance/lifetime consequence |
|---|---|---|
| MI-A / A-S1 | Would prohibit advancement until the new duty is disposed | New prerequisite; compatibility with stronger “required delivery” must be established, not assumed |
| MI-A / A-S2 | Would allow advancement while the duty survives | Requires an authoritative retained fact and owner; old-object readability alone is insufficient |
| MI-B | Claim activation does not establish post-settlement retention | Claim persistence is not an accepted workload-duty lifetime |
| MI-C | Accounting precedes settlement but does not prove workload observation | Settlement can still outrun the proposed new duty |
| MI-D | Could retain a derived obligation independently | Necessity, transfer/derivation, retention owner and source independence remain unresolved |
| MI-X | No smaller complete settlement relationship established | Unresolved |

A-S2 would effectively become MI-D if it requires a separately retained semantic obligation with independent lifetime, even if no new physical object is allocated.

Per-candidate classification remains **MSC-U / SA-U** for the prospective workload duty. Existing failed/unaccounted settlement rejection is accepted and complete.

Source impact is likewise unresolved:

- Current receipt obligations are ledger-owned within the source/capability responsibility graph.
- None of A–C establishes an independently surviving workload duty.
- D proposes one but does not yet lawfully create or retain it.
- No unresolved workload duty is newly declared source-independent, and no new finalization prerequisite or source cut is selected.

Invocation COMPLETE presently requires its own source/restoration/receipt/composition facts. This task adds none. Whether a future selected MI contract needs an additional prerequisite is IC-U; workload result terminality must not be circularly inserted.

For terminal targets, accepted immutability forbids result mutation. SM-A and SM-B require different new ordering/disposition facts; neither is established. A STALE acknowledgement is not created by this finding.

## S. MI-D / MI-X ANALYSIS

MI-D is **incomplete; semantic necessity is not established**.

A valid derived obligation would need one creator and owner, an exact trigger, immutable Association/episode/receipt linkage, a defined relation to the canonical action, and independent retention/disposition semantics. It must not independently decide whether cancellation occurred or belongs to different work.

| Trigger | Failure-schedule result |
|---|---|
| DO-T1 Qualified receipt | Could cover G1/G5; adds derivation responsibility at receipt. Partial derivation must not leave qualified membership without its required duty. |
| DO-T2 Action claim | Covers G2/G3 only if derivation is authoritatively inseparable or otherwise recoverably retained; misses unclaimed G1/G5 |
| DO-T3 Action entry | Misses G1/G2; entry-to-derivation uncertainty remains |
| DO-T4 Coherent accounting | Misses G1–G3 and unaccounted G5; accounting-to-derivation gap remains |
| DO-T5 Another point | No exact complete point established |
| Selected assessment | **DO-TU** |

MI-D §117 burdens:

- Trigger, creator, owner and admission: incomplete.
- Immutable linkage and one-episode aggregation: necessary constraints, not completed transitions.
- No duplicate truth: not proved across partial derivation.
- Gate-13 and derivation failure: incomplete.
- Owner loss: no successor; duty disposition incomplete.
- Settlement and independent lifetime: incomplete.
- Old/new episode and historical/current separation: constraints established; derived-duty contract absent.
- No replay and no generalized subsystem: preserved.
- Authority classification: consequential choices unresolved.

MI-X has no distinct smaller complete contract. An informational-only read does not resolve AE-U. An obligatory observation protocol would still need the same admission, failure and lifetime authority; renaming it does not close those gaps.

A direct membership model and a necessary derived-obligation model remain viable in principle. Neither is selected as a preferred incomplete model.

## C. MI-U INHERITED OBSERVER-ADMISSION PROBLEM

MI-U’s exact selected edge is:

```text
canonical Association’s fixed same-work context
→ immutable admission of a legitimate workload-observation owner
```

Its established limits remain:

- Qualified membership is cancellation-side authority.
- No workload-observation authority is presently delegated.

- A distinct derived effect obligation is not proved necessary.

This investigation narrows the blocker: **the fixed structural work selector has no authenticated binding to the actor entitled to nominate or become its workload observer.**

That is a work-ownership provenance problem before it is an observer scheduling problem.

## D. ASSOCIATION / WORK / OWNER AUTHORITY

The [accepted ownership/interface contract](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-u1-u2-rr1-pass-comprehensive-continuation.md:9405) and [current Association/Registry](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:386) distinguish these roles.

**Notation correction:** accepted CS-R1 **D is the native root/control/evidence cell**, not the action dispatcher. The dispatcher is the sole runner’s `_Ledger._dispatch`. Conflating them would incorrectly transfer action authority to a structural native cell.

| Actor/object | Classification | Authority actually established |

| Registry | AO-STRUCT | Retains canonical work→Association mappings; no global broker or workload admission role |

**No recovered actor qualifies as AO-OBSERVER.**

Registry reservation semantics are exact:

1. `_reserve(work)` constructs `_Invocation()`.
2. It constructs `_Association(self, work, owner)`.
3. It links invocation, ledger and initial episode.
4. `setdefault` retains the first Association under that key.
5. Duplicate reservation does not replace that owner.
6. `_admit_new_work` rejects: “this registry is not new-work admission authority.”

The retained “owner” is therefore the invocation owner. Its permanence does not establish ownership of official execution, preparation assessment or any other concrete enclosing workload.

Association construction receives **Registry, work string and invocation**. It derives ledger, executor, entry and preparation references. It receives no application actor or workload-owner authority.

Association has no separate meta-owner. Registry constructs and retains it; its members point back to it. Existing private constructors/transitions may establish only their enumerated relationships. The prospective source-binding writer is the exact Registry, but that is specifically source binding—not arbitrary relationship admission.

The accepted [source graph](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-u1-u2-rr1-pass-comprehensive-continuation.md:125) fixes Association→S/H, S→H and H→D. No second S, shared H, alias factory or rebind is admitted.

The future-actor placeholders constrain retention before work/source effects, legitimate ownership, supported runtime/profile and later qualified attachment. They do **not** identify an observer, its cardinality, nominating authority or receipt-relative admission timing.

## E. OBSERVER ROLE / IDENTITY

**OBS-B — observation plus authority to enter a separately governed effect protocol.**

The minimum coherent prospective role is:

> A legitimately admitted observer may authoritatively observe qualified current membership for its already-fixed enclosing work, retain its exact attribution, and enter a future effect protocol only under that protocol’s separately established authorization.

This is a role definition, **not admission of an actor or activation of an MI duty**. OBS-A as a merely available read would not satisfy MI-U’s WA-MI1. OBS-C would unnecessarily grant effect ownership.

The minimum authoritative read would identify:

- Canonical Association and fixed work context.
- Exact current episode and selected/subsumed membership.
- Relevant FAILED and settlement/currentness facts.
- The admitted observer’s authority over that context.

Historical facts may support diagnostics and attribution; they are not fresh commands. Diagnostic views already exist, but [their interface contract](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-u1-u2-rr1-pass-comprehensive-continuation.md:9435) explicitly supplies no delegation.

**OID-U — observer identity unresolved.**

| Candidate | Finding |
|---|---|
| OID-A: actor/lifecycle | Could distinguish an exact observer, but actor identity alone does not prove entitlement to this work |
| OID-B: controller-operation owner | Resource operation ownership exists; no canonical work/observer mapping |
| OID-C: workload-domain owner | Potentially sufficient and result-neutral; no exact admitted domain-owner relation |
| OID-D: result owner | Not required by the bounded observation role; selecting it would prematurely resolve a different gate |
| OID-X | No other complete authenticated identity |
| OID-U | Required classification |

Python object identity can distinguish objects inside the authenticated graph; it cannot establish workload legitimacy. A PID, controller instance or operation ID likewise does not establish that relationship. Reconstructed objects or restarted processes cannot inherit observer authority by resemblance.

An actor could conceptually own several works, and several actors could participate in one work. Neither fact supplies authority for multiple observers. No accepted mapping resolves those cardinalities here.

| Model | Assessment |
|---|---|
| OC-1 | Compatible in principle with one immutable same-work observer; admission, loss and lifetime remain incomplete |
| OC-S | No transition authority; fresh episodes alone cannot authorize a different observer |
| OC-M | Unsupported: no composition preventing independent effects or conflicting dispositions |
| OC-X | No distinct complete bounded model |

Concurrent fan-out is rejected as an available authority. Sequential replacement is also unavailable absent an explicit transition contract.

A single observer is the smallest plausible cardinality, but its plausibility does not complete the admission or lifetime contract and is not selected as a preferred incomplete OA architecture.

## G. ADMISSION-OWNER ANALYSIS

**ADM-U — admission authority unresolved.**

“Early enough” below concerns observer admission, not merely existence of a structural object.

| Candidate | Knows fixed work? | Exists early enough? | Owns delegation? | Can bind immutable observer? | Borrows other authority? | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Registry reservation authority | Knows local selector/graph; concrete work-owner mapping absent | Before invocation entry; observer knowledge unproved | No accepted workload delegation | No current transition | Yes, if reservation is promoted into workload authority | Unsupported currently; incomplete prospectively |
| Association constructor | Receives selector and invocation | Before prepared execution; observer not an input | No | No observer construction contract | Yes, if constructor authenticity is treated as actor legitimacy | Incomplete |
| Source-binding/admission authority | Knows canonical source/Association | Before source responsibility; workload timing unresolved | Source authority only | No workload delegation | Yes | Unsupported as sufficient |
| Actual work/controller owner | Knows its own local workload | Varies; no canonical ordering established | Local responsibilities only | Missing authenticated mapping to Registry work | Self-assertion would borrow canonical admission authority | Incomplete |
| Invocation owner/executor | Knows canonical cancellation graph | Exists before receipts | Invocation execution only | No actor-attachment operation | Yes | Unsupported as sufficient |
| Eventual Registry-retaining actor | Placeholder for enclosing executable ownership | Required before effects in accepted architecture | No instantiated nomination contract | Unresolved | Cannot infer from retention | Incomplete |
| Distinct bounded authority | Would need to attest exact work-owner relation | Unspecified | Not established | Conceivable, not authorized | Avoidable only with an independent authority chain | Incomplete |
| Other accepted authority | No additional qualifying owner found | Unestablished | Unestablished | Unestablished | Unresolved | Unsupported |

A bounded distinct authority, if justified later, would attest only:

```text
this exact lifecycle actor is authorized for
this preexisting Association’s fixed enclosing work
```

It would not be a general actor directory. Naming such an authority does not establish who legitimately possesses it.

The official orchestrator has its own [bound lifecycle authorities](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/orchestrator.py:817). Preparation has a [sole outer assessor](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/evidence_preparation.py:736). Resource operation ownership is separately governed. None is currently connected to Registry `work` by an observer-nomination contract.

Self-admission is circular unless an independently established work-owner relationship precedes and authenticates it. Source ownership cannot supply that missing workload relationship.

## H. FIXED-WORK ANCHOR

**FW-U — semantic sufficiency of the fixed-work anchor remains unresolved.**

The existing graph does establish:

```text
exact Registry
→ exact work selector
→ first retained Association
→ exact invocation / ledger / executor
→ accepted canonical source relationship
```

This is sufficient to distinguish the **same canonical cancellation context** from another graph. It does not establish which actual enclosing workload the selector denotes or who may represent that work.

Therefore:

- FW-A is not established for legitimate observer admission.
- FW-B is possible, but a new domain identity is not proved necessary: an authenticated owner relationship might suffice.
- FW-C is not required by the observation role.
- A string key is not an actor credential.

**LA-B**, as an analytical anchor assessment: the existing graph constrains the context, but an additional exact admission fact is needed. That fact is not yet supplied.

**OW-U:** whether one observer can span sequential result targets inside a larger work context remains unresolved. A later target transition cannot change the meaning of old receipts.

## I. PRE-RECEIPT BINDING ANALYSIS

The clean hypothetical sequence is:

```text
fixed work and legitimate owner established
→ observer admitted
→ qualified receipt retained with that observer context
```

This would provide attribution before receipt without requiring a result identity. It would grant no application, child, result or source power.

But **AT-A is not established**, and **PRQ-U** remains.

The [adopted receipt rule](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/governance/rq003-stage3c-sole-reaper-cancellation-receipt-settlement-clarification-candidate.md:120) requires source-specific legitimate ingress and indivisible retention/classification. It does not make observer presence an eligibility predicate.

| Proposed prerequisite | Consequence |
|---|---|
| PRQ-S: block source admission | New source-admission prerequisite; compatibility and before-source coverage must be established |
| PRQ-R: block qualified receipt | Cannot be silently added; conflicts with existing receipt obligations if used to reject otherwise eligible ingress |
| PRQ-W: block cancellable work start | Does not by itself prove admission precedes **every receipt** |
| PRQ-X | No exact alternative established |

If observer admission rejects or is uncertain, no observer authority is proved. Existing source/receipt rules remain in force. No retry, source activation, new work-start permission, retirement or successful binding follows.

Prebinding is a possible architecture. The evidence does not prove it necessary or currently authorized.

## J. LATE-ADOPTION ANALYSIS

An otherwise qualified receipt remains valid cancellation-side membership when no observer exists. Prospective observer incompleteness does not invalidate historical receipt authority.

Late adoption would require an authoritative fact that the admitted actor belongs to the **already-fixed work**, rather than choosing work for the receipt afterward.

Missing elements include:

- An independently legitimate adoption authority.
- An exact observer identity.
- Exclusion of competing candidates.
- Permission relative to FAILED.
- Permission relative to settlement.
- A retained obligation, if adoption must remain possible after ordinary settlement eligibility.
- Loss/replacement and episode-span rules.

A receipt remaining current, with no intervening target change or effect, is the strongest late-adoption case. Those circumstances eliminate some hazards but do not create delegation authority.

| Membership state | Prospective adoption classification | Present ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| Selected/unclaimed | UNRESOLVED | Retain membership; no observer delegation |
| Claimed/pre-entry | UNRESOLVED | Claim stays consumed; no second consumer authority |
| Entered/unaccounted | UNRESOLVED | No replay or inferred accounting |
| Coherently accounted | UNRESOLVED | Local success is not observer admission |
| Invocation FAILED | UNRESOLVED | No new observer authority through failed capability |
| Participating-retained | UNRESOLVED | Earlier membership preserved; dequeue is not new admission |
| Settlement-eligible | UNRESOLVED | No selected adoption/settlement ordering |
| Historical membership | DENY | **HM-NO:** no fresh workload authority from history |

“UNRESOLVED” is not permission to attempt adoption. It means no complete prospective rule is established.

An unavailable intended observer cannot be replaced by whichever candidate is available. That would require precisely the successor/nomination authority missing here.

## K. RECEIPT / ADMISSION / SETTLEMENT / FAILED RACES

**AT-U. FO-U. SO-U. HM-NO.**

| Ordering | Established result | Missing observer consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Admission before receipt | Only meaningful if admission is independently valid | No qualifying admission contract yet |
| Receipt before admission | Eligible receipt retains its original membership | Lawful later adopter/timing unresolved |
| Concurrent receipt/admission | Receipt retains adopted source/settlement semantics | No common ordering authority established |
| FAILED before admission | Retained receipt survives; dispatcher/settlement exclusion remains | Whether new observation-only delegation is permissible is unresolved |
| Admission before FAILED | Failure cannot justify retargeting existing attribution | Survival and availability of the proposed observer duty unresolved |
| Settlement before adoption | Old membership becomes historical under lawful settlement | Cannot subsequently become fresh workload authority |
| Adoption before settlement | Any actual required duty would need an explicit disposition/lifetime rule | Such a duty is not yet admitted |
| Read immediately before settlement | A read proves at most its ordered observation | Does not prove later application, handoff or duty survival |

FAILED’s accepted permissions are retained pre-cut receipt, inspection and separately bounded unrelated computation. Its prohibitions include new work, delivery/replay, clean settlement, COMPLETE and detachment through the failed capability.

It would be unsound both to:

- Infer **FO-A** merely because the proposed observer “only reads”; or
- Infer a complete **FO-B** merely from a prohibition on dispatch/new work.

Whether a new delegation is an allowed read relationship or prohibited new attachment is the missing authority choice.

Likewise, existing settlement prerequisites remain unchanged. Missing prospective observer architecture does not itself add a settlement blocker. Conversely, a future mandatory adoption duty cannot silently disappear through settlement. Selecting SO-B would introduce that new duty and require explicit compatibility analysis.

Gate-13:

| Schedule | Accepted cancellation-side result | Observer-admission result |
|---|---|---|
| G1: failure before claim | Membership retained; no alternate runner; no settlement | No admitted observer duty; later admission unresolved |
| G2: claim then pre-entry failure | Claim consumed; no replay | Claim does not delegate observation |
| G3: entry then pre-accounting failure | Entry does not establish accounting; no replay | Observation delegation still absent |
| G4: coherent accounting | Local action complete; other settlement prerequisites still required | No proof of workload observation |
| G5: FAILED then eligible pre-cut receipt | Select/subsume in retained current episode; no dispatch revival | Receipt does not admit an observer |
| G6: participating retention | Membership begins at retention; dequeue continues it | Same missing delegation; no origin-specific shortcut |

No MI settlement policy or workload application rule is selected.

## L. OBSERVER LOSS / REPLACEMENT

**ORP-U. OL-U. OLIFE-U.**

The immutable-attribution ceiling is established; a complete operational loss policy is not.

| Loss boundary | Required preservation | Unresolved consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Before first receipt | Do not infer clearing/replacement permission | Whether work/source may start, binding may be replaced, or work must retire |
| After receipt, before observation | Receipt cannot migrate; retain original attribution where established | Required workload failure/retirement and observation disposition |
| After observation, before AE application | Observation is not application or acknowledgement | Whether a separately admitted effect owner already holds responsibility |
| After a future lawful effect-owner handoff | Only actually established handoff evidence counts | No such handoff contract selected here |

Replacement before first receipt is not automatically harmless: it may change the actor defining the same-work relationship. Replacement after receipt cannot rewrite attribution.

A genuinely new work context is not replacement for old receipts. But Registry permanence does not authorize reusing the old Association for that new work.

Process restart, reconstructed object, result-owner recovery and observer replacement are distinct. No existing recovery contract was found that transfers this unadmitted role.

Observer loss is not automatically controller retirement status 12. That status has the separate [acquisition-ownership uncertainty trigger](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/governance/rq003-stage3c-controller-retirement-status-clarification-candidate.md:118).

## M. EPISODE / PARTICIPATING SPAN

**OE-U. POBS-U. OLIFE-U.**

Accepted episode semantics remain:

- First qualified receipt selects.
- Eligible same-work repeats subsume.
- Lawful settlement advances the ledger.
- A successor’s first qualified receipt is fresh.
- Participating retention establishes membership before dequeue.

One same-work observer spanning all episodes is coherent in principle. No accepted observer lifetime yet establishes OE-A. Per-episode admission would need justification and could not let a fresh episode select a new owner for old receipts.

There is no evidence supporting a different observer authority for participating membership. A future uniform contract is compatible with the accepted receipt rule, but **POBS-A is not claimed as an already-complete observer contract**.

Observer authority cannot extend to unrelated later work merely because the same process, actor or retained graph remains. Physical retention may outlast authority.

## N. OBSERVER / RESULT / EFFECT / SOURCE / LEDGER AUTHORITY CEILINGS

**ORO-A — observer and result owner may differ.** The role can remain result-neutral. Neither official nor preparation is selected.

**OEO-A — observation is separate from effect ownership.** This is a role separation, not an admitted handoff. A future AE protocol must authenticate any effect owner and delegation; OBS-B does not authorize forwarding to an arbitrary actor.

Observer admission alone grants none of the following:

| Authority | Ceiling |
|---|---|
| Source | No S ownership transfer, installation/restoration, registration, source cut, E3 or reference discharge |
| Receipt | No admission, selection, subsumption or reclassification |
| Action | No dispatcher claim, action execution, accounting or replay |
| Ledger | No settlement, epoch advancement or FAILED mutation |
| Result | No VALID/INVALID/FAILED publication, preparation assessment or terminal rewrite |
| Child/process | Observation is not termination; no spawn, kill, wait or synthetic terminal disposition |
| F2 | No acquisition-policy mutation or borrowed retirement authority |
| Recovery | No retry, successor admission or ownership transfer |

The [bridge contract](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:1170) already separates retention/continuation from source installation and descriptor ownership. The [sole-reaper contract](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/governance/rq003-stage3c-sole-reaper-interruption-admission-clarification-candidate.md:301) separately governs disposition, restoration and pending delivery.

## C. OA-U INHERITED WORK-PROVENANCE PROBLEM

OA-U’s exact missing relation is:

```text
Registry’s fixed work selector / Association
→ authenticated legitimate lifecycle owner of that enclosing work
```

The current evidence establishes a canonical cancellation graph. It does not establish the actor entitled to represent the workload denoted by its selector.

Three distinct facts must remain separate:

1. A caller supplies a valid key.
2. Registry retains one canonical Association under that key.
3. An independently authorized actor owns the actual enclosing work.

Only the first two are established by reservation. Choosing observer timing cannot supply the third. Source authority, invocation ownership, diagnostic access and result identity cannot supply it either.

## D. REGISTRY `work` SEMANTICS / PROOF CEILING

**WI-B — Registry work is cancellation-capability association identity only.**

This classification describes the selector’s established functional meaning: it selects one canonical cancellation association within one Registry. Its value is caller-chosen; it is not an authenticated workload identifier.

The [current implementation](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:386) and [accepted interface contract](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-u1-u2-rr1-pass-comprehensive-continuation.md:9435) establish:

| Property | Exact finding |
|---|---|
| Type | Exact `str`; subclasses and other types rejected. |
| Validation | Nonempty; no workload-specific grammar, normalization or provenance validation. |
| Value chooser | Caller of `_reserve(work)`. |
| Arbitrary naming prevention | Type/nonempty validation only; no independent semantic naming authority. |
| Uniqueness | Registry-instance-local dictionary-key equality. |
| Lookup | Equal string values select the retained mapping; distinct string-object identity is not a new work. |
| Reservation | Constructs `_Invocation`, constructs `_Association`, links invocation/ledger/initial episode, retains through `setdefault`. |
| Duplicate | Returns inspection of the retained original; cannot replace Association or invocation. |
| Owner | Newly constructed InvocationRecord; not the reservation caller. |
| Lifetime | First mapping retained permanently within that Registry; no delete/reset/retry API. |
| Persistence | No accepted durable/restart reconstruction contract. |
| New work | `_admit_new_work` explicitly rejects: “this registry is not new-work admission authority.” |
| Source | Accepted prospective canonical source binding is subordinate to the fixed Association; source ownership does not establish workload ownership. |
| Diagnostics | `_records` is a copy; `_inspect` is diagnostic, not an owner credential or delegation. |

First-reservation permanence proves a stable canonical Association and invocation graph. Accepted source binding separately constrains its later S/H/D relation. It proves neither a stable workload owner nor a result owner nor an observer.

No production WO-CONTROLLER, WO-REQUEST, WO-ATTEMPT or WO-OPERATION mapping is established. Generating any such value would not itself authenticate ownership.

**RC-U — production reservation-caller relationship unresolved.** The internal constructor is infrastructure; that does not establish whether the eventual attached caller is owner or delegate.

## E. LIFECYCLE-OWNER DEFINITION / IDENTITY

The minimum coherent role remains:

> **The actor with authoritative responsibility for admitting, retaining and terminating one bounded enclosing work lifecycle.**

“Terminating” means responsibility for the lifecycle’s terminal disposition. It does not automatically grant process-killing, source-restoration or result-publication power.

| Responsibility | Included by this definition? |
|---|---|
| Work admission | Yes, for its exact bounded lifecycle |
| Retention | Yes, continuity of that lifecycle’s responsibility |
| Termination | Yes, authoritative lifecycle disposition |
| Scientific/result publication | No automatic grant |
| Source authority | No |
| Child/process authority | No automatic grant |
| Cancellation transitions | No |
| Observer nomination | Requires later explicit authority |
| Result/effect-owner binding | Requires separate authority |

**LOID-U — no exact canonical lifecycle-owner identity is established.**

| Identity candidate | Assessment |
|---|---|
| LOID-A Retained actor/lifecycle object | Can distinguish an actor locally; does not prove entitlement to this work. |
| LOID-B Authenticated controller-operation | Existing operation identities cover coordination/resources, not the required enclosing-work relation. |
| LOID-C Bounded domain plus actor | Semantically sufficient in principle; exact domain and admitting authority absent. |
| LOID-D Result owner | Unnecessary for the minimum role and would prematurely choose another gate. |
| LOID-X | No smaller complete alternative found. |

A future identity must remain attributable across subordinate child churn. An actor reference, PID or result hash alone cannot provide that guarantee.

**WR-N / LO-RO-A:** lifecycle ownership can remain distinct from result ownership. This is a supported role separation, not an instantiated ownership binding.

**LO-U:** whether the owner itself observes or may nominate/delegate observation remains unselected. WP supplies no observer authority.

Supporting distinctions:

- [Official execution](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/orchestrator.py:847) orders readiness → launch preparation/authentication → smoke → remote revalidation → allocation → STARTED → primary work → reconstruction/publication.
- Its [lifecycle authority](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/orchestrator.py:1020) binds process-local capabilities to the exact orchestrator. The module expressly remains port-driven and non-operational without configured authority.
- [Allocation](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/attempts.py:325) distinguishes rejected, ambiguous-ordinal-consumed and committed outcomes. Its immutable attempt identity is profile-specific and unavailable before allocation.
- [Preparation’s outer entry](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/evidence_preparation.py:736) owns the assessment. The detached controller returns evidence; its stdout is not outer authority.
- Preparation request material supplies source, experiment, policy and input context. It does not establish a unique authenticated request-attempt/lifecycle-owner identity.
- [Operation IDs](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/governance/rq003-experiment-005-bounded-streaming-source-processing-prerequisite-v1.md:252) are controller-generated coordination authority, explicitly not scientific or artifact identity.

Canonical Invocation FAILED supplies no termination or survival rule for these external actors. No accepted relation makes them canonical owner merely because they remain alive.

## G. ROOT-OF-TRUST / ATTESTING-AUTHORITY ANALYSIS

**ROOT-U — independent authority over the Registry-work/owner relation remains unresolved.**

Reservation validates structural context. It does not validate the caller’s jurisdiction over an enclosing workload.

| Authority | Already owns work relation? | Can identify owner? | Independent of self-assertion? | Pre/atomic/post capable? | Scope bounded? | Classification |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Registry caller | Not proved | Can name itself; legitimacy unproved | No established check | Reservation-local only | Structural Registry scope | Unresolved |
| Controller creation authority | Owns particular child launch | Identifies launched controller, not whole-work owner | Yes for launch; not WP relation | Before child; WP timing unresolved | Yes locally | Accepted locally; WP unresolved |
| Official request authority | Request names experiment | Does not identify owner | No owner credential | Before execution; WP timing unresolved | Request scope | Insufficient |
| Preparation request authority | Supplies authenticated preparation inputs | No admitted lifecycle owner | Source authenticity is not ownership attestation | Before detached execution; WP timing unresolved | Input/pipeline scope | Insufficient |
| Attempt allocation authority | Owns official allocation relation | Binds attempt/control context | Yes within allocation contract | After launch preparation; WP timing unresolved | Yes | Accepted locally; WP prospective |
| Resource operation/root authority | Owns resource coordination | Identifies resource owner | Yes within resource contract | Local operation ordering only | Yes | Conflict if promoted without authority |
| Official lifecycle binder | Owns process-local official capability issuance | Identifies exact orchestrator lifecycle | Independently checks its local lifecycle facts | Before/within official execution | Yes | Accepted locally; no Registry mapping |
| Distinct bounded work authority | No established instance | Would need to identify owner | Not yet grounded | Unselected | Could be bounded | Prospective, necessity unresolved |
| Source authority | Owns source obligations | Does not authenticate workload owner | Independent only in source domain | Irrelevant to WP attestation | Yes | Unsupported as WP root |

Registry possession is not an exclusive owner credential. Accepted retention requirements do not forbid legitimate helpers from possessing references, establish a non-transferable reservation capability, or authenticate a parent commissioning relationship. Private Python naming provides no such proof.

A minimum semantic attestation would be:

```text
ATTEST(exact work context, exact lifecycle owner, independently authorized attestor)
```

Required meaning:

| Element | Requirement / present result |
|---|---|
| Work context | Exact Registry/selector/Association plus independently established enclosing-work meaning; latter absent |
| Owner | Exact bounded lifecycle actor, not merely PID/name; unselected |
| Attestor | Already possesses admission authority over that same work; unselected |
| SUCCESS | Authoritative establishment of that exact relation, not successful string insertion |
| CONFLICT | Incompatible claimant/context cannot replace established attribution |
| Uncertainty | No successful provenance claim until authoritative evidence resolves it |
| Immutability | Already-established attribution cannot be rewritten by duplicate claim, receipt, loss or recovery |

These are completeness requirements, not a selected transition. No implementation, serialization or new authority is created.

## H. RESERVATION / PROVENANCE ORDERING

**PO-U. PA-U.**

| Ordering | Evidence and limit |

“Register before work” in accepted architecture orders structural retention against governed work/effects. It does not independently settle when owner provenance is established.

An otherwise qualified receipt can exist without a workload-owner attestation under current cancellation-side rules. This does **not** establish a lawful production owner-adoption contract.

POST therefore lacks its independent anchor-to-actual-work relation and adopting authority. Receipt retention cannot supply them retrospectively.

| Case | Established rule |

For a future contract allowing one actor to own several works, identity must bind at least **(owner identity, exact work context)**. Actor identity alone is insufficient. Current evidence neither establishes universal one-to-one ownership nor admits arbitrary multi-work ownership.

A mismatch between authenticated work A and selected context B cannot bind by “closest match.” The binding must remain unproved/conflicting. A specific quarantine, failure or recovery transition is not established here.

## L. OWNER LOSS SCHEDULES

The rows below distinguish required attribution preservation from an **unresolved operational loss policy**. They do not assume an actual owner binding already exists.

| Boundary | Old owner attribution | Replacement allowed? | Recovery allowed? | Receipt retargeting? | New work required? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before reservation | Preserve any independently proved prior relation | No inferred successor; exact policy unresolved | Only independently scoped recovery; no WP transfer | No receipt yet; no future reassignment by convenience | Continuation versus abandonment unresolved |
| After reservation / before receipt | Structural mapping remains; any proved attribution preserved | Duplicate reservation cannot replace owner | No accepted WP recovery | Future receipt cannot justify reassignment | Whether same work remains active unresolved |
| After receipt | Original receipt/context and proved owner history remain | No automatic successor | No WP transfer established | **No** | Loss consequence/new-work boundary unresolved |
| After FAILED | Attribution remains; failed graph retained | No replacement through failed capability | No revival; other recovery retains separate scope | **No** | New work cannot reuse failed authority |
| After lawful settlement | Historical episode remains historical; work may be distinct from episode lifetime | No succession from settlement | No WP transfer established | **No** | Settlement alone does not require or establish new work |
| After terminal result | Valid historical attribution may remain after actor disappears | Result existence grants no successor | Result recovery does not transfer ownership | **No** | A new workload needs independently established provenance |

Owner loss does not, by itself, prove source closure, Association invalidity, successful retirement, or permission for later source/observer attachment. Those consequences cannot be supplied by borrowing controller-retirement status or source-failure rules.

Immutable evidence could preserve historical ownership after an actor disappears. No live actor need exist forever merely to preserve a true historical fact. The actual evidence-retention contract remains unbound.

## M. RECEIPT / FAILED / SETTLEMENT / SUCCESSOR RELATION

| Schedule | Established result | WP ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| Receipt before owner provenance | Independently qualified cancellation-side membership remains valid | No workload authority; later active adoption unresolved |
| FAILED before provenance | Retained eligible membership survives; dispatch/clean-settlement restrictions remain | No new attachment or revival inferred |
| Lawful settlement before provenance | Membership becomes historical | Later attribution cannot turn it into fresh cancellation authority |
| Owner provenance before FAILED | Any valid attribution remains historically true | Cannot reactivate FAILED |
| Fresh receipt after lawful settlement | New episode under existing rules | Not a new lifecycle owner or new workload by inference |
| Participating retention before dequeue | Membership begins at retention | Later dequeue cannot change provenance or create freshness |

**SP-N:** current cancellation-side settlement does not add a workload-owner-provenance prerequisite. Existing action, native-terminal, protection, receipt and uncertainty requirements remain controlling. FAILED still prevents clean settlement.

The following separation is a necessary compatible constraint on any future WP contract:

- Invocation FAILED cannot erase valid historical work-owner provenance.
- Valid work-owner provenance cannot revive FAILED dispatch/capability.

The first statement preserves attribution; it does not establish a new provenance-admission operation after FAILED.

**EPW-SAME, conditional on independently established same enclosing work:** a fresh cancellation episode does not itself change the work-owner relation. The current missing owner binding prevents an operational span claim.

For genuinely new work, stale attribution cannot suffice. Its semantic work context and legitimate owner relationship must be established independently. Current first-Association permanence prevents replacing the old invocation under the same Registry key; it does not authorize a new-work creation mechanism.

Provenance alone grants no source installation/restoration, receipt admission, dispatcher claim/action, ledger settlement, child termination, result publication or observer delegation.

## N. HISTORICAL PROVENANCE / UNCERTAINTY

**HP-A — historical attribution is permissible for provenance/audit only, when independent evidence proves the historical relation.**

This is a result-neutral evidentiary boundary, not authority for post-hoc operational adoption.

| Historical case | Permitted claim |
|---|---|
| HP1 Owner known prospectively and retained | Report the established relation within its original scope. |
| HP2 Evidence lost but reconstructable | Re-establish the historical fact only from independently authoritative evidence; resemblance is insufficient. |
| HP3 Owner never established prospectively | Do not invent a past admission. A later declaration cannot make a nonexistent authoritative act historical. |
| HP4 Competing historical claims | Preserve conflict; no sole-owner claim until competent authority/evidence resolves it. |
| HP5 Selector reused later | Keep contexts separate; later use does not identify old owner. |
| HP6 Terminal result but no owner provenance | Result existence proves only its own governed facts, not Registry-work ownership. |

No indefinite storage requirement or reconstruction mechanism is selected.

Provenance uncertainty:

| Case | Work-owner fact | Registry/Association fact | Permitted observation | Prohibited inference/action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PU1 Admission definitely rejected | No relation from that attempt | Independent reservation facts unchanged | Inspect rejection and existing state | Treat rejection as success |
| PU2 Admission may have succeeded | Unproved | Independently observed facts only | Reobserve authoritative evidence | Infer success; install convenient replacement |
| PU3 Reservation succeeded, owner uncertain | Unproved | Original structural mapping established | Inspect both facts separately | Promote reservation into attestation |
| PU4 Owner relation proved, reservation uncertain | Relation may exist independently | Reservation unproved | Authenticate actual retained mapping | Assume reservation or repeat an undefined transition |
| PU5 Owner lost during transition | Only independently established disposition counts | Only observed reservation counts | Preserve uncertainty and loss evidence | Infer rollback, success or successor |
| PU6 Conflict after apparent success | Prior evidence plus unresolved contradiction | Existing mapping cannot be overwritten | Retain and investigate conflict | Last-writer-wins or silent evidence repair |

Rereading authoritative evidence is not replaying admission. A same-actor repeat is not automatically an idempotent transition. Different-actor claims cannot be resolved by arrival order.

## C. WP-U INHERITED COMMISSIONING-AUTHORITY PROBLEM

The exact inherited missing edge is:

```text
an independently legitimate bounded-work admission authority
→ commissioning the eventual Registry-retaining actor
  to represent that exact work context
```

The distinction is between:

1. Creating a structural cancellation Association.
2. Identifying an actual enclosing work.
3. Having jurisdiction over that work.
4. Authorizing an exact actor to represent it.

The [Registry implementation](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:410) establishes the first. It accepts an exact nonempty string, retains the first Association/invocation, and rejects using `_admit_new_work` as new-work admission authority.

It does not establish the remaining three. A caller’s presence, object possession, or successful reservation cannot supply them.

## H. COMMISSIONING FACT / SUCCESS / CONFLICT / UNCERTAINTY

The minimum prospective fact is:

```text
COMMISSION(W, L, A)
```

Its required meaning is:

- W is one exact independently established bounded work.
- A already has jurisdiction over W.
- L is the exact actor authorized for the selected CR role.
- The role is bounded to W.
- Commissioning neither redefines W nor grants unrelated powers.
- Successful attribution cannot be silently overwritten.
- Uncertain commissioning is not successful commissioning.

This is a completeness specification, not a selected or executed transition.

Success must prove W, L, A, A’s jurisdiction, L’s bounded role, immutable attribution, and the scope of permissible later reliance. Successful construction, launch, request validation, or reservation is insufficient.

**CCONFLICT-U:** no complete adjudication contract is established. The mandatory ceiling is nevertheless exact: retain prior authoritative attribution and the contradictory evidence; no last-writer-wins and no authority selection by actor arrival.

| Situation | Claim ceiling |
|---|---|
| Definite rejection | No commission from that attempt. W’s independent existence is a separate fact. |
| Uncertain transition | Neither L nor Registry may rely on unproved commissioning. |
| Same A/W/L repeats | Rereading evidence is distinct from replaying admission; idempotence is not assumed. |
| Different L appears | Appearance supplies no replacement authority. |
| Competing A/B claims | Their jurisdiction must be established independently; agreement-shaped data is insufficient. |
| Known success, later evidence publication fails | Do not erase known success solely because publication failed; later consumers still need authoritative evidence. |
| Observation | Independently authorized observation may clarify disposition; it grants no new transition power. |

Choosing another actor, replaying commissioning, declaring rollback, or proceeding because “it probably succeeded” is unavailable without a separately established rule.

A later mismatch must remain mismatch. It cannot be repaired by changing what W meant or selecting convenient work after receipt.

## M. FAILED / SETTLEMENT / SUCCESSOR / HISTORICAL RELATION

**CS-N — no commissioning prerequisite is added to current cancellation-side settlement.**

The following separation is preserved:

- A true commission remains true as provenance after Invocation FAILED.
- FAILED remains failed.
- Commissioning cannot reopen dispatch, clean settlement, or COMPLETE.
- Existing membership and attribution are not erased by external actor loss.

**CE-U** for a completed operational successor-episode contract. The inherited conditional invariant remains: if independently established W continues, a fresh cancellation episode does not itself establish new work or a new representative. No automatic renewal or replacement follows.

**CHP-A — independently authoritative evidence may reconstruct historical commissioning for audit only.**

This permits proof of an actual past act. It does not permit inventing a past act, resolving conflicting claims by convenience, or converting historical attribution into fresh operational authority.

Minimum semantic evidence would retain:

- Exact W, L, and A.
- A’s jurisdiction and bounded role.
- Successful disposition, or rejection/uncertainty/conflict as applicable.
- Relevant loss, terminal, and historical status.

Evidence must remain authenticatable whenever authorized Registry provenance, receipt attribution, OA, or same-work successor analysis relies on it. Historical audit requires sufficient independent evidence to prove the past relation. No indefinite storage mechanism or complete retention contract is selected.

Genuinely new work requires a new work context and new commissioning relation. Neither the same actor nor the same raw Registry string inherits the old commission automatically.
