Accepted RA-A-CFW now supplies the root antecedent **prospectively**, when an actual exact admission fact is established. Its LR-B representative role controls; WP does not import the original WP-U’s broader owner definition to give L admission or termination powers.

**D. WP TIMING ORACLE**

This table concerns WP-conforming attachment. “Before” means before the binding fact is established, not before notification is received.

`FORBIDDEN-BEFORE` permits the expressly selected joint first-retention/binding transition. `REQUIRED-BEFORE` requires a preceding established fact.

| Event | Classification | Exact ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Registry object creation | MAY-PRECEDE | Object existence creates neither W nor binding. |
| 2. Selector validation | MAY-PRECEDE | Structural validation does not authenticate work. |
| 3. Association allocation | MAY-PRECEDE | Internal inert candidate only. |
| 4. Registry insertion / first retention | FORBIDDEN-BEFORE | Authoritative first retention and binding occur together. |
| 5. InvocationRecord construction | MAY-PRECEDE | Cancellation-local structure only. |
| 6. Empty EpisodeLedger allocation | MAY-PRECEDE | No qualified membership or source responsibility. |
| 7. Usable Association publication | REQUIRED-BEFORE | Includes capability, receipt, source same-work and downstream use. |
| 8. Source attachment/use relying on same-work identity | REQUIRED-BEFORE | SRC-WP-PRE-USE. |
| 9. Receipt qualification | REQUIRED-BEFORE | WP-RQ-PRE. |
| 10. Participating receipt retention | REQUIRED-BEFORE | Earlier adapter retention cannot escape the cut. |
| 11. Selected/subsumed classification | REQUIRED-BEFORE | Existing receipt ordering remains unchanged. |
| 12. Action claim | REQUIRED-BEFORE | Inherited path follows qualified membership; no new claim authority. |
| 13. Dispatch | REQUIRED-BEFORE | Same ordering; existing runner restrictions remain. |
| 14. Action accounting | REQUIRED-BEFORE | Derived ordering, not a new reauthentication gate. |
| 15. Invocation FAILED | INDEPENDENT | Failure cannot wait for provenance or erase it. Failed candidates cannot become usable bindings. |
| 16. Settlement | INDEPENDENT | No added settlement predicate; conforming retained A already has binding. |
| 17. Successor episode | REQUIRED-BEFORE | Original binding persists; no second binding transition. |
| 18. OA consumption of positive provenance | REQUIRED-BEFORE | Provides the premise only, not observer admission. |
| 19. Historical audit/recovery observation | INDEPENDENT | May establish absence/uncertainty; positive attribution needs proof of the original binding. |

Pre-W and pre-WP are different boundaries. These structural allowances do **not** extend RA-A-CFW’s NC ceiling.

For this selected operational reservation model, valid root provenance precedes the reservation attempt. The actual constructors’ implementation authentication and context checks are not declared NC merely because their outputs are structural. A Registry may independently pre-exist W; its existence supplies no work authority.

**E. PRE / ATOMIC / POST COMPARISON**

| Burden | WP-PRE | WP-ATOMIC | WP-POST-B |
|---|---|---|---|
| Permanent first retention | Root-before-reservation alone does not specify when winner binding becomes authoritative. | First retained A is bound in the same semantic commit. | Requires permanently retained unbound state. |
| Failed binding / poison | Needs an additional winner/failure rule. | Definite noncommit leaves no new retained A; committed A remains bound. | Failed retained A must remain unusable; replacement would violate first retention. |
| Concurrent same-selector/different-W | Must compare the actual incumbent; candidate construction is insufficient. | One exact pair wins; mismatch conflicts. | Must fix intended provenance before retention and prevent a competing bind. |
| Same-selector/same-W | Can reuse only after exact incumbent comparison. | Observe incumbent; no second commit. | Pending and established cases require different treatment. |
| Losing candidate | Prebound authoritative loser would violate no-ghost-binding. | Proposal only; never authoritative. | Must likewise remain inert. |
| Uncertainty | Requires precise retained/bound disposition. | Observe original joint disposition; fail closed. | Must distinguish reservation uncertainty from binding uncertainty. |
| Structural authority separation | Preserved if root evidence is only an input. | Preserved; no root admission occurs in WP commit. | Preserved, with an additional recording phase. |
| Root authority separation | Root already admitted W/L. | Root already admitted W/L. | Root and intended relation must already be fixed. |
| No-retarget | Needs immutable winner relation. | Integral to the retained fact. | Requires fixed intent plus permanent refusal of other W/L. |
| Receipt non-retroactivity | Needs binding before usable publication. | Follows from joint retention/binding and publication gating. | Requires all receipt paths closed until binding. |
| Source-use ordering | Separate ceiling required. | Separate ceiling retained. | Separate ceiling plus pending-state exclusion required. |
| Evidence complexity | Root ordering plus exact binding event still needed. | One WP fact; notification is observation. | At least retention, fixed intended relation, binding and unusable failure dispositions. |
| Current-source compatibility | Existing constructor has no provenance. | Bounded immutable-state and reservation/publication changes required. | Bounded changes plus retained-unbound lifecycle required. |

**WP-PRE — COLLAPSES-INTO-SELECTED-MODEL** for the complete form that satisfies this task’s no-ghost-binding rule: candidate provenance can be fixed beforehand, but it becomes authoritative for the exact Association only when that Association wins first retention. That is the selected joint semantic event. Root-before-reservation by itself is incomplete.

This does not require atomic root admission and Registry reservation. Root admission remains earlier and separate.

**WP-POST-B — VIABLE-BUT-NONSELECTED**, provided its full extra disposition is defined:

- Root provenance and intended same-work relation fixed before structural retention.
- No usable publication before binding.
- No competing caller may choose another W.
- Definite binding failure leaves the retained selector permanently unusable.
- Uncertainty permits observation only.
- No replacement, deletion, rebind or receipt repair.

That model can be safe by sacrificing the selector, but adds a retained-unbound state and a separate irreversible failure boundary. The source establishes no requirement for that intermediate state. POST’s safety is not disproved; its additional semantics are unnecessary here.

**F. SELECTED WP MODEL**

```text
WP-ATOMIC —
FIRST ASSOCIATION RETENTION AND W/L/ROOT PROVENANCE BINDING
ARE ONE ATOMIC SEMANTIC TRANSITION.
```

The positive binding means only:

> This exact retained Association belongs to exact W, represented by exact L under the accepted root-admission provenance.

It is an authoritative identity assertion. It is not ownership transfer, observer admission, effect authority or new-work admission.

The selection has one WP commit boundary. Internal preparation may comprise several implementation operations, but no externally usable or authoritative retained-unbound Association is an allowed intermediate state.

**G. INERT ASSOCIATION / INVOCATION / LEDGER SEMANTICS**

Selections:

```text
IAS-YES
INV-PRE-OK
LEDGER-ALLOC-PRE
```

**IAS-YES:** an internal candidate may have Registry/selector/Invocation relations and proposed provenance inputs. Before winning retention it asserts no authoritative enclosing-W relation, qualifies no receipts, supports no source same-work reliance, exports no OA premise and establishes no action/effect provenance.

Under WP-ATOMIC, that candidate **may not become permanently first-retained while unbound**.

The [Association constructor](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:386) currently receives Registry, selector and Invocation. It derives Ledger, executor, entry and preparation references. It receives no L, W or root evidence and performs no source attachment or receipt qualification.

Its sealed structure supports prospective immutable provenance construction; it does not authorize a later mutable ownership setter.

**INV-PRE-OK:** the [Invocation constructor](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:338) creates a native generator and Ledger without entering the generator. Its ownership is cancellation-invocation-local. It cannot serve as W evidence.

**LEDGER-ALLOC-PRE:** the [Ledger constructor](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:712) creates an empty initial Episode with no receipt or claim; `prepared` is false. Empty structure is not receipt participation.

These are pre-binding allowances within the selected root ordering, not permission to run consequential reservation helpers before root admission.

**H. BINDING AUTHORITY / TRANSITION**

Authority decomposition:

| Authority | Role |
|---|---|
| Registry structural authority | Existing selector validation, candidate construction, first retention and structural duplicate handling |
| Root provenance authority | Established exact W, L, profile/scope and attributable ROOT-1 admission |
| WP binding | Consumption of both authorities to establish the exact retained Association relation; no new binder actor |

Registry authority cannot manufacture W. Possession of root evidence cannot authorize arbitrary Registry mutation. Naming L does not appoint L as Registry owner.

Selections:

```text
L-AUTH-N
ROOT-LIVE-N
```

L need not perform or separately acknowledge binding. The root actor need not remain live. Authentic evidence of the established admission is sufficient for this provenance purpose; it does not prove either actor’s current availability.

Non-normative transition name:

```text
RESERVE_BOUND_ASSOCIATION(R, X, candidate, W, L, root_admission)
```

**Preconditions**

1. Accepted RA-A-CFW admission is established for exact immutable W/L, profile and scope.
2. The operation has existing structural authority over exact Registry R.
3. X satisfies the existing selector contract.
4. The candidate’s exact Invocation/Ledger/Registry relationships are canonical.
5. No receipt, source same-work use, workload export or operational entry has used that candidate.
6. No incompatible incumbent or unresolved original reservation disposition permits new reliance.
7. Applicable independent lifecycle restrictions remain satisfied.

**Success**

One semantic event establishes:

```text
R[X] is exact A
AND
A → exact W → exact L → exact accepted root-admission fact
```

The authoritative binding applies only to the retained winner.

**Minimum immutable evidence**

Exact Registry; exact Association; retained selector; fixed Invocation graph; exact W and scope/profile; exact L and representative role; attributable root/admission evidence; established binding disposition; incumbent/duplicate/conflict disposition; and ordering sufficient to establish binding before usable publication and receipt.

This specifies semantic facts, not fields, serialization or storage.

**Duplicate:** exact incumbent provenance is observed/reused without a second transition.

**Conflict:** reject the contender without changing the incumbent.

**Uncertainty:** fail closed and observe the original disposition.

No result, request string, source owner, object class or historical resemblance substitutes for these facts.

**I. FIRST-RETENTION / CONCURRENCY**

For concurrent attempts:

```text
R, X, W1/L1/root1
R, X, W2/L2/root2
```

Exactly one retained Association and its immutable provenance relation may win. The other attempt receives conflict when the relations differ. No mixed result such as A1 with W2 provenance is permissible.

The implementation may choose the winner; architecture requires consistency through supported reentry/interruption and any subsequently supported concurrency. The current main-thread implementation’s `setdefault` behavior is not proof of a general multithreaded mechanism.

A losing candidate:

- Receives no authoritative WP binding.
- Cannot qualify receipts or support source same-work use.
- Cannot be published as the bound Association or exported to OA.
- Cannot become an alternate Association for X.
- May be discarded only under existing structural disposal rules.

The current [`_graph` check](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:938) already requires the exact Association to be the Registry’s retained mapping. WP preserves that identity requirement.

**Failure disposition**

- **Definitely before commit:** no new retained Association and no binding from this attempt. An unrelated winning incumbent remains unchanged. Inert candidate disposal adds no source/recovery authority.
- **Commit succeeded, response failed:** A remains retained and bound. Notification failure does not undo either fact.
- **Disposition uncertain:** no assumption of absence, replacement or safe replay.
- **Retained but unbound:** prohibited for a conforming new reservation. An observed legacy or defective instance remains unusable for WP attachment; it is not overwritten or repaired through this correction.

Thus the selected model has no unexplained permanent unbound-first state.

**J. DUPLICATE / CONFLICT / CARDINALITY**

```text
DUP-SAME-OBSERVE
ABCard-1
WCard-AM
```

**DUP-SAME-OBSERVE:** reuse requires authoritative equality of the retained A, W, L and root-admission relation. Equal input strings alone are insufficient. Another evidence copy may prove the same admission fact; it does not constitute a second chain or commission.

| Presented case | Disposition |
|---|---|
| Same A / same W/L/root | Observe/reuse; no second binding |
| Same selector / different W | Conflict; incumbent unchanged |
| Same W / different L | Conflict under LCard-1/LREP-N |
| Same W / conflicting authoritative root facts | Suspend disputed provenance reliance; preserve evidence |
| Equal strings / different Registries | Separate contexts; no inferred W equality |
| Old selector / genuinely new W | Conflict if it still retains old A |
| Attempted first binding after receipts or FAILED | Reject; no retrospective adoption |
| Unsupported claimant contradicts proved incumbent | Reject claimant; do not invalidate incumbent merely for appearing |

**ABCard-1:** every successfully retained WP-conforming Association has exactly one immutable W/L/root binding for its retained lifetime. Internal losing candidates have none. Failure, settlement, terminality and L loss do not make a bound A unbound.

**WCard-AM:** WP does not require an inverse one-to-one mapping. Multiple separately legitimate Associations may reference one W. This creates no permission for duplicate source ownership, multiple action delivery or additional observers; those contracts remain separate.

**Different W / same L:** LCard-1 is a per-W rule, not by itself a universal inverse-cardinality theorem. The accepted root review requires independent admission and profile eligibility for every proposed relation. Official instance reuse is constrained by its lifecycle contract; preparation’s exact outer-invocation identity cannot simply be recycled. WP adds no reusable-L permission and never infers same W from actor identity or class.

**Registry selector rule**

X remains a Registry-local cancellation-capability selector. It may be associated with W through exact R/A provenance. It neither identifies W globally nor derives W. Matching X cannot transfer provenance to new work.

**K. BINDING UNCERTAINTY / OBSERVATION**

State meanings are semantic; PB4 describes knowledge of disposition, and PB5 describes a rejected/conflicting attempt rather than overwriting the incumbent.

| State | Usable publication | Receipt qualification | Source same-work reliance | Duplicate attempt | Another W claim | Retry | OA provenance export |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PB0: no retained A | No | No | No | Fresh authorized reservation may begin | May independently compete before commitment | No implicit replay | No |
| PB1: internal unbound candidate | No | No | No | Contender remains subject to first-retention arbitration | Cannot rewrite this candidate’s fixed proposal | No implicit replay | No |
| PB2: retained-unbound | Prohibited state | No WP-authorized activation | No | Observation/rejection only | No | No replacement or repair | No |
| PB3: binding established | Eligible under existing contracts | Existing receipt rules | Provenance premise only | Exact same relation may be observed | No | No second bind | Exact bounded export |
| PB4: original commit uncertain | No | No new path may be activated | No | Observe original disposition only | No | No | No positive export |
| PB5: conflict | No for contender | No through contender | No through contender | Incumbent’s independent rights remain | No | No overwrite | No disputed export |
| PBH: historical binding | Historical exposure only; no fresh capability grant | Existing residual source rules only | Attribution of existing responsibility only | Historical observation, no rebind | No | No | Historical premise only |

PBH does not decide source closure. If W terminality precedes independently lawful source discharge, WP cannot use that terminality to drop an otherwise eligible receipt. Conversely, a permanently closed capability is not revived.

For original binding uncertainty:

```text
BIND-UNCERTAIN
→ no usable publication
→ no receipt-path activation
→ no source same-work reliance
→ no OA export
→ no competing W/L binding
→ no destructive replay
```

Only independently authorized observation of the original act may establish:

```text
ESTABLISHED
NOT-ESTABLISHED
CONFLICT
STILL-UNCERTAIN
```

Observation cannot choose W, change L, replace A, replay receipts or settle episodes.

Proved noncommitment is not an automatic retry instruction. Any subsequent reservation must independently satisfy existing authority and the original rejection/failure constraints.

Later loss of an evidence copy does not undo a previously established binding. It closes unsupported positive provenance claims; it cannot retroactively invalidate receipts, erase obligations or introduce a discretionary receipt filter.

**L. PUBLICATION BOUNDARY**

Usable publication includes:

- Returning A as cancellation-capability structure.
- Supplying A to an operational receipt/Ledger path.
- Supplying A to a source path for same-work reliance.
- Supplying A to an OA/downstream provenance consumer.

Internal candidate allocation and linking may precede binding. **Authoritative Registry first retention may not precede binding; the two are the joint transition.**

A physical implementation may prepare private storage before commitment, but that storage cannot already count as a separately completed retained mapping visible to competing canonical operations.

Diagnostic observation remains distinct. Current `_reserve` returns an inspection. That does not permit a future operation to expose usable unbound capability state through another alias.

No receipt or source attachment occurs in the inspected reservation/construction call chain. Receipt requires the separate prepared-Ledger path; current production source installation remains unavailable. Nevertheless, a return-only guard would be insufficient if internal aliases could be used earlier. The selected commit governs every usable path, including reentry before return.

**M. RECEIPT HARD CUT**

```text
WP-RQ-PRE
```

**No qualified or participating receipt may arise through a WP-conforming Association before its exact WP binding is established. A receipt cannot establish, select or repair that provenance.**

Afterward:

- Receipt and episode classification retain their existing indivisible ordering.
- Selected, subsumed and repeated receipts cannot change W/L/root.
- Participating adapter retention obeys the same cut.
- Dequeue/continuation preserves earlier membership.
- Successor receipts do not rebind A.
- FAILED does not erase attribution or retained membership.

This is an **earlier construction/publication ordering requirement**, not a new discretionary acceptance decision at ingress. A future implementation must establish WP before exposing a supported receipt route; it may not queue participating requests unclassified while waiting for WP.

The [adopted receipt rules](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/governance/rq003-stage3c-sole-reaper-cancellation-receipt-settlement-clarification-candidate.md:118) remain authoritative. Historical unattached-component receipts are not retroactively invalidated. They also cannot be adopted into W by a newly invented binding. An observed ordering violation remains a violation, with its actual obligations preserved.

**N. SOURCE CEILING**

```text
SRC-WP-PRE-USE
```

Any future source attachment/use relying on Association A as identifying the same enclosing work must observe an already-established immutable A→W/L/root binding.

WP does not independently require every inert source object allocation to follow binding. Nor does it declare source attachment fully independent.

This correction selects no source actor, startup sequence, coverage interval, F2 composition, physical installation, finalization or restoration mechanism. It changes none of S/H/D’s owning relations. D remains the native root/control/evidence cell; it is not the action dispatcher.

**O. FAILED / GATE-13**

Invocation FAILED:

- Preserves established A→W/L/root history.
- Does not permit W2, L2, a new binding or replacement.
- Does not revive entry, action claim, dispatch, clean settlement or COMPLETE.
- Does not erase qualified selected/subsumed or participating receipts.
- Does not detach source responsibility or imply restoration.

Gate-13 remains intact: otherwise eligible pre-cut receipt after FAILED remains receipt under the existing source/Ledger contract.

A first-binding attempt after FAILED is not permitted by WP-ATOMIC. Observation of an already-established historical binding is not a new binding transition.

**P. SETTLEMENT / SUCCESSOR EPISODE**

```text
WP-SETTLE-N
```

WP introduces **no cancellation-side settlement prerequisite**. No live root, live L, new provenance acknowledgement or evidence-copy availability check is added to settlement.

Binding evidence has its own attribution lifetime. Settlement does not erase it.

Successor continuity is supported directly by [`_Ledger._settle`](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:874): it creates the next Episode using the existing Association authority and changes the Ledger’s current Episode. It does not replace the Association or Invocation.

Therefore, while W remains the same active work:

```text
same A / W / L / root binding
→ lawful successor Episode
→ same immutable binding
```

No repeated WP transition occurs. Episode-specific receipt/action rules remain unchanged. A successor Episode does not prove W remains active, terminate W, or authorize continuation after W terminality.

**Q. W TERMINALITY / NEW WORK**

At W terminality, binding becomes historical; A never becomes unbound.

L loss likewise preserves history. Registry does not become L, and neither an observer nor a recovery actor inherits representation.

For new W2:

```text
new accepted root admission for W2
+
separately legitimate distinct Registry/Association relation
```

Old A1 cannot become W2. If R[X] permanently retains A1 for W1, X cannot mean W2 in that Registry, even after settlement, failure or terminality.

Another unused selector or Registry context may provide a structurally distinct path if independently permitted. WP chooses neither and grants no creation bypass. Renaming the same failed or uncertain work is not legitimate new work.

Registry/Association objects may remain structurally present after L loss or W terminality. Presence supplies no healthy-reuse inference.

**S. OA / DOWNSTREAM EXPORT**

The exact positive export is:

No separate authoritative cleanup is required for these conforming inert candidates.

The generator body does not execute at creation. CPython 3.14.5’s `gen_close` handles `FRAME_CREATED` by marking completion and clearing the frame without entering its body; deallocation uses that close path. Thus pre-entry destruction does not execute the `_invoke` action path. [CPython source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.5/Objects/genobject.c).

The inspected `_invoke` also contains no source installation or resource acquisition and no cleanup `finally`. Constructor checks and local failure bookkeeping do not establish workload participation.

## I. BINDING AUTHORITY-COMPOSITION REVIEW

**AC-A. Binding authority composition is complete.**

The decisive distinction is between **establishing the provenance of Registry-owned structure** and **authorizing effects upon W**.

1. Registry authority has jurisdiction over the exact R/X reservation and retained Association.
2. Accepted root provenance establishes W’s actual admitted identity, scope, profile and commissioned L.
3. WP-C §H makes their joint consumption the prospective authority-creating act for A’s attribution.
4. The act creates neither observer duties nor workload cancellation effects.

Registry authority alone could select structure but could not establish a legitimate W/L antecedent. Root evidence alone could establish that antecedent but could not authorize mutation or retention in R. The authorized reservation with both inputs establishes the missing relation.

The original accepted interface already separates reservation from effect permissions: reserve/prepare grants no receipt, membership, action, cut or restoration authority. [Preserved interface contract](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-u1-u2-rr1-pass-comprehensive-continuation.md:9444).

**Unrelated Registry R2:** an authorized R2 reservation explicitly consuming W1/L1/root1 may establish a new R2 Association attributed to W1. R2’s prior use does not itself prohibit that relation. This follows from the selected binding transition and WCard-AM, not an inferred private intention.

It does not assert that R2 previously belonged to W1, that its other Associations belong to W1, or that R2 may affect W1. An incompatible retained Y conflicts. Unauthenticated structural access fails §H’s authority prerequisite.

No third work-side permission is necessary for this provenance-only act. Such a permission would become necessary if attachment itself imposed workload-side cancellation obligations; the authored package expressly does not do that.

The official source retains the same receiver across [pre-allocation and allocated execution](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/orchestrator.py:847). The accepted correction additionally requires inert allocation followed by same-object initialization. **An initialization-pending object cannot use OA to bypass the accepted operational guard.**

The preparation correction expressly retains the outer instance through detached work and assessment. The [current outer entry](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/evidence_preparation.py:736) authenticates returned evidence and produces the assessment; child output does not replace that role.

Neither current source path already provides the OA observation interface. That is bounded future conformance work.

A blocked or waiting outer actor is not automatically lost. However, retention alone does not prove an observation occurred. If the outer actor actually stops or becomes unavailable while a detached child continues, OA supplies no child substitution: observer operation ends and cancellation observation may be stranded.

This is compatible with accepted LREP-N’s explicit availability sacrifice. OA does not require extending L artificially beyond its accepted lifetime.

## G. OBSERVER ADMISSION TRANSITION

Non-normative semantic name:

```text
ADMIT_L_OBSERVER(A, W, L, wp_provenance)
```

This describes semantics, not an implementation API.

**Preconditions**

- Exact accepted WP binding is established for canonical A and immutable W/L/root provenance.
- O is that exact L.
- The activation is attributable to L under the bounded rule in E.
- L is live and observer-eligible; historical commission alone is insufficient.
- Required profile initialization and observation-context prerequisites hold.
- W remains within its independently established active lifetime.
- No established different observer, unresolved original admission, or authoritative contradiction permits competing reliance.
- No previous established loss/end of this observer lifetime is being bypassed.
- Timing rules J–M hold.

**Success**

One atomic semantic fact establishes the exact A/W/O observer admission. Admission and its authority-bearing disposition are one fact; notification is not a second grant.

**Definite failure before commitment**

No new admission exists. Existing membership and any independently established incumbent remain unchanged. No automatic retry follows.

**Duplicate**

**OA-DUP-OBSERVE:** exact same A, W, O and authority basis may observe/reuse the established admission. There is no second OA commit, renewed lifetime or replacement.

**Conflict**

A different O or incompatible basis is rejected without mutating the incumbent. Genuine authoritative contradiction closes disputed reliance.

**Uncertainty**

The original disposition remains unproved. No active observer authority, competing admission or assumed replay follows.

**Loss**

Admission history remains; active authority ends under I. No effect power exists at any stage.

## H. OBSERVER STATE MACHINE

These states distinguish actual admission history from knowledge about it. A rejected contender does not overwrite an incumbent’s state.

| State | Active observation? | Duplicate/history read? | Different O admitted? | Positive operational MI premise? | Successor use? | Retry? | Audit? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **OA0 — no admission established, noncommitment known** | No | No positive admission to reuse | No; selected identity must be exact L | No | Only after first valid admission | Fresh authorized attempt may satisfy G; never automatic | Yes, under separate authority |
| **OA1 — admission established; O currently eligible** | Yes, under O–P | Same exact admission may be observed/reused | No | Only an established qualifying actual observation under S | Yes, conditionally | No second admission | Yes |
| **OA2 / OA-LOST — established observer lifetime ended through loss/unavailability/ineligibility** | No | Historical admission only | No | No new positive premise | No | No reactivation or replacement in V1 | Yes |
| **OA3 — original admission disposition uncertain** | No | Original-disposition evidence only | No | No | No | No assumed retry | Yes |
| **OA4 — conflict** | No for contender or disputed relation | Preserve evidence; independently proved incumbent remains governed by its own state | No | None from disputed claim | None from disputed claim | No overwrite or winner selection | Yes |
| **OAH — W terminal; admission historical** | No | Historical only | No | No | No | No operational retry | Yes |
| **OAS — admission established, current eligibility unproved** | No | Admission history remains observable | No | No new positive premise | No while suspended | Eligibility evidence may clarify continuity; no new admission | Yes |

OAS is distinct from OA3. It means admission is known but present eligibility cannot be established.

Clarifying OAS may restore reliance on **the continuously valid same admission** if evidence establishes that no loss or lifetime end occurred. It cannot reverse established OA2 loss.

Principal transitions:

```text
OA0 → OA1       successful admission
OA0 → OA3       admission attempted; disposition uncertain
OA3 → OA0       original noncommitment established
OA3 → OA1       original commitment and current eligibility established
OA3 → OA2/OAH  commitment established, but observer lost/W terminal
OA1 → OAS      present eligibility cannot be proved
OA1/OAS → OA2 established observer loss/lifetime end
any → OAH      independently established W terminality
```

An unsupported O2 claim is rejected without demoting a proved OA1 incumbent. A genuine contradiction between authoritative facts suspends the disputed relation; it is not resolved by arrival order.

## I. CARDINALITY / REPLACEMENT / LOSS

Selections:

```text
OCard-1
OREP-N
OA-LOST
```

**OCard-1:** at most one active observer per exact A; a successful admission identifies exactly one O. An Association is not required to have an active observer at all times.

Because O=L and LCard-1/LREP-N are frozen, no alternative observer identity is available for that A/W. OA nevertheless requires its own admission; L commission alone is insufficient.

Multiple physical observations by O do not create multiple observers.

**OREP-N:** no replacement, succession or reactivation after an established end of the observer lifetime in V1. A historically admitted O returning after established loss cannot renew its authority by repeating admission.

This deliberately sacrifices availability. Ordinary waiting or temporary inability to complete a read is not, by itself, proof that the actor’s lifetime ended; uncertainty uses OAS.

On established loss:

- Historical admission remains true.
- Source/Ledger membership remains governed by its existing authorities.
- No subsequent observation is inferred.
- OA supplies no new positive operational MI premise.
- No child, result owner, recovery actor or Registry inherits observation authority.
- No effect authority migrates.
- No receipt is erased.
- No settlement or W-terminal disposition follows.

No source graph, root, pin or owner is added to keep O alive.

## J. TIMING / LATE ADMISSION

**OT-B.**

OA is an observation prerequisite, **not a receipt-ingress prerequisite**.

| Boundary | OA rule |
|---|---|
| WP binding | Must precede positive OA admission |
| Source attachment | Independent source authority and SRC-WP-PRE-USE govern; OA adds no attachment prerequisite |
| First qualified receipt | May precede OA |
| Participating retention | May precede OA; original membership time remains authoritative |
| First active observation | Requires established OA and current eligibility |
| Invocation FAILED | OAF-A applies |
| Settlement | Settled membership cannot support a new operational observation |
| Lawful successor | OBS-EP-WIDE applies |
| W terminality | Operational OA authority ends |

The valid late-observation sequence is:

```text
WP established
→ receipt qualifies and membership is retained
→ no observer yet
→ exact L is admitted as O
→ membership is still MEM-CURRENT
→ O actually observes that current state
```

That first observation is valid. It does not alter receipt time, claim an earlier observation, retroactively qualify anything, or create intent for elapsed historical state.

OT-A is unnecessary and would introduce an unjustified receipt/source ordering burden. OT-C unnecessarily prevents advance observer admission while an episode is empty.

OA does not guarantee that every membership will be observed before lawful settlement. It adds no mandatory observation duty, scheduling guarantee or settlement hold. Those cannot be silently supplied at an admission gate.

## K. CURRENT vs HISTORICAL MEMBERSHIP

**MEM-CURRENT:** authoritative qualified/retained membership in the Ledger’s current unresolved episode under existing episode governance, eligible for observation and later MI interpretation.

**MEM-HIST:** established membership that is historical under that governance, including membership of an episode closed by lawful settlement/advancement. It cannot generate a new operational OA premise.

“Current” does not mean “requires workload cancellation.” That remains MI’s question.

The [Ledger receipt and settlement paths](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:822) preserve membership in the current episode and replace the current episode at lawful settlement. OA consumes those authoritative facts.

Important limits:

- Claim, action entry and coherent accounting do not themselves remove current membership.
- FAILED does not itself make retained membership merely historical.
- Queue absence does not establish absence of retained membership.
- A surviving old Episode object is not proof that its membership remains current.
- Current source/Ledger retention supports late observation only while actually available and current.
- No permanent archive of every episode is assumed.
- Missing or contradictory currentness evidence closes operational observation; O cannot classify by guesswork.

W terminality independently closes OA authority even if residual source/Ledger obligations remain unresolved. OA does not relabel or erase those obligations.

## L. FAILED / GATE-13

**OAF-A.**

After Invocation FAILED, the same exact live/eligible L may receive OA admission solely to observe retained consequential MEM-CURRENT membership preserved by the existing contract.

The authority comes from the independent accepted A/W/L provenance plus the prospective OA rule. It does **not** come from FAILED or from permission to restart the failed executor.

This admission:

- Creates no new W or Association.
- Does not invoke preparation, operational entry or a dispatcher transition through the failed capability.
- Does not reset a claim.
- Does not replay action.
- Does not authorize restoration resumption or detachment.
- Does not permit clean settlement or COMPLETE.

The [accepted Gate-13 contract](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/project-checkpoints/ore-v3-stage3c-post-u1-u2-rr1-pass-comprehensive-continuation.md:9513) preserves otherwise eligible pre-cut receipt after FAILED. Its current membership is consequential, not merely diagnostic history.

| FAILED schedule | OA observation ceiling |
|---|---|
| Failure before claim | Observe retained current membership with unclaimed/FAILED context; no alternate runner |
| Claim consumed before entry | Preserve consumed claim and absent/unproved entry; no replay |
| Entry before accounting failure | Preserve actual entry and accounting uncertainty |
| Earlier coherent accounting | Preserve accounting as local fact; FAILED exclusions still apply |
| Later eligible pre-cut receipt | Observe selected/subsumed current membership when established |
| Participating retention before dequeue | Observe original retained membership; dequeue is not fresh ingress |

The observation context must preserve **FAILED, consumed claim where applicable, dispatch exclusion, settlement exclusion and retained receipt consequence**.

FAILED is not proof that L is lost, nor is live L proof that the cancellation executor remains usable.

A new post-FAILED admission relies on actual consequential current membership. FAILED alone, or an empty episode alone, supplies no positive cancellation-observation premise.

## M. SETTLEMENT / SUCCESSOR EPISODES

Selections:

```text
OA-SETTLE-N
OBS-EP-WIDE
```

**OA-SETTLE-N:** lawful settlement ends operational OA observation of that episode’s settled membership. Admission history remains.

OA adds no settlement prerequisite requiring:

- An admitted observer.
- A completed observation.
- Observer acknowledgement.
- Live L.
- A retained OA evidence copy.

It cannot delay otherwise lawful settlement merely to create an observation opportunity.

An observation ordered before settlement proves what O actually observed then. It does not establish a workload duty surviving settlement. A later read of that settled membership is historical only.

**OBS-EP-WIDE:** one A/W observer admission spans lawful successor episodes while the same O remains live/eligible and W remains active.

Each observation must independently bind the exact episode and current state. Admission persistence proves neither W activity nor successor lawfulness.

If admission first occurs after an episode settled, it is admission for still-active A/W under an independently lawful subsequent context—not operational admission to the settled episode. Old membership is never reactivated.

An empty lawful successor may coexist with an eligible observer, but supplies no positive cancellation membership until receipt establishes it.

## N. W TERMINALITY / MULTIPLE ASSOCIATIONS

W terminality is consumed from accepted profile authority. OA does not establish it.

At established W terminality:

- Active observer authority ends.
- Admission becomes historical: OAH.
- No new operational observation or positive operational MI export is available.
- No replacement, succession or reuse follows.
- Separately authorized audit may inspect historical evidence.
- Residual receipt, source, restoration and reaper obligations are not erased.

Invocation FAILED, child exit, result existence, source closure and Ledger settlement are not substituted for W terminality.

**OA-MA-YES.**

The same exact O=L may hold separate OA admissions for A1 and A2 belonging to the same W, if each independently satisfies the contract.

However:

- A1 admission does not authorize observation of A2.
- Each admission binds exact A and its own WP provenance.
- Each observation binds exact A/Episode/membership.
- WCard-AM grants no cross-Association receipt aggregation, intent deduplication or effect permission.
- Actor equality does not establish W equality.

## O. OBSERVATION SURFACE / CONSISTENCY

O receives semantic access to an **authoritative read-only membership observation surface for exact A**.

Observer authority alone cannot:

- Qualify or create a receipt.
- Alter selected/subsumed classification.
- Mutate or erase membership.
- Claim or run action.
- Publish action accounting.
- Settle or advance an episode.
- Mutate source authority.
- Publish an effect or result.

Existing diagnostic views are not automatically authoritative OA interfaces. A future mechanism must establish authentic attribution, coherent state and legitimate access. Merely renaming `_inspect` or copying a diagnostic object does not meet that requirement.

**OBS-SNAPSHOT.**

Each authoritative observation binds to one exact authoritative membership/episode state at one logical observation point. The same point must support the required OA eligibility and lifetime predicates and relevant inherited context.

This requires:

- No half-transition membership state.
- No mixture of Episode N membership with Episode N+1 identity.
- An ordering consistent with completed receipt/settlement transitions.
- No hidden assumption that an earlier eligibility check remains valid through a later read.
- Failure to obtain a coherent point produces no authoritative active observation.

Locks, timestamps, process/thread primitives and storage formats are deferred. OBS-SNAPSHOT does not require blocking settlement or retaining a new source lifetime.

## P. OBSERVATION FACT / ACTIVE-HISTORICAL DISTINCTION

**Admission is not observation. Membership is not observation.**

An authoritative observation fact binds:

| Field of meaning | Required content |
|---|---|
| Work attribution | Exact A, W and accepted WP provenance |
| Observer attribution | Exact O=L and exact OA admission |
| Episode | Exact episode/context identity, not a bare ordinal detached from A |
| Membership | Exact authoritative selected/subsumed/participating state observed |
| Currentness | MEM-CURRENT or MEM-HIST |
| Observer eligibility | Established at the logical observation point |
| Invocation context | Relevant status, including FAILED and claim/accounting restrictions |
| Ordering | Sufficient relation to receipt, settlement, episode transition and applicable lifetime boundary |
| Observation disposition | Established, not established or uncertain |
| Operational classification | OBS-ACTIVE or OBS-HISTORICAL |

**OBS-ACTIVE:** an established observation made while O was active/eligible, W was within its active lifetime, and membership was MEM-CURRENT.

**OBS-HISTORICAL:** a separately authorized inspection of evidence whose operational conditions no longer hold. It supplies historical attribution, not a new operational MI premise.

An established earlier OBS-ACTIVE event remains true history after settlement or observer loss. That does not make its cached contents current or authorize a new operational export after closure.

An empty authoritative view may establish absence of current membership at its observation point. It is not a positive cancellation-membership observation.

One admission may authorize multiple non-consuming observations. No fresh admission is required per receipt or read. Repeated observations do not create independent cancellation events or effect attempts.

For repeated/subsumed receipts, O observes the existing aggregate membership classification. It cannot unpack subsumption into new independent requests.

For dequeue/continuation, O observes authoritative retained membership, not transient queue presence. Continuation cannot manufacture freshness or erase retained membership.

An observation fact is a semantic fact requiring sufficient evidence for reliance. OA does not prescribe a separately allocated durable artifact for every read.

## Q. ADMISSION / OBSERVATION UNCERTAINTY

**Admission uncertainty — OA3**

O is not assumed admitted. No authoritative operational observation may be generated under the uncertain admission; MI receives no positive premise.

No second O, destructive replay or automatic retry is permitted.

Independently authorized observation of the original disposition may establish:

```text
ESTABLISHED
NOT-ESTABLISHED
CONFLICT
STILL-UNCERTAIN
```

ESTABLISHED still requires current eligibility before operational reliance. NOT-ESTABLISHED does not itself authorize retry.

**Observation uncertainty**

Admission may be established while occurrence or disposition of one particular observation remains uncertain.

Then:

- That observation supplies no positive MI premise.
- Neither intent nor effect is inferred.
- No duplicate observation is invented as historical fact.
- Authorized evidence may clarify what actually occurred.

A later permitted read, while OA1 and all currentness predicates hold, is a new observation of then-current state. It does not prove the earlier read occurred or replay an effect.

**Eligibility uncertainty — OAS**

Historical commission, a retained object or absence of a reported failure is insufficient by itself. Positive reliance needs evidence of the exact actor’s supported live lifecycle and authoritative access at the observation point.

Missing evidence closes reliance without undoing earlier admission, receipts or observations. Established loss cannot be repaired by reconstructing a similar actor.

## R. EVIDENCE LIFETIME

Minimum **admission evidence** establishes exact A/W, accepted WP provenance, exact O, OA authority basis, admission disposition, unique-incumbent/conflict disposition, and applicable active/lost/historical status.

Minimum **observation evidence** establishes exact admitted O and A/W, exact Episode/membership state, active/historical classification, relevant inherited Invocation context, logical ordering, and established/not-established/uncertain observation disposition.

| Boundary | Classification | Required meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **OAE1 Observer admission** | REQUIRED | Exact committed admission and authority basis must be authenticatable |
| **OAE2 First active observation** | REQUIRED | Admission, eligibility, exact state and actual observation occurrence |
| **OAE3 MI consumption** | REQUIRED | Exact observation provenance and context; no substitution of admission for observation |
| **OAE4 Invocation FAILED** | REQUIRED | Preserve applicable admission/observation history and inherited FAILED restrictions |
| **OAE5 Settlement** | REQUIRED | Preserve still-required attribution and ordered transition to historical membership |
| **OAE6 Successor episode** | REQUIRED | Same admission plus independently established current eligibility and exact new episode |
| **OAE7 Observer loss** | REQUIRED | Historical admission and loss boundary sufficient to exclude later active reliance |
| **OAE8 W terminality** | REQUIRED | Historical attribution and cessation of operational OA authority |
| **OAE9 Historical audit/recovery** | REQUIRED | Proof for every authorized historical claim or disposition reconstruction |

“Required” means proof available for authorized reliance and applicable attribution obligations. It does not require keeping L, root, Association or every evidence object alive forever.

Rows do not require fabricating evidence of an event that never occurred. Settlement and FAILED do not become contingent on successfully writing an OA record.

Physical storage, retention implementation and authorized reconstruction mechanisms remain deferred. Missing evidence prevents unsupported claims; it does not authorize rewriting history or erasing obligations.

## S. OA→MI EXPORT

The maximum positive operational export is:

> **Exact admitted observer O, while currently eligible, authoritatively observed exact MEM-CURRENT membership M for exact Association A belonging to exact W, in exact Episode/context E under accepted WP-C provenance.**

Where relevant, it preserves inherited FAILED context.

This proves only:

- Exact legitimate observer.
- Actual observation occurred.
- Exact current membership was observed at its logical observation point.
- Exact same-work provenance.

It does not prove membership→cancellation intent, an effect target, delivery, application, acknowledgement, result or terminality.

The observation is an as-of fact. OA does not silently promise that membership remains current forever. At an operational handoff, known settlement, observer loss/ineligibility, W terminality or other closing context must not be suppressed. A stale cached fact cannot be offered as a new current premise.

OA supplies no positive operational premise when:

- No observer is admitted.
- Observer is lost/ineligible or current eligibility is unproved.
- Admission is uncertain or authoritatively disputed.
- Observation is uncertain.
- Membership is historical.
- Only historical inspection exists.
- W is terminal.

Earlier valid observation history remains true. Any obligation already lawfully created by a future MI contract would require that contract’s own survival/disposition rules; OA creates none.

Under FAILED, the ceiling is:

> Legitimate current observation under FAILED context.

It does not imply an available dispatcher, replay permission, clean settlement or required workload effect.

## C. REVIEW SCOPE / ORIGINAL OA-U CLOSURE

→ legitimate observer admission
```

Accepted RA-A-CFW establishes exact W and commissioned L. Accepted WP-C establishes immutable A→W/L/root provenance. OA-C then expressly adds a separate, attributable observer-admission transition for that exact L.

## D. OA ADMISSION STATE ORACLE

The authored states are sufficient. They distinguish committed facts, present eligibility and uncertainty; they are not interchangeable health labels.

| State | Consequential oracle |
|---|---|
| OA0 | Noncommitment known; no observer authority. A fresh authorized attempt must satisfy all admission preconditions. |
| OA1 | Admission established; current eligibility established. Positive export still requires an actual qualifying observation. |
| OA2 / OA-LOST | Observer lifetime actually ended. Historical admission remains; no reactivation or replacement. |
| OA3 | Original admission disposition uncertain. No operational observation, competing admission or assumed replay. |
| OA4 | Contender/conflict state. Unsupported contenders do not demote a proved incumbent; genuinely disputed authority closes reliance. |
| OAS | Admission established, present eligibility unproved. No active observation pending proof of continuity. |
| OAH | W terminal; operational OA authority ended. Existing admission history remains historical. |

These classifications may coexist with independent Invocation, source and Episode states. That product structure introduces no “maybe active” authority.

Nominal admission creates exactly one admission fact, even with no membership present. It creates no observation fact and no positive MI premise.

Admission before W terminality cannot be inferred from an attempted admission afterward. Likewise, a historical L object cannot satisfy present liveness.

## K. CURRENT vs HISTORICAL MEMBERSHIP REVIEW

The authored distinction is sufficient.

**MEM-CURRENT** means authoritative membership in the Ledger’s current unresolved Episode. It does not mean unclaimed, healthy, unaccounted or requiring another effect.

The [Ledger source](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:822) retains membership through claim and accounting; settlement replaces the current Episode.

Consequently:

- Claim consumption does not make membership historical.
- Accounting does not itself remove membership.
- FAILED does not itself make retained membership historical.
- Dequeue does not erase membership.
- A surviving old Episode object does not establish currentness.
- Source closure, result terminality and observer loss are not invented membership transitions.
- W terminality independently closes OA even if residual membership obligations remain.

OA consumes currentness from the authoritative Ledger context. Missing or contradictory evidence closes observation.

Subsumed repeats retain their existing aggregate meaning. OA does not reconstruct independent physical events or infer additional effects.

The three uncertainty cases are distinct and complete.

It does not prove intent, target, delivery, application, acknowledgement, result or terminality.

OA2

→ immutable admission of a legitimate workload-observation owner
```

## D. MI MODEL COMPARISON

| Burden | MI-C1: deterministic intent | MI-C2: intermediate derived obligation |
|---|---|---|
| Authority source | Accepted OA fact plus explicit MI rule | OA plus creation rule and separate activation authority |
| Another policy decision | None | Required if activation is genuinely independent |
| State needed | Identity, contributors, disposition, uncertainty and history | Those facts plus intermediate activation lifecycle |
| Duplicate observations | Same basis reuses its existing mapping | Requires equivalent deduplication |
| Repeated/subsumed membership | One existing semantic basis | Must preserve the same aggregation |
| FAILED | Can establish intent through independent MI rule | Requires an additional FAILED activation rule |
| Local accounting | Preserved context; neither trigger nor satisfaction | Separate activation model must decide its role |
| Settlement | Committed intent survives independently; no hold | Separate retained obligation can also survive |
| Successor Episodes | New basis joins active W intent | Requires composition across intermediate obligations |
| W terminality | Historical unresolved disposition; no new MI effect authority | Must terminate both activation and active-obligation authority |
| Multiple Associations | One active W intent, exact contributors retained | Requires the same cross-A composition rule |
| Stale observations | Currentness validated at MI commit | Must specify both observation and later activation timing |
| Uncertainty | Original commit/contribution disposition only | Additional uncertainty between derivation and activation |
| AE handoff | One established obligation with exact provenance | Must distinguish intermediate state from actionable intent |
| Governance | No receipt, dispatcher or settlement amendment | Potentially compatible, but adds another semantic boundary |
| Implementation complexity | Bounded semantic state; concurrency remains substantive | Additional state and activation transitions |

**MI-C1 is selected.**

Deduplication and retained identity do not require an independent intent-policy decision. If MI-C2 activates immediately under exactly the same predicates, it reduces to MI-C1. If it genuinely waits for another semantic decision, that additional authority is unnecessary for this gate.

The original MI-U observation that a surviving duty might resemble MI-D remains historically accurate. This task expressly distinguishes models by **independent activation**, not merely by whether state survives.

## E. SELECTED MI MODEL / AUTHORITY BASIS

Selections:

```text
MI-C1
MI-AUTH-D
```

The prospective rule is:

```text
established accepted OBS-ACTIVE observation
+
exact current qualifying context at MI commitment
+
the deterministic identity/composition rules below
→ establish or reuse the one applicable authoritative intent
```

There is no intermediate “observed, awaiting policy approval” state.

No live root, Registry decision, observer discretion, result owner or source owner decides whether the qualifying request deserves intent. The mechanism enforcing MI has no authority to choose another W, discard an inconvenient contributor or choose a cancellation policy.

O provides the accepted observation. O does not receive an independent right to decide “cancel” versus “do not cancel.”

**MI-B is rejected — MISSING-AUTHORITY.** OA grants observation, not discretionary cancellation policy.

**MI-C is rejected — MISSING-AUTHORITY.** Dispatcher claim/accounting cannot substitute for accepted observation or determine workload intent by itself.

This is a new bounded semantic derivation rule. It is not a claim that existing code already implements it.

## F. INTENT SEMANTICS / KIND / SCOPE

The three facts are distinct:

| Fact | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Observation | Exact admitted O actually observed exact current membership under OA |
| Intent | The workload-effect protocol has one authoritative cancellation obligation to resolve for exact W, supported by the retained contributor provenance |
| Effect | A separately authorized AE contract determines delivery, application, acknowledgement and disposition |

**Final semantic definition:**

> Workload-cancellation intent I is an authoritative obligation to consider and resolve the cancellation request for exact W through the separately governed workload-effect protocol. Its established provenance must remain represented until an authoritative protocol disposition or the selected W-terminal historical disposition. Establishing I does not require or prove any particular effect.

“Required” applies to **accounting for and resolving the request under the effect protocol**. “Authorized” permits that protocol to rely on the established intent premise. Neither means “apply an effect regardless of feasibility, uncertainty or other authority.”

No bounded execution latency or guaranteed successful cancellation is added.

**Kind:** the existing semantic request to cancel exact enclosing W. This is not an arbitrary command framework.

**Scope: IS-WE** — one active work-level cancellation scope with exact Association/Episode/membership contributors.

No process, thread, child, signal, exception instance or result object is selected. Local `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit` action profiles remain inherited context; they do not independently create different MI command kinds. Profile-specific effect targeting remains AE work.

## G. INTENT IDENTITY / MEMBERSHIP CARDINALITY

Selections:

```text
IB-ME
MCard-ONE
ICard-W
```

**Intent basis:**

```text
B = (exact A, exact E, exact semantic membership basis M)
```

M is the Ledger-governed retained cancellation obligation selected by the first qualified receipt, including its eligible subsumed and participating membership.

M is not:

- An observation-event identifier.
- A physical-signal count.
- A transient queue entry.
- A bare Episode ordinal detached from A.
- A new MI reclassification of receipts.

Selected/subsumed refinements do not change this semantic basis. If an interface cannot establish the canonical basis, MI cannot invent it.

**MCard-ONE:** one MI basis for that retained semantic obligation. Physical repeats do not create independent bases.

There are two deliberately distinct identities:

| Identity | Purpose |
|---|---|
| B | Immutable source-provenance basis |
| I | The active work-level obligation to which B contributes |

An established mapping `B → I` is immutable. Repeated observations of B reuse that mapping, including after I becomes historical. They never reopen B as a new obligation.

**ICard-W:** at most one operationally unresolved MI intent for exact W at a time.

Distinct successive intents for the same still-active W may exist historically, but only after authoritative closure of the preceding active intent and admission of a previously unrepresented qualifying basis. Their identities are distinguished by their exact MI establishment acts; no new global request-ID scheme is required.

Thus one historical intent does not absorb all future requests forever.

## H. CROSS-ASSOCIATION COMPOSITION

**MI-XH is selected.**

Per-A/per-membership provenance obligations contribute to one active W-level cancellation intent. Here, a contributor’s obligation is to remain represented in that intent’s disposition; it is **not an additional independent workload-effect obligation**.

The rule is:

| Situation | MI result |
|---|---|
| First qualifying basis for active W; no incumbent intent | Establish I and its first contributor |
| Another qualifying basis for the same W while I is active | Add that basis to I; no second workload obligation |
| Same basis observed again | Reuse its existing mapping |
| Different W | Cannot join I |
| W equality unproved | No cross-A aggregation |
| Authoritative contradiction | Close disputed reliance; no convenient merge |
| Prior I authoritatively closed; genuinely new qualifying basis | May establish a distinct successor I |
| Previously mapped basis presented after closure | Historical reuse only; no reactivation |

**Authority for composition:** accepted WP supplies exact W equality; accepted source governance limits this cancellation semantic to same-enclosing-work requests without independent per-request effects. This MI correction prospectively selects work-level obligation composition. WP and OA alone did not already grant it.

The [receipt governance](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/governance/rq003-stage3c-sole-reaper-cancellation-receipt-settlement-clarification-candidate.md:218) does not permit silently coalescing requests requiring independent per-request effects. Such a request cannot be relabeled as the supported MI cancellation kind merely because its A references W.

Composition does **not**:

- Merge Ledgers, Episodes or source ownership.
- Change receipt classification.
- Satisfy either Association’s local action.
- Infer effect idempotence.
- Require one acknowledgement per Association.
- Infer W equality from equal selectors or equal O.

Every contributing A, E, M, accepted OA basis and inherited context remains attributable. Aggregation removes duplicate **workload obligation cardinality**, not request history.

A contributor addition is ordered against any later external disposition of I. A disposition covering an earlier contributor set cannot silently close a later committed contributor. This is an exact MI handoff requirement; AE’s disposition mechanism is not selected here.

## I. ACTIVATION PREDICATE / TIMING

**MI-TIME-B is selected.**

For a **new basis admission**, the logical MI commit must establish all of the following:

1. Accepted RA-A-CFW provenance establishes exact immutable W/L/profile/scope.
2. Accepted WP-C establishes exact A→W/L/root provenance.
3. Exact OA admission and an actual, established **OBS-ACTIVE** observation exist.
4. That observation binds exact A/W/E/M and its original snapshot/context.
5. The same semantic membership basis remains **MEM-CURRENT** in the same authoritative Episode at MI commit.
6. W remains within its independently governed active lifetime; absence of terminal evidence alone is insufficient.
7. The same OA admission remains eligible for operational handoff. Known O/L loss, ended eligibility or unresolved eligibility cannot be bypassed using the earlier observation.
8. Relevant original and commit-time FAILED/claim/action/accounting context is preserved or authoritatively referenceable.
9. No unresolved upstream authority contradiction or relevant prior MI commitment uncertainty permits reliance.
10. The immutable basis mapping and one-active-intent-per-W rule have one coherent disposition.

Local action uncertainty may be retained as an explicit value. It is not automatically an upstream identity/currentness failure.

Non-normative transition:

```text
ESTABLISH_WORKLOAD_INTENT(A, W, E, M, observation, context)
```

| Disposition | Meaning |
|---|---|
| New establishment | Commit I, first contributor and B→I together |
| Existing active I, new B | Commit B→I and contributor addition together |
| Existing B→I | Observe/reuse; no second admission or establishment |
| Definite noncommit | No new MI fact; upstream facts remain |
| Conflict | Reject unsupported contender or suspend genuinely disputed reliance |
| Uncertain commitment | Preserve original uncertain disposition; no second intent |

Deduplication is a branch of the transition, not a requirement that every valid observation find no incumbent.

**Stale schedule:**

```text
valid OA observation at T1
→ membership settles
→ proposed MI commit at T2
→ no new intent or contributor from that stale basis
```

The observation remains true history. An intent committed before settlement remains governed by its own lifetime.

An updated subsumption snapshot may still represent the same M. MI preserves what O actually observed and separately validates current basis continuity; it must not claim O saw later details.

**Availability tradeoff:** lawful settlement can outrun MI. OA already permits membership to settle without observation. MI adds no settlement hold and no durable entitlement arising from observation alone.

MI-TIME-A is not selected because it would give an uncommitted observation a surviving operational entitlement beyond currentness.

## L. SETTLEMENT

**MI-SETTLE-N is selected.**

An intent committed before settlement survives as an unresolved workload-side obligation after its contributing Episode becomes historical.

Cancellation-side settlement:

- Does not require live O/L.
- Does not discharge I.
- Does not establish AE success.
- Does not permit new contributor admission from settled membership.

This separation is an explicit **MI prospective architecture correction**, not an inference from an old Episode object remaining reachable.

Its intended-exception delivery remains the adopted cancellation-side action delivery. AE-U explicitly distinguishes that from workload effect.

Consequently, “Episode settled” must never be represented as “workload cancellation resolved.” Unresolved MI remains visible in its own authority/evidence domain.

MI evidence must survive independently of the source Episode’s physical retention. No source ownership transfer, source-release permission or new source-finalization prerequisite follows.

## M. SUCCESSOR EPISODES

**MI-EP-SUBSUME is selected.**

A lawful successor Episode has a distinct membership basis. Its first qualified receipt remains fresh under cancellation-side governance.

If a W-level I remains active, a qualifying successor observation contributes that new basis to I. It does not create a second workload obligation.

This does not subsume the successor’s local action into the predecessor’s local action. Each Episode retains its existing receipt/action/settlement rules.

After I has an authoritative external protocol disposition:

- Its contributor mappings remain immutable.
- Reobserving an old contributor cannot reopen it.
- A previously unrepresented qualifying basis may establish a new I for still-active W.
- Settlement alone cannot close I or create that opportunity.

No fresh Episode is silently discarded as “cancelled sometime before.”

## N. W TERMINALITY / OBSERVER LOSS

**MITERM-DISPOSITION is selected.**

Independently established W terminality changes an unresolved active I to:

```text
historical, non-actionable, unresolved at W terminality
```

This preserves the fact that cancellation intent existed without fabricating its successful resolution.

After that boundary:

- No new MI intent or contributor is admitted for W.
- No new effect may begin solely from MI.
- Historical attribution remains available.
- No result, source, receipt or reaper obligation is erased.
- An independently begun AE operation remains subject to AE’s own contract; MI neither completes nor replays it.

W terminality is consumed from accepted profile authority. Invocation FAILED, child exit, source closure, Episode settlement or result existence alone cannot substitute for it.

**Observer loss after commitment:** established I and its contributors survive. AE does not need live O merely to authenticate I.

**Observer loss before commitment:** no new basis admission from the stale operational handoff. The earlier observation remains history. This preserves OA-C’s closing-context restriction and introduces no replacement.

Loss or uncertainty about W/L does not fabricate W terminality. Where operational lifetime cannot be proved, new operational reliance closes while established history remains.

## O. MI STATE MACHINE

These states distinguish semantic history from consumer knowledge. An uncertainty overlay does not undo a fact that actually committed.

| State | Meaning | Positive operational AE premise |
|---|---|---|
| **MI0** | No intent established; applicable noncommitment known | No |
| **MI1** | I established, exact contributors retained, operationally unresolved | Yes, subject to current W/context validity |
| **MI2** | Relevant establishment, contribution or disposition uncertain | No from the uncertain scope |
| **MI3** | Established I historical/non-actionable, with exact closing reason retained | No |
| **MI4** | Genuine authoritative contradiction affecting the relied-on relation | No from the disputed scope |

MI3 distinguishes:

- **W-terminal historical-unresolved**.
- **Externally disposed**, supported by a separately authorized AE disposition for exact I and its covered contributor set.

The second records external disposition attribution; it does not independently claim delivery or application.

Principal transitions:

| Transition | Required basis |
|---|---|
| MI0 → MI1 | Successful qualifying establishment |
| MI1 → MI1 | New qualifying contributor joins same I |
| MI1 → MI1 | Duplicate basis observed; no new commitment |
| MI0/MI1 → MI2 | Relevant original transition disposition becomes uncertain |
| MI2 → established prior state | Authorized evidence proves original commitment/noncommitment |
| MI1 → MI3 | Independently established W terminality |
| MI1 → MI3 | Separately authorized exact external disposition covers the current contributor set |
| Any disputed relation → MI4 | Genuine contradictory authoritative evidence |

A stale rejected observation does **not** create MI3: there may never have been an intent. It leaves no new intent, while preserving the rejected attempt’s history.

No transition out of historical state reactivates the same I. A later distinct intent requires a new qualifying basis and the absence of an active or uncertain predecessor.

A no-intent fact at an earlier time is not automatically contradictory to a later valid establishment. Conflict requires incompatible claims about the same relevant identity/disposition/order.

**MI2 rules:**

- No positive premise from uncertain establishment or contribution.
- No second intent by convenience.
- No automatic retry.
- Observe the original disposition through independently authorized evidence.
- Proven commitment reuses the original identity.
- Proven noncommitment permits only a fresh attempt satisfying all then-current predicates.

Uncertain contributor admission or uncertain closure prevents using an older aggregate snapshot to bypass the ambiguity or create a competing I. It does not retroactively negate independently established history.

An AE operation already begun under its own valid contract is not undone by MI’s knowledge state. Its handling remains downstream.

## C. REVIEW SCOPE / ORIGINAL MI-U CLOSURE

**MIU-CLOSED — the original membership→workload-intent gap is fully closed.**

Original MI-U distinguished qualified membership from legitimate workload observation and from an obligation to enter a workload-effect protocol. Accepted RA/WP/OA supply the missing antecedents. MI-C §§E–I prospectively supply the remaining derivation, identity and composition rules.

The completed edge is:

```text
accepted qualifying OA observation
+ exact MI commitment predicates
+ deterministic identity/composition rule
→ authoritative intent for exact W
→ bounded positive premise for separately governed AE
```

This does not complete AE, AR, CD, CW, source coverage, result binding or implementation.

## D. INTENT / CONTRIBUTOR IDENTITY ORACLE

| Object | Exact meaning |
|---|---|
| B | Exact Association A, exact Episode E and the Ledger-governed retained semantic membership obligation M |
| I | Exact MI establishment act for W, carrying one operationally unresolved work-level cancellation obligation |
| B→I | Immutable mapping from a committed contributor basis to its intent |
| Contributor set | Every committed distinct B, with provenance, contextual evidence and commitment ordering |
| Historical mapping | The original B→I remains attributable after settlement, disposition or successor intent |

M is established by the first qualified receipt and includes its eligible subsumed/participating membership. It is not a physical-signal count, observation ID or newly invented receipt identity.

The identities are non-circular: Ledger supplies B’s membership component; accepted WP supplies W equality; MI supplies I’s establishment identity and composition. Repeated reads neither create M nor establish a second I.

OA observation previously proved an observed fact, not a workload obligation. MI-C’s explicit prospective rule adds the obligation to account for and resolve the cancellation request through AE.

There is no subsequent policy-activation decision:

- The MI transition applies the authored predicates and composition rule.

Retained state serves identity, contributors, deduplication, uncertainty and history. It does not convert MI-C1 into MI-C2.

## G. MEMBERSHIP / INTENT IDENTITY AND CARDINALITY REVIEW

**IB-ME, MCard-ONE and ICard-W are satisfied.**

The [receipt contract](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/governance/rq003-stage3c-sole-reaper-cancellation-receipt-settlement-clarification-candidate.md:118), accepted owner integration and [Ledger implementation](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/src/orev3/execution/cancellation_capability.py:822) distinguish first qualified receipt, eligible subsumption and continuation of participating retention. Selected/subsumed refinements do not replace M. Participating dequeue cannot become a fresh basis. Distinct Episodes remain distinct even when their ordinals or input descriptions resemble one another.

ICard-W permits successive historical intents, not simultaneous duplicate active obligations. A successor requires authoritative predecessor closure, still-active W and a previously unmapped qualifying B. Old B remains attached to its original I forever for attribution purposes.

This does not absorb future requests into one lifetime intent.

## H. CROSS-ASSOCIATION / CONTRIBUTOR COMPOSITION REVIEW

**XA-SAFE.**

Exact W equality alone would not justify aggregation. The additional grounds are:

1. The supported cancellation kind is already restricted to same-enclosing-work requests without independent per-request effects.
2. WP-C permits multiple Associations for one W without granting extra delivery authority.
3. MI-C §H explicitly selects one active workload obligation prospectively.
4. Each contributor must remain represented in the intent’s disposition.

The [governance eligibility restriction](/Users/erale/Documents/orev3/docs/research/governance/rq003-stage3c-sole-reaper-cancellation-receipt-settlement-clarification-candidate.md:218) does not itself prescribe cross-A MI composition. It bounds eligible requests; MI supplies the new composition rule.

| Cross-A schedule | Result |
|---|---|
| XA1: only A1 has qualifying membership | Only A1 contributes |
| XA2: both current, same proven W | Both distinct contributors; one active I |
| XA3: different W | Separate intents; no aggregation |
| XA4: equal selectors, different/unproved W | No aggregation |
| XA5: different FAILED/action contexts | Preserve each contributor’s context |
| XA6: B2 addition disputed while B1 established | Preserve B1 history; block operational aggregate reliance through the uncertain/disputed coverage |

The rule does not infer carrier idempotence, merge local Ledgers, suppress local successor action, or select acknowledgement cardinality.

## I. CONTRIBUTOR / DISPOSITION RACE REVIEW

MI-C §§H–I, O–Q and its qualification oracles provide sufficient semantic atomicity and ordering.

| Race | Required authored outcome |
|---|---|
| A: two first contributors | One I; each successful contributor retained exactly once |
| B: establishment versus join | Establishment precedes the join logically; no attachment to nonexistent I |
| D: two joins | Both successful additions retained; neither overwrites the other |
| E: two observations of B | One immutable B→I; applicable additional context may be retained |
| F: B after settlement | Historical mapping only; no new admission |
| G: B after I closure | No reopening |
| H: new B after closure | Distinct successor I only when closure and current predicates are established |

The contributor collection is **set-like in membership and ordered for commitment/disposition coverage**. No prescribed lock or global sequence number is necessary.

For race C:

- **Disposition before B2 commitment:** closed I cannot receive a new contributor; a qualifying unmapped B2 may establish a successor.
- **B2 commitment before disposition:** closure must cover the current set including B2. Coverage of `{B1}` cannot close B2.
- **Disposition uncertain:** no presumed closure, continuing actionability or successor intent.

These requirements are authored constraints, not a reviewer-supplied AE repair.

## S. MI→AE EXPORT / STALE-EXPORT REVIEW

The exact authored export is:

> Exact authoritative workload-cancellation intent I exists for exact W, derived from exact accepted OA observation(s) and exact cancellation-membership provenance, with exact intent identity and scope, the exact committed contributor set, preserved Episode/FAILED/local-action context, and an established intent disposition.
